---
<!-- head-1: body_md -->
For \(k\ge2\), let \([k]:=\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(e_1,\ldots,e_k\) be the standard basis of
\(\mathbb R^k\). 
For positive integers \(b,N\), we write \(b\mid N\) if \(N\) is divisible by \(b\).
For matrices, \(\langle A,B\rangle:=\operatorname{tr}(A^\top B)\),
\(\|A\|_{\max}:=\max_{r,j}|A_{r,j}|\), and
\(\|A\|_{\mathrm{sum}}:=\sum_{r,j}|A_{r,j}|\); we use
\(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm F}\) for the spectral and Frobenius norms.
For \(W\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) with rows \(w_r^\top\), define
\(\|W\|_{\mathrm{row}}:=\|W\|_{2,\infty}:=\max_{r \in [k]}\|w_r\|_2\) as a row norm.
For \(a\in\mathbb R^k\) and \(c\in[k]\), define \(\mathbb{S}_c(a):=e^{a_c}/\sum_{\ell=1}^k e^{a_\ell}\), the \(c\)-th component of the softmax map.
We write \(A^{\odot p}\) for entrywise powers and \(\oslash\) for entrywise division, with \(0/0:=0\).
For nonzero vectors \(u,v\), let \(\angle(u,v)\in[0,\pi]\) denote the angle between \(u\) and \(v\).
Write \(\widehat v:=v/\|v\|_2\) for \(v\neq{\mathbf 0}\).
For random quantities indexed by \(d\), \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) denotes a term that converges to zero in probability as \(d\to\infty\).
<!-- end head-1 -->
<!-- assumption-1: body_md -->
\label{ass:gaussian-cloud}
The training dataset consists of \((x_{i,s},i)\) for \(i\in[k]\) and \(s\in[n_i]\) such that
\begin{equation}
x_{i,s}:=\mu_i+r z_{i,s},
    \qquad\text{where}\qquad \mu_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d),\qquad z_{i,s}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d).
\label{eq:gaussian-cloud}
\end{equation}
A test example \(X^{\mathrm{te}}\) with label \(Y\) is
\begin{equation}
X^{\mathrm{te}}:=\mu_Y+r_{\mathrm{te}}z^{\mathrm{te}},\qquad \mathbb P(Y=i)=\pi_{i,d},\qquad z^{\mathrm{te}}\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d),
\label{eq:population-test-model-clean}
\end{equation}
where \((\mu_i)_{i=1}^k\), \((z_{i,s})_{i,s}\), \(Y\), and \(z^{\mathrm{te}}\) are mutually independent. 
Here, \(r=r(d)\ge0\), \(r_{\mathrm{te}}=r_{\mathrm{te}}(d)>0\), \(\pi_{i,d}>0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^k\pi_{i,d}=1\).
<!-- end assumption-1 -->
<!-- assumption-2: body_md -->
\label{ass:asymptotic-regime}
Along a sequence of models indexed by \(d\), with \(k=k(d)\), \(n_i=n_i(d)\), and \(\pi_{\min,d}:=\min_i\pi_{i,d}\),
\begin{equation}
k/d\to\alpha\in(0,\infty),\qquad n_{\min}\to\infty,\qquad \log N=o(d),\qquad \log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d).
\label{eq:asymptotic-regime-clean}
\end{equation}
Furthermore, \(r_0:=\sup_d r(d)<\infty\) and \(r_{\mathrm{te},0}:=\sup_d r_{\mathrm{te}}(d)<\infty\).
<!-- end assumption-2 -->
<!-- assumption-3: body_md -->
\label{ass:bounded-minibatches}
Under random-reshuffling training with batch size \(b=b_d\), the number of mini-batches per epoch, \(m_d:=N(d)/b_d\), satisfies \(m_0:=\sup_d m_d<\infty\).
<!-- end assumption-3 -->
<!-- assumption-4: body_md -->
\label{ass:adam-init}
For full-batch Adam, every entry of \(\nabla L(W_0)\) is nonzero.
<!-- end assumption-4 -->
<!-- assumption-5: body_md -->
\label{ass:lr-base}
The sequence \(\{\eta_t\}_{t\ge0}\) is positive and nonincreasing, with \(\eta_t\to0\) and \(\sum_{t=0}^\infty \eta_t=\infty\).
<!-- end assumption-5 -->
<!-- assumption-6: body_md -->
\label{ass:lr-momentum}
For every \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(c_1>0\), there exist \(t_0\in\mathbb N\) and \(c_2>0\) such that \(\sum_{s=0}^{t}\beta^s\bigl(\exp(c_1\sum_{\tau=1}^{s}\eta_{t-\tau})-1\bigr)\le c_2\eta_t\) for all \(t\ge t_0\).
<!-- end assumption-6 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}
Define the full-batch optimizer groups
\begin{equation}
\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}}:=\{\mathrm{RowGD},\mathrm{RowGDM}\},\quad
\mathcal O_{\mathrm{comp}}:=\{\mathrm{SpecGD},\mathrm{Muon},\mathrm{SignGD},\mathrm{Signum},\mathrm{Adam}\}.
\label{eq:det-optimizer-groups}
\end{equation}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud}, \ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. Then, for every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-\sqrt d}\) over the training data, the following holds for all momentum parameters \(\beta \in (0,1)\) of RowGDM, Muon, and Signum:
\begin{equation}
\min_{\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}}}\liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right)
>
\max_{\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{comp}}}\limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right).
\label{eq:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
The proof proceeds through the implicit biases of the optimizers. RowGD and RowGDM approach row-norm margin solutions, SpecGD and Muon approach spectral-norm margin solutions, and SignGD, Signum, and Adam approach max-norm margin solutions. Here, a \(\psi\)-norm margin solution minimizes \(\psi(W)\) among classifiers with training margin at least one; the formal solution sets are defined in Appendix~\ref{app:deterministic-margin}. Under the Gaussian-cloud model, these three solution sets have the distinct asymptotic classifier structures summarized in Proposition~\ref{prop:limiting-geometry}, and Gaussian pairwise-error bounds convert this geometric separation into the population-accuracy ordering.
Because Theorem~\ref{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean} is proven through a uniform comparison over all norm-induced margin solutions approached by the optimizers, it does not require directional convergence of optimizers.

























































\begin{proposition}[Limiting classifier geometry]
\label{prop:limiting-geometry}
Let \(W_t^{\rm opt}\) have rows \((w_{i,t}^{\rm opt})^\top\), and let \(\Theta_t^{\rm opt}:=k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^k\angle(w_{i,t}^{\rm opt},\mu_i)\) denote the average angle between the class mean and classifier row. 
Let \(M_\mu\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) have rows \(\mu_i^\top\), let \(P:=I_k-k^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\) and \(r_d:=\min\{k-1,d\}\), and let \(C_\mu:=PM_\mu\) have compact SVD \(U_\mu\Sigma_\mu V_\mu^\top\) and polar factor \(Q_\mu:=U_\mu V_\mu^\top\). Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud}, \ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{\rm RowGD/RowGDM:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\max_i\bigl\|\widehat w_{i,t}^{\rm opt}-\widehat\mu_i\bigr\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
\text{\rm SignGD/Signum/Adam:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\max_i\left\|\widehat w_{i,t}^{\rm opt}-\frac{\operatorname{sign}(\mu_i)}{\sqrt d}\right\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
\text{\rm SpecGD/Muon:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac1{r_d}\left\|\frac{PW_t^{\rm opt}}{\|PW_t^{\rm opt}\|_{\rm op}}-Q_\mu\right\|_{\rm F}^2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}|\Theta_t^{\rm opt}-\theta|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), where \(\theta=0\) for RowGD/RowGDM and \(\theta=\arccos\sqrt{2/\pi}\) for SignGD/Signum/Adam. 
If the aspect ratio \(\alpha>1\), then \(\theta=\arccos\kappa_{\rm sp}(\alpha)\) for SpecGD/Muon, where \(\kappa_{\rm sp}:(0,\infty)\to(0,1)\) is a positive constant depending only on \(\alpha\).\footnote{Its explicit formula is given in \eqref{eq:app-det-all-aspect-scales}. Numerically, \(\kappa_{\rm sp}(1)\approx0.84883\) and \(\kappa_{\rm sp}(2)\approx0.93280\).}
\end{proposition}
<!-- end head-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:limiting-geometry}
Let \(W_t^{\rm opt}\) have rows \((w_{i,t}^{\rm opt})^\top\), and let \(\Theta_t^{\rm opt}:=k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^k\angle(w_{i,t}^{\rm opt},\mu_i)\) denote the average angle between the class mean and classifier row. 
Let \(M_\mu\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) have rows \(\mu_i^\top\), let \(P:=I_k-k^{-1}\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top\) and \(r_d:=\min\{k-1,d\}\), and let \(C_\mu:=PM_\mu\) have compact SVD \(U_\mu\Sigma_\mu V_\mu^\top\) and polar factor \(Q_\mu:=U_\mu V_\mu^\top\). Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud}, \ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{\rm RowGD/RowGDM:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\max_i\bigl\|\widehat w_{i,t}^{\rm opt}-\widehat\mu_i\bigr\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
\text{\rm SignGD/Signum/Adam:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\max_i\left\|\widehat w_{i,t}^{\rm opt}-\frac{\operatorname{sign}(\mu_i)}{\sqrt d}\right\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\\
\text{\rm SpecGD/Muon:}\quad&
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac1{r_d}\left\|\frac{PW_t^{\rm opt}}{\|PW_t^{\rm opt}\|_{\rm op}}-Q_\mu\right\|_{\rm F}^2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}|\Theta_t^{\rm opt}-\theta|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), where \(\theta=0\) for RowGD/RowGDM and \(\theta=\arccos\sqrt{2/\pi}\) for SignGD/Signum/Adam. 
If the aspect ratio \(\alpha>1\), then \(\theta=\arccos\kappa_{\rm sp}(\alpha)\) for SpecGD/Muon, where \(\kappa_{\rm sp}:(0,\infty)\to(0,1)\) is a positive constant depending only on \(\alpha\).\footnote{Its explicit formula is given in \eqref{eq:app-det-all-aspect-scales}. Numerically, \(\kappa_{\rm sp}(1)\approx0.84883\) and \(\kappa_{\rm sp}(2)\approx0.93280\).}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:det-optimizer-error-exponents}
Let \(\mathcal E_{t,d}^{\mathrm{opt}} := 1-\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}})\). 
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud}, \ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. 
Then
\begin{align*}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\left|\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log \! \frac{\mathcal E_{t,d}^{\mathrm{Adam}}}{\mathcal E_{t,d}^{\mathrm{RowGDM}}}-\frac{\pi-2}{4\pi}\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(1), \ \ \
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log \! \frac{\mathcal E_{t,d}^{\mathrm{Muon}}}{\mathcal E_{t,d}^{\mathrm{RowGDM}}}\ge\frac{1-\kappa_{\rm sp}(\alpha)^2}{4} \! - \!o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\end{align*}
where \(\kappa_{\rm sp}\) is the constant as in Proposition~\ref{prop:limiting-geometry}. 
The same conclusion holds with RowGDM replaced by RowGD, Adam by SignGD or Signum, and Muon by SpecGD.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:stoch-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud}, \ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, \ref{ass:bounded-minibatches}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. Then there exists \(\beta_0=\beta_0(\alpha,r_0,m_0)\in[0,1)\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-\sqrt d}\) over the training data, the following holds for all momentum parameters \(\beta \in [\beta_0,1)\) of RR-RowSGDM, RR-Muon, and RR-Signum, and for every realization of the reshuffling:
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}}\right)
>
\max_{\mathrm{opt}\in\{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Muon},\,\mathrm{RR\text{-}Signum}\}}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right).
\label{eq:stoch-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:rr-adamproxy-epoch-high-memory}
For each epoch \(r=0,1,2,\ldots\), let \(\tau_r:=mr\) denote the index of its first update and \(\gamma_r:=\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}\eta_{\tau_r+s}\) its total learning rate. Fix a training set with \(x_n[a]\neq0\) for all \(n\in[N]\) and \(a\in[d]\). 
Suppose that \(b<N\) and that Assumptions~\ref{ass:lr-base} and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. Then, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), RR-Adam in \eqref{eq:adam-update-clean} satisfies
\begin{equation}
\lim_{\substack{(\beta_1,\beta_2)\to(1,1)\\
0<\beta_1\le\beta_2<1}}
\limsup_{r\to\infty}
\mathbb P\left(
\left\|
\frac{W_{\tau_{r+1}}^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Adam}}-W_{\tau_r}^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Adam}}}{\gamma_r}
+\Phi_{N,b}\!\left(W_{\tau_r}^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Adam}}\right)
\right\|_{\max}>\varepsilon
\right)=0,
\label{eq:rr-adamproxy-one-epoch-limit-clean}
\end{equation}
where the probability is over the random reshuffling.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:adamproxy-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}
Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud}, \ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, \ref{ass:bounded-minibatches}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold. Then there exists \(\beta_1=\beta_1(\alpha,r_0,m_0)\in[0,1)\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-\sqrt d}\) over the training data, the following holds for all momentum parameters \(\beta\in[\beta_1,1)\) of RR-RowSGDM and for every realization of the reshuffling:
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}}\right)
>
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{AP}}\right).
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- assumption-7: body_md -->
\label{ass:aniso-clean}
Let \(\Gamma,\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_k\) be positive-definite covariance matrices with \(\operatorname{tr}\Gamma=\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_i=d\) for every \(i\in[k]\).\footnote{A fixed trace preserves total variance while allowing covariance spectra and orientations to vary.} Training uses the clean class signals \(\{(\mu_i,i)\}_{i=1}^k\). A test example with label \(Y\) is \(X^{\mathrm{te}}:=\mu_Y+r_{\mathrm{te}}z^{\mathrm{te}}\), where, conditionally on the covariance matrices, \((Y,z^{\mathrm{te}})\) is independent of \((\mu_i)_{i=1}^k\) and
\begin{equation}
\mu_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},\Gamma),\qquad
\mathbb P(Y=i)=\pi_{i,d}>0,\qquad
z^{\mathrm{te}}\mid Y\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},\Sigma_Y).
\label{eq:aniso-training-model}
\end{equation}
Along the sequence indexed by \(d\), \(k/d\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)\) and \(r_{\mathrm{te}}>0\) satisfies \(r_{\mathrm{te},0}:=\sup_d r_{\mathrm{te}}(d)<\infty\).
<!-- end assumption-7 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:aniso-dd-ordering}
Let \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}}\) and \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{comp}}\) be as in \eqref{eq:det-optimizer-groups}, with fixed \(\beta\in(0,1)\) for RowGDM, Muon, and Signum. Suppose Assumptions~\ref{ass:aniso-clean}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold, with the covariances in \eqref{eq:aniso-covariances} for \(0\le s_\mu<1\) and \(s_\Sigma\ge0\). Assume that \(\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d/\log d)\) and that \(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}/\|W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_{\mathrm F}\) converges almost surely as \(t\to\infty\) for every \(\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}}\cup\mathcal O_{\mathrm{comp}}\). Then there exist constants \(c,C>0\), independent of \(d\), such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-Cd^{-c}\) over \(U_\mu\), \(O_1,\ldots,O_k\), and the class means,
\begin{equation}
\min_{\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}}}\liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right)
>
\max_{\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{comp}}}\limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right).
\label{eq:aniso-det-optimizer-ordering-clean-data}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Unlike the accuracy comparisons in Section~\ref{sec:main-results}, which hold uniformly over all classifier families that the normalized iterates approach and therefore do not require directional convergence, Theorem~\ref{thm:aniso-dd-ordering} assumes directional convergence for each optimizer.
Related directional-convergence assumptions are common in the implicit-bias literature \citep{gunasekar2018implicit, nacson2019convergence, chizat2020implicit, baek2026implicit}.
Under clean training, conditional on the training data, the limit of \(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}/\|W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_{\mathrm F}\) is fixed and independent of the test-noise eigenbases, which enter only at test time. 
Hence, the concentration bounds over the Haar-random test-noise eigenbases apply to the fixed limiting direction.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
We find that the fitted class-mean spectral exponents can be smaller than one (\(s_\mu<1\)) in language-model representations; see Appendix~\ref{app:language-model-represen}. This provides a possible connection between the anisotropic regime covered by Theorem~\ref{thm:aniso-dd-ordering} and representation geometry in language models.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:main-coordinate-reversal}
Let \(\lambda\in[0,1]\). 
Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{ass:aniso-clean}, \ref{ass:adam-init}, \ref{ass:lr-base}, and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} hold with \(\Gamma=\Gamma_d\) and \(\Sigma_1=\cdots=\Sigma_k=\Sigma_{\lambda,d}\) as in \eqref{eq:coordinate-aligned-covariances}.
Suppose also that \(\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d)\), \(0<\inf_{a,d}\gamma_{a,d}\le\sup_{a,d}\gamma_{a,d}<\infty\), and the limits \(\bar\gamma_q:=\lim_{d\to\infty}d^{-1}\sum_{a=1}^d\gamma_{a,d}^q\) exist \(\forall q\in\{1/2,2\}\) and satisfy \(2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2\bar\gamma_2>\pi\).\footnote{This requires a sufficiently dispersed spectrum. Corollary~\ref{cor:app-coordinate-dispersed-profiles} gives a sufficient condition.}
Then \(\lambda_c:=(\pi/(2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2)-1)/(\bar\gamma_2-1)\) lies in \((0,1)\), and the following hold.\footnote{The same conclusions hold with RowGDM replaced by RowGD.}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em,nosep]
    \item \emph{Diagonal covariance.} For every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\setminus\{\lambda_c\}\), there exist \(c_\lambda,C_\lambda>0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda d}\) over the class means, for all \(\beta \in (0,1)\),
    \[
        \begin{aligned}
        \liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}}\right)
        &>
        \limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}}\right)
        &&\text{if }\lambda<\lambda_c,\\
        \liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}}\right)
        &>
        \limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}}\right)
        &&\text{if }\lambda>\lambda_c.
        \end{aligned}
    \]
    \item \emph{Recovery under Haar rotation.} Let \(Q\) be Haar-uniformly random on \(\mathsf{SO}(d)\) and independent of the class means, and replace every training and test input \(x\) by \(Qx\). There exist \(c_{\mathrm{rot}},C_{\mathrm{rot}}>0\) such that, for every fixed \(\lambda\in[0,1]\) and every sufficiently large \(d\), with probability at least \(1-C_{\mathrm{rot}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{rot}}d}\) over the class means and \(Q\), the RowGDM-over-Adam ordering holds.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:effective-margin-direction-convergence}
Suppose \(W_t\ne{\mathbf 0}\) eventually and, for some \(0\le\varepsilon<\gamma_\psi(X)\),
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\ge\gamma_\psi(X)-\varepsilon.
\label{eq:app-effective-margin-convergence}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
d_{\cos}(W_t,\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X)\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:app-effective-direction-convergence}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
By scale invariance of \(d_{\cos}\), consider \(W_t/\psi(W_t)\), which lies on the compact \(\psi\)-unit sphere. If the conclusion failed, a subsequence whose cosine discrepancy from \(\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X\) is bounded below by a positive constant would have a further subsequence converging to some \(U_\infty\). Continuity of the margin and~\eqref{eq:app-effective-margin-convergence} give \(\operatorname{mar}_X(U_\infty)\ge\gamma_\psi(X)-\varepsilon\), so \(U_\infty\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X\), contradicting continuity of the cosine discrepancy.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:exact-margin-direction-convergence}
If
\begin{equation}
\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\longrightarrow\gamma_\psi(X),
\label{eq:app-exact-margin-convergence}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
d_{\cos}(W_t,\mathcal U_\psi^X)\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:app-exact-direction-convergence}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:effective-margin-direction-convergence} with \(\varepsilon=0\).
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-general-lr-remainders}
Suppose Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-base} holds. Then \(S_t\to\infty\), and for every \(q>1\), \(c>0\), and fixed \(t_0\in\mathbb N\),
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\eta_s^q}{S_t}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \sum_{s=t_0}^{t-1}\eta_s\exp\!\left(-c\sum_{\tau=t_0}^{s-1}\eta_\tau\right)=O(1).
\label{eq:app-general-lr-remainders}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Fix \(\varepsilon>0\) and choose \(T\) so that \(\eta_s^{q-1}\le\varepsilon\) for all \(s\ge T\). Then
\[
\frac{\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}\eta_s^q}{S_t}\le\frac{\sum_{s=0}^{T-1}\eta_s^q}{S_t}+\varepsilon,
\]
which proves the first limit. For the second assertion, enlarge \(T\ge t_0\) so that \(c\eta_s\le1\) for \(s\ge T\), and set \(A_s:=\sum_{\tau=t_0}^{s-1}\eta_\tau\). Since \(1-e^{-x}\ge x/2\) for \(x\in[0,1]\),
\[
e^{-cA_s}-e^{-cA_{s+1}}\ge\frac c2\eta_s e^{-cA_s}.
\]
The tail therefore telescopes to a bounded quantity, while the finite prefix is harmless.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-general-lr-normalization}
Let \(\mathfrak m:\mathbb R^{k\times d}\to\mathbb R\) be continuous and positively homogeneous, let \(\Gamma_*:=\max_{\psi(W)\le1}\mathfrak m(W)>0\), and suppose \(0<\Gamma\le\Gamma_*\). Assume \(S_t\to\infty\). If
\[
\mathfrak m(W_t)\ge\Gamma S_t-r_t,\qquad \psi(W_t)\le C_0+S_t,\qquad r_t=o(S_t),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\mathfrak m(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\ge\Gamma.
\label{eq:app-general-lr-normalization}
\end{equation}
If \(\Gamma=\Gamma_*\), then \(\mathfrak m(W_t)/\psi(W_t)\to\Gamma_*\), and every accumulation point of \(W_t/\psi(W_t)\) maximizes \(\mathfrak m\) over the \(\psi\)-unit ball.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Since \(r_t=o(S_t)\) and \(S_t\to\infty\), the lower bound \(\Gamma S_t-r_t\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(t\). In particular, \(W_t\ne0\) eventually. For such \(t\),
\[
\frac{\mathfrak m(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\ge\frac{\Gamma S_t-r_t}{C_0+S_t}\longrightarrow\Gamma.
\]
This proves the liminf statement without imposing a sign condition on \(r_t\). When \(\Gamma=\Gamma_*\), positive homogeneity gives \(\mathfrak m(W_t)/\psi(W_t)\le\Gamma_*\), proving convergence. Compactness of the \(\psi\)-unit sphere and continuity of \(\mathfrak m\) give the accumulation-point statement.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-ms-basic}
Let \(\psi\) satisfy~\eqref{eq:app-ms-sandwich}, and let \(\psi^*\) be its dual norm. Then, for every matrix \(G\), every \(h\) with \(\|h\|_1\le R_1(X)\), and every \(A\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\),
\begin{equation}
\psi^*(G)\le\|G\|_{\mathrm{sum}},\qquad \|Ah\|_\infty\le R_1(X)\psi(A).
\label{eq:app-ms-basic-bounds}
\end{equation}
Moreover, if \(s\in\mathbb R^k\) is a probability vector and \(H(s):=\operatorname{diag}(s)-ss^\top\), then for every \(c\in[k]\),
\begin{equation}
h^\top A^\top H(s)Ah\le4R_1(X)^2(1-s_c)\psi(A)^2.
\label{eq:app-ms-hessian}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since the \(\psi\)-unit ball is contained in the entrywise max-norm unit ball,
\[
\psi^*(G)=\max_{\psi(A)\le1}\langle G,A\rangle\le\max_{\|A\|_{\max}\le1}\langle G,A\rangle=\|G\|_{\mathrm{sum}}.
\]
Also, \(\|Ah\|_\infty\le\|A\|_{\max}\|h\|_1\le R_1(X)\psi(A)\). For \(v=Ah\), the softmax covariance bound gives \(v^\top H(s)v\le4(1-s_c)\|v\|_\infty^2\), which proves~\eqref{eq:app-ms-hessian}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:app-ms-full-batch}
Let \(\psi\) be max--sum dominated. Under Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-base}, normalized steepest descent
\begin{equation}
\Delta_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\psi(\Delta)\le1}\langle\nabla L(W_t),\Delta\rangle,\qquad W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta_t\Delta_t
\label{eq:app-ms-nsd}
\end{equation}
satisfies
\begin{equation}
\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\longrightarrow\gamma_\psi(X).
\label{eq:app-ms-nsd-margin}
\end{equation}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:lr-base} and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}, the same conclusion holds for every fixed \(\beta\in(0,1)\) under normalized momentum descent with \(M_0={\mathbf 0}\):
\begin{equation}
M_{t+1}=\beta M_t+(1-\beta)\nabla L(W_t),\qquad
\Delta_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\psi(\Delta)\le1}\langle M_{t+1},\Delta\rangle,
\qquad
W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta_t\Delta_t,
\label{eq:app-ms-nmd}
\end{equation}
In either case, every accumulation point of \(W_t/\psi(W_t)\) is a \(\psi\)-maximum-margin solution.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The geometry-dependent steps in the normalized steepest-descent and momentum proofs of \citet[Appendices~D and E]{fan2026implicit} use only norm duality, the lower bound \(\psi^*(\nabla L(W))\ge\gamma_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W)\), the upper bound \(\psi^*(\nabla L(W))\le2R_1(X)\mathcal G(W)\), and the logit and Hessian controls in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ms-basic}. Substituting these bounds into their pre-rate scalar argument gives
\[
\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)\ge\gamma_\psi(X)S_t-r_t,\qquad \psi(W_t)\le\psi(W_0)+S_t,
\]
where \(r_t\) is a finite-prefix term plus sums of the forms \(\sum_s\eta_s^2\) and \(\sum_s\eta_s\exp(-c\sum_{\tau<s}\eta_\tau)\); in the momentum case, Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} controls the additional geometric-memory term. Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-remainders} gives \(r_t=o(S_t)\), and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-normalization} with \(\mathfrak m=\operatorname{mar}_X\) and \(\Gamma=\Gamma_*=\gamma_\psi(X)\) proves the result.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:app-ms-full-batch-adam}
Consider full-batch Adam without bias correction or a numerical-stability constant, initialized by \(M_0=V_0={\mathbf 0}\):
\begin{align}
M_{t+1}&=\beta_1M_t+(1-\beta_1)\nabla L(W_t),\nonumber\\
V_{t+1}&=\beta_2V_t+(1-\beta_2)\nabla L(W_t)^{\odot2},\nonumber\\
W_{t+1}&=W_t-\eta_tM_{t+1}\oslash V_{t+1}^{\odot1/2}.
\label{eq:app-full-batch-adam}
\end{align}
Assume \(0<\beta_1\le\beta_2<1\), Assumptions~\ref{ass:lr-base} and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}, and \(\min_{c\in[k],\,j\in[d]}|\nabla L(W_0)[c,j]|^2\ge\omega\) for some \(\omega>0\). Then, with
\[
\gamma_{\max}(X):=\max_{\|W\|_{\max}\le1}\operatorname{mar}_X(W),
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\|W_t\|_{\max}}\longrightarrow\gamma_{\max}(X),
\label{eq:app-adam-margin}
\end{equation}
and every accumulation point of \(W_t/\|W_t\|_{\max}\) is a max-norm maximum-margin solution.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
The pre-rate part of \citet[Appendix~G]{fan2026implicit} gives
\[
\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)\ge\gamma_{\max}(X)S_t-r_t,\qquad \|W_t\|_{\max}\le C_0+S_t,
\]
where \(r_t\) consists of a finite prefix, \(\sum_s\eta_s^{3/2}\), and an exponentially weighted remainder. Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-remainders} gives \(r_t=o(S_t)\), and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-normalization} proves~\eqref{eq:app-adam-margin} and the accumulation-point conclusion.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-ga-atomic-package}
For every matrix norm \(\psi\), every sample \(x_n\), every matrix \(A\), and all classes \(a,c\in[k]\),
\begin{equation}
\|Ax_n\|_\infty\le R_\psi(X)\psi(A),\qquad \psi^*((e_a-e_c)x_n^\top)\le2R_\psi(X).
\label{eq:app-ga-logit-atom}
\end{equation}
For every \(W\),
\begin{equation}
\gamma_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W)\le\psi^*(\nabla L(W))\le2R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W).
\label{eq:app-ga-gradient-proxy}
\end{equation}
For every sample \(n\), every \(W\), and every perturbation \(A\),
\begin{equation}
D^2\ell_n(W)[A,A]\le4R_\psi(X)^2\bigl(1-{\mathbb{S}}(Wx_n)_{y_n}\bigr)\psi(A)^2.
\label{eq:app-ga-hessian}
\end{equation}
Moreover, for all \(U,W\),
\begin{equation}
|L(U)-L(W)|\le2R_\psi(X)\psi(U-W).
\label{eq:app-ga-loss-lipschitz}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
For every \(c\in[k]\), norm duality gives
\[
|e_c^\top Ax_n|=|\langle A,e_cx_n^\top\rangle|\le\psi(A)\psi^*(e_cx_n^\top)\le R_\psi(X)\psi(A),
\]
which proves the first bound in~\eqref{eq:app-ga-logit-atom}; the second follows from the triangle inequality. Writing \(p_n(W):={\mathbb{S}}(Wx_n)\), the sample gradient has the decomposition
\[
\nabla\ell_n(W)=\sum_{c\ne y_n}p_{n,c}(W)(e_c-e_{y_n})x_n^\top,
\]
so
\[
\psi^*(\nabla\ell_n(W))\le2R_\psi(X)\bigl(1-p_{n,y_n}(W)\bigr).
\]
Averaging proves the upper bound in~\eqref{eq:app-ga-gradient-proxy}. For the lower bound, choose \(A_\star\) with \(\psi(A_\star)\le1\) and margin \(\gamma_\psi(X)\); then
\[
-\nabla L(W)=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\sum_{c\ne y_n}p_{n,c}(W)(e_{y_n}-e_c)x_n^\top
\]
gives \(\psi^*(\nabla L(W))\ge\langle A_\star,-\nabla L(W)\rangle\ge\gamma_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W)\). For the Hessian bound, set \(v:=Ax_n\) and let \(C\) be categorical with law \(p_n(W)\). Then
\[
D^2\ell_n(W)[A,A]=\operatorname{Var}(v_C)\le\mathbb E[(v_C-v_{y_n})^2]\le4(1-p_{n,y_n}(W))\|v\|_\infty^2,
\]
which proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-hessian}. Finally, convexity and the upper gradient bound, together with \(\mathcal G\le1\), yield \(L(U)-L(W)\le2R_\psi(X)\psi(U-W)\); exchanging \(U,W\) proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-loss-lipschitz}.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-ga-stability-package}
For \(U,W\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\), define \(h:=R_\psi(X)\psi(U-W)\). Then, for every sample \(n\) and class \(c\),
\begin{equation}
e^{-2h}\le\frac{p_{n,c}(U)}{p_{n,c}(W)}\le e^{2h},\qquad e^{-2h}\le\frac{1-p_{n,y_n}(U)}{1-p_{n,y_n}(W)}\le e^{2h}.
\label{eq:app-ga-softmax-ratios}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\mathcal G(U)\le e^{2R_\psi(X)\psi(U-W)}\mathcal G(W),
\label{eq:app-ga-proxy-stability}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\psi^*(\nabla L(U)-\nabla L(W))\le2R_\psi(X)\Bigl(e^{2R_\psi(X)\psi(U-W)}-1\Bigr)\mathcal G(W),
\label{eq:app-ga-full-gradient-stability}
\end{equation}
and, for every mini-batch \(B\),
\begin{equation}
\psi^*(\nabla L_B(U)-\nabla L_B(W))\le2mR_\psi(X)\Bigl(e^{2R_\psi(X)\psi(U-W)}-1\Bigr)\mathcal G(W).
\label{eq:app-ga-batch-gradient-stability}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Set \(\delta_n:=(U-W)x_n\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-atomic-package} gives \(\|\delta_n\|_\infty\le h\), and the softmax formula gives
\[
\frac{p_{n,c}(U)}{p_{n,c}(W)}=e^{\delta_{n,c}}\frac{\sum_{a=1}^ke^{e_a^\top Wx_n}}{\sum_{a=1}^ke^{e_a^\top Wx_n+\delta_{n,a}}}\in[e^{-2h},e^{2h}].
\]
Summing over \(c\ne y_n\) proves the second ratio and~\eqref{eq:app-ga-proxy-stability}. If \(p:=p_n(W)\) and \(q:=p_n(U)\), the ratio bounds imply
\[
\sum_{c\ne y_n}|q_c-p_c|\le(e^{2h}-1)(1-p_{y_n}),\qquad |q_{y_n}-p_{y_n}|\le(e^{2h}-1)(1-p_{y_n}).
\]
Since \(\nabla\ell_n(U)-\nabla\ell_n(W)=(q-p)x_n^\top\),
\[
\psi^*((q-p)x_n^\top)\le\sum_{c=1}^k|q_c-p_c|\psi^*(e_cx_n^\top)\le2R_\psi(X)(e^{2h}-1)(1-p_{y_n}).
\]
Averaging over all samples proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-full-gradient-stability}; averaging over \(B\), enlarging the resulting nonnegative sample sum to \([N]\), and using \(N/b=m\) proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-batch-gradient-stability}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-ga-batch-noise}
\label{lem:app-ga-frozen-rr}
For a mini-batch \(B\) of size \(b\), define \(\Xi_B(W):=\nabla L_B(W)-\nabla L(W)\). Then
\begin{equation}
\psi^*(\Xi_B(W))\le2(m-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W).
\label{eq:app-ga-batch-noise}
\end{equation}
Moreover, let \(\{B_t\}_{t\ge0}\) be any random-reshuffling sequence, so that \(B_{qm},\ldots,B_{qm+m-1}\) partition \([N]\) for every epoch \(q\), and define
\begin{equation}
E_t(W):=(1-\beta)\sum_{\tau=0}^t\beta^\tau\bigl(\nabla L_{B_{t-\tau}}(W)-\nabla L(W)\bigr).
\label{eq:app-ga-frozen-ema}
\end{equation}
Then, deterministically for every reshuffling realization,
\begin{equation}
\psi^*(E_t(W))\le(1-\beta)m(m^2-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W).
\label{eq:app-ga-frozen-rr-bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
When \(m\ge2\), let \(B^c=[N]\setminus B\). The finite-population identity
\[
\Xi_B(W)=\frac{m-1}{m}\bigl(\nabla L_B(W)-\nabla L_{B^c}(W)\bigr)
\]
and the single-sample bound in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-atomic-package} give
\[
\psi^*(\Xi_B(W))\le\frac{m-1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N\psi^*(\nabla\ell_n(W))\le2(m-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W),
\]
while \(m=1\) is immediate.

For the second assertion, write \(\Xi_t(W):=\nabla L_{B_t}(W)-\nabla L(W)\). Every complete epoch satisfies \(\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\Xi_{qm+r}(W)={\mathbf 0}\). Put \(K_\Xi(W):=2(m-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W)\). For a complete epoch contained in \(\{0,\ldots,t\}\), subtracting the constant coefficient \(\beta^{t-qm}\) and using \(1-\beta^r\le r(1-\beta)\) gives
\[
\psi^*\left(\sum_{r=0}^{m-1}\beta^{t-qm-r}\Xi_{qm+r}(W)\right)\le K_\Xi(W)\beta^{t-(q+1)m}(1-\beta)\frac{m(m-1)}2.
\]
Summing over complete epochs and using \((1-\beta)/(1-\beta^m)\le1\), then adding the at most \(m\) terms in the current incomplete epoch, gives
\[
\psi^*(E_t(W))\le(1-\beta)\frac{m(m+1)}2K_\Xi(W)=(1-\beta)m(m^2-1)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W).
\]
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-ga-momentum-approximation}
\label{prop:app-ga-descent-recurrence}
Assume Assumptions~\ref{ass:lr-base} and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}. For every fixed finite dataset, fixed matrix norm \(\psi\), and fixed \(\beta\in(0,1)\), there exist \(t_{0,\psi,\beta}<\infty\) and \(c_{\psi,\beta}<\infty\) such that, for all \(t\ge t_{0,\psi,\beta}\),
\begin{align}
\psi^*(M_{t+1}-\nabla L(W_t))\le\Bigl[&2m(1-\beta)R_\psi(X)c_{\psi,\beta}\eta_t+(1-\beta)m(m^2-1)R_\psi(X)\nonumber\\
&+2R_\psi(X)\beta^{t+1}\Bigr]\mathcal G(W_t).
\label{eq:app-ga-momentum-approximation}
\end{align}
Define
\begin{equation}
\rho_{\psi,\beta,b}(X):=\gamma_\psi(X)-2(1-\beta)m(m^2-1)R_\psi(X),
\label{eq:app-ga-effective-margin}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
C_{\psi,\beta,b}:=4m(1-\beta)R_\psi(X)c_{\psi,\beta}+2R_\psi(X)^2e^{2R_\psi(X)\eta_0},\qquad D_\psi:=4R_\psi(X).
\label{eq:app-ga-descent-constants}
\end{equation}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(t\),
\begin{equation}
L(W_{t+1})\le L(W_t)-\eta_t\Bigl(\rho_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)-C_{\psi,\beta,b}\eta_t-D_\psi\beta^{t/2}\Bigr)\mathcal G(W_t).
\label{eq:app-ga-descent-recurrence}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Unrolling the momentum recursion and adding and subtracting frozen batch gradients at \(W_t\) gives
\begin{align}
M_{t+1}-\nabla L(W_t)=&(1-\beta)\sum_{\tau=0}^t\beta^\tau\Bigl(\nabla L_{B_{t-\tau}}(W_{t-\tau})-\nabla L_{B_{t-\tau}}(W_t)\Bigr)\nonumber\\
&+(1-\beta)\sum_{\tau=0}^t\beta^\tau\Bigl(\nabla L_{B_{t-\tau}}(W_t)-\nabla L(W_t)\Bigr)-\beta^{t+1}\nabla L(W_t).
\label{eq:app-ga-momentum-decomposition}
\end{align}
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-stability-package} and~\eqref{eq:app-ga-path-length} bound the first term by
\[
2m(1-\beta)R_\psi(X)\mathcal G(W_t)\sum_{\tau=0}^t\beta^\tau\left(\exp\left(2R_\psi(X)\sum_{q=1}^{\tau}\eta_{t-q}\right)-1\right).
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}, applied with \(c_1=2R_\psi(X)\), bounds the final sum by \(c_{\psi,\beta}\eta_t\) for all sufficiently large \(t\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-frozen-rr} controls the second term, and the upper gradient bound in~\eqref{eq:app-ga-gradient-proxy} controls the last, proving~\eqref{eq:app-ga-momentum-approximation}.

For the descent recurrence, the steepest-descent property and norm duality give
\begin{equation}
\langle\nabla L(W_t),\Delta_t\rangle\ge\psi^*(\nabla L(W_t))-2\psi^*(M_{t+1}-\nabla L(W_t)).
\label{eq:app-ga-first-order-alignment}
\end{equation}
The mean-value Taylor formula,~\eqref{eq:app-ga-hessian}, and \(\psi(\Delta_t)\le1\) bound the quadratic remainder in \(L(W_t-\eta_t\Delta_t)\) by
\[
2\eta_t^2R_\psi(X)^2\sup_{0\le s\le1}\mathcal G(W_t-s\eta_t\Delta_t).
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-ga-stability-package} bounds the supremum by \(e^{2R_\psi(X)\eta_0}\mathcal G(W_t)\). Substituting~\eqref{eq:app-ga-gradient-proxy} and~\eqref{eq:app-ga-momentum-approximation} into~\eqref{eq:app-ga-first-order-alignment}, adding the quadratic remainder, and using \(\beta^{t+1}\le\beta^{t/2}\) proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-descent-recurrence}.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-ga-margin-transfer}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:lr-base} and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}, suppose \(\rho_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)>0\). Then
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\ge\rho_{\psi,\beta,b}(X).
\label{eq:app-ga-margin-conclusion}
\end{equation}
Consequently, with
\begin{equation}
\varepsilon_{\psi,\beta,b}(X):=2(1-\beta)m(m^2-1)R_\psi(X),
\label{eq:app-ga-epsilon}
\end{equation}
one has
\begin{equation}
d_{\cos}\!\left(W_t,\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)}^X\right)\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:app-ga-direction-conclusion}
\end{equation}
More quantitatively, there exist a finite \(t_2\) and \(C_{\mathrm{ga}}<\infty\) such that
\begin{equation}
\rho_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)-\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\psi(W_t)}\le C_{\mathrm{ga}}\frac{\mathcal R_t^{\psi,\beta,b}}{S_t},
\label{eq:app-ga-general-lr-bound}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align}
\mathcal R_t^{\psi,\beta,b}:=&1+\sum_{s=0}^{t_2-1}\eta_s+C_{\psi,\beta,b}\sum_{s=t_2}^{t-1}\eta_s^2+\frac{D_\psi\eta_0}{1-\sqrt\beta}\nonumber\\
&+\sum_{s=t_2}^{t-1}\eta_s\exp\!\left(-\frac{\rho_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)}4\sum_{\tau=t_2}^{s-1}\eta_\tau\right).
\label{eq:app-ga-remainder}
\end{align}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Write \(\rho:=\rho_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)>0\). Since \(\eta_t\to0\) and \(\beta^{t/2}\to0\), Proposition~\ref{prop:app-ga-descent-recurrence} gives a finite \(t_1\) after which the coefficient of \(\eta_t\mathcal G(W_t)\) is at least \(\rho/2\). The loss Lipschitz bound~\eqref{eq:app-ga-loss-lipschitz}, the divergence \(S_t\to\infty\), and the standard low-loss entrance argument give a finite \(t_2\ge t_1\) after which all empirical margins are nonnegative. The usual cross-entropy loss-to-margin conversion then yields
\[
\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)\ge\rho\sum_{s=t_2}^{t-1}\eta_s\frac{\mathcal G(W_s)}{L(W_s)}-C_{\psi,\beta,b}\sum_{s=t_2}^{t-1}\eta_s^2-\frac{D_\psi\eta_0}{1-\sqrt\beta}-C_0,
\]
where \(C_0<\infty\) absorbs the finite prefix. The post-entrance descent recurrence and the standard cross-entropy proxy inequalities give
\[
\frac{\mathcal G(W_s)}{L(W_s)}\ge1-\exp\!\left(-\frac{\rho}{4}\sum_{\tau=t_2}^{s-1}\eta_\tau\right).
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)\ge\rho S_t-C_1\mathcal R_t^{\psi,\beta,b}\) for some \(C_1<\infty\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-remainders} gives \(\mathcal R_t^{\psi,\beta,b}=o(S_t)\), while \(\psi(W_t)\le\psi(W_0)+S_t\) follows directly from the normalized update. Lemma~\ref{lem:app-general-lr-normalization} proves~\eqref{eq:app-ga-general-lr-bound} and~\eqref{eq:app-ga-margin-conclusion}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:effective-margin-direction-convergence} gives~\eqref{eq:app-ga-direction-conclusion}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-row-steepest}
For every \(A,G\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\),
\begin{equation}
\|A\|_{\max}\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{row}}\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{sum}},
\label{eq:app-row-max-sum}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
N_{\mathrm{row}}(G)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm{row}}\le1}\langle G,\Delta\rangle,\qquad \max_{\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm{row}}\le1}\langle G,\Delta\rangle=\sum_{r=1}^k\|G_{r,:}\|_2.
\label{eq:app-row-steepest}
\end{equation}
Thus row-wise normalized gradient methods are normalized steepest-descent methods for the row norm.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Every entry is bounded by the Euclidean norm of its row, while \(\max_r\|A_{r,:}\|_2\le\sum_r\|A_{r,:}\|_1=\|A\|_{\mathrm{sum}}\), proving~\eqref{eq:app-row-max-sum}. The constraint \(\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm{row}}\le1\) is equivalent to \(\|\Delta_{r,:}\|_2\le1\) for every row \(r\), so
\[
\max_{\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm{row}}\le1}\langle G,\Delta\rangle=\sum_{r=1}^k\max_{\|u\|_2\le1}\langle G_{r,:},u\rangle=\sum_{r=1}^k\|G_{r,:}\|_2,
\]
and \(N_{\mathrm{row}}(G)\) attains the maximum.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-row-full-batch}
Consider any fixed linearly separable multiclass dataset with bounded features. Under Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-base}, row-wise normalized GD satisfies
\begin{equation}
\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\|W_t\|_{\mathrm{row}}}\longrightarrow\gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(X),\qquad \inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X}\left\|\frac{W_t}{\|W_t\|_{\mathrm F}}-\frac{V}{\|V\|_{\mathrm F}}\right\|_{\mathrm F}\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:app-row-gd-direction}
\end{equation}
If Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-momentum} also holds, the same two conclusions hold for row-wise normalized GD with every fixed momentum parameter \(\beta\in(0,1)\).
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-row-steepest} shows that the row norm is max--sum dominated and that row normalization is its exact steepest direction. Theorem~\ref{thm:app-ms-full-batch} therefore gives normalized-margin convergence, and Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-margin-direction-convergence} gives \(d_{\cos}(W_t,\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X)\to0\). Since
\[
\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X}\left\|\frac{W_t}{\|W_t\|_{\mathrm F}}-\frac{V}{\|V\|_{\mathrm F}}\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2=2d_{\cos}(W_t,\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X),
\]
the Frobenius direction-set convergence follows.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{cor:row-sgdm-rr-margin-clean}
Consider any fixed linearly separable multiclass dataset with bounded features. Run random-reshuffling row-wise normalized SGDM with \(b\mid N\), \(m:=N/b\), and fixed \(\beta\in(0,1)\). Define
\begin{equation}
R_{\mathrm{row}}(X):=\max_{n\in[N]}\|x_n\|_2,\qquad \varepsilon_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}(X):=2(1-\beta)m(m^2-1)R_{\mathrm{row}}(X).
\label{eq:app-row-sgdm-epsilon}
\end{equation}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:lr-base} and~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}, if \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}(X)<\gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(X)\), then
\begin{equation}
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\|W_t\|_{\mathrm{row}}}\ge\gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(X)-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}(X),
\label{eq:row-sgdm-rr-margin-clean}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
d_{\cos}\!\left(W_t,\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}(X)}^X\right)\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:row-sgdm-rr-direction-clean}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:app-ga-margin-transfer} with \(\psi=\|\cdot\|_{\mathrm{row}}\). Equation~\eqref{eq:app-ga-three-radii} gives \(R_\psi(X)=R_{\mathrm{row}}(X)\), so~\eqref{eq:app-ga-effective-margin} becomes \(\gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(X)-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}(X)\), yielding~\eqref{eq:row-sgdm-rr-margin-clean}. Equation~\eqref{eq:row-sgdm-rr-direction-clean} follows from~\eqref{eq:app-ga-direction-conclusion}.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-common-rescaling}
Let \(c>0\), let \(cX:=\{(cx_n,y_n)\}_{n=1}^N\), and let \(\psi\) be any matrix norm. Then
\begin{equation}
\mathcal F_{cX}=c^{-1}\mathcal F_X,\qquad \mathcal M_\psi^{cX}=c^{-1}\mathcal M_\psi^X,\qquad \mathcal U_\psi^{cX}=\mathcal U_\psi^X.
\label{eq:app-common-rescaling}
\end{equation}
The normalized pairwise row directions and \(D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}\) are unchanged. If the test inputs are also multiplied by \(c\), then \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(c^{-1}W;cX^{\mathrm{te}})=\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W;X^{\mathrm{te}})\).
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The constraint \((w_{y_n}-w_j)^\top(cx_n)\ge1\) is equivalent, after writing \(W=c^{-1}V\), to \((v_{y_n}-v_j)^\top x_n\ge1\). Positive homogeneity of \(\psi\) proves the identities for the feasible and minimum-norm sets, and the ray identity follows from \eqref{eq:minmax-equivalence-clean}. Finally, \((c^{-1}w_j)^\top(cx)=w_j^\top x\), so all predictions agree.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:deterministic-separation-clean}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud} and~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, there are deterministic \(\omega_d\downarrow0\) and events \(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}})\ge1-e^{-\sqrt d},
\label{eq:app-det-clean-probability}
\end{equation}
and, on \(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}}\), \(\mathcal F_X\ne\varnothing\) and
\begin{align}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X}\max_{i\ne j}\|u_{ij}^U-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2&\le\omega_d,
\label{eq:det-row-uniform-clean}\\
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U)&\le\omega_d,
\label{eq:det-row-clean}\\
\inf_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U)&\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)-\omega_d,
\label{eq:det-sp-clean}\\
\inf_{U\in\mathcal U_{\max}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U)&\ge\delta_{\max}-\omega_d.
\label{eq:det-max-clean}
\end{align}
Consequently, for every sufficiently large \(d\) on \(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}}\),
\begin{equation}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U)<\min\left\{\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V),\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\max}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V)\right\}.
\label{eq:det-set-order-clean}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-ray-reduction}
For every $\psi\in\{\psi_{\mathrm{row}},\psi_{\mathrm{sp}},\psi_{\max}\}$,
\begin{align}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_\psi^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U)
&=
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_\psi^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W),
\label{eq:app-det-ray-sup}\\
\inf_{U\in\mathcal U_\psi^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U)
&=
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_\psi^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W).
\label{eq:app-det-ray-inf}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
By \eqref{eq:minmax-equivalence-clean}, $\mathcal U_\psi^X=\{aW:a>0,\ W\in\mathcal M_\psi^X\}$. The conclusion follows from the positive scale invariance of $D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-common-event}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud} and~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, there are deterministic \(\varepsilon_d\downarrow0\), universal \(C<\infty\), a constant \(c=c(r_0)>0\), and events \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) such that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\!\left((\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}})^c\right)\le C\exp\!\left[-c\sqrt{d\log(2N(d)(d+1))}\right]
\label{eq:app-det-common-event-probability}
\end{equation}
and the following statements hold simultaneously on \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(H\arabic*)]
\item \label{item:app-det-H1} \(\max_i\|m_i-\mu_i\|_2\le\varepsilon_d\).
\item \label{item:app-det-H2} \(\max_i|\|m_i\|_2-1|\le\varepsilon_d\) and \(\max_{i\ne j}|m_i^\top m_j|\le\varepsilon_d\).
\item \label{item:app-det-H3} \(\max_{i,j,s}|m_j^\top e_{i,s}|\le\varepsilon_d\).
\item \label{item:app-det-H4} \(\max_{i\ne j}\|u_{ij}^m-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2\le\varepsilon_d\).
\item \label{item:app-det-H5} The max-norm optimum is finite and satisfies
\begin{equation}
2\sqrt d\,r_{\max}^*(X)\le\sqrt{2\pi}+\varepsilon_d.
\label{eq:app-det-max-optimum-upper}
\end{equation}
\item \label{item:app-det-H6} Uniformly over ordered pairs,
\begin{equation}
\sup_{0\le\tau\le1}|H_{u_{ij}^m}(\tau)-A_{\max}(\tau)|+\sup_{0\le\tau\le1}|J_{u_{ij}^m}(\tau)-B_{\max}(\tau)|\le\varepsilon_d.
\label{eq:app-det-HJ-uniform}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Put \(L_d:=\log(2N(d)(d+1))\) and \(a_d:=(L_d/d)^{1/4}\).
The assumptions \(\log N=o(d)\) and \(n_{\min}\to\infty\) imply \(a_d\to0\).
All normalized Gaussian vectors below obey the shell bound
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\!\left(\left|\frac{\|g\|_2}{\sqrt d}-1\right|>t\right)\le2e^{-cdt^2},\qquad 0<t<1,
\label{eq:app-det-gaussian-shell}
\end{equation}
and every centered Gaussian scalar with variance at most \(C/d\) obeys \(\mathbb P(|Z|>t)\le2e^{-cdt^2/C}\).

Since \(\bar z_i\overset{\mathrm d}=g_i/\sqrt{n_i d}\), the event \(\max_i\|\bar z_i\|_2\le2/\sqrt{n_{\min}}\) fails with probability at most \(2N e^{-cd}\).
Thus
\begin{equation}
\max_i\|m_i-\mu_i\|_2\le\frac{2r_0}{\sqrt{n_{\min}}}=o(1)
\label{eq:app-det-mean-concentration}
\end{equation}
on an event whose failure probability is smaller than the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:app-det-common-event-probability}.
Applying \eqref{eq:app-det-gaussian-shell} to \(\mu_i\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d/d)\), with threshold \(Ca_d\), and taking a union bound proves \(\max_i|\|\mu_i\|_2-1|\le Ca_d\).
Conditionally on \(\mu_i\), the variable \(\mu_i^\top\mu_j\) is centered Gaussian with variance \(\|\mu_i\|_2^2/d\).
Another union bound over at most \(N^2\) ordered pairs gives \(\max_{i\ne j}|\mu_i^\top\mu_j|\le Ca_d\).
Combining these estimates with \eqref{eq:app-det-mean-concentration} proves (H1) and (H2).

Conditionally on all empirical means, \(m_j^\top e_{i,s}\) is centered Gaussian with variance at most \(r_0^2\|m_j\|_2^2/d\).
On the event \(\max_j\|m_j\|_2\le2\), a union bound over at most \(N^2\) triples gives \(\max_{i,j,s}|m_j^\top e_{i,s}|\le Ca_d\) with the required failure probability.
This proves (H3).
Items (H1)--(H2) imply \(\inf_{i\ne j}\|m_i-m_j\|_2\ge1\) and \(\inf_{i\ne j}\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2\ge1\) for all sufficiently large \(d\).
The normalization map is Lipschitz on vectors with norm at least one, so (H1) gives (H4).

For (H5), let \(s_i:=\operatorname{sign}(m_i)\in\{-1,1\}^d\).
Because each \(m_i\) is isotropic Gaussian, \(s_i\) is a uniform sign vector, and it is independent of every residual in its own class.
Bernstein's inequality for \(\|m_i\|_1\), Gaussian tails for \(s_j^\top m_i\) when \(i\ne j\), conditional Gaussian tails for \(s_j^\top e_{i,s}\), and a union bound give
\begin{equation}
\min_i\|m_i\|_1\ge\left(\sqrt{\frac2\pi}-o(1)\right)\sqrt d,\qquad \max_{i\ne j}|s_j^\top m_i|+\max_{i,j,s}|s_j^\top e_{i,s}|=o(\sqrt d)
\label{eq:app-det-sign-inputs}
\end{equation}
outside an event bounded as in \eqref{eq:app-det-common-event-probability}.
The matrix with rows \(w_i=t_ds_i\), where \(t_d\) is the reciprocal of the minimum bracket in
\begin{equation}
(s_i-s_j)^\top x_{i,s}\ge\|m_i\|_1-|s_j^\top m_i|-2\max_{\ell}|s_\ell^\top e_{i,s}|,
\label{eq:app-det-sign-margin}
\end{equation}
is feasible.
Equation \eqref{eq:app-det-sign-inputs} gives \(t_d\le(\sqrt{\pi/2}+o(1))/\sqrt d\), which is exactly (H5).

For (H6), each difference \(m_i-m_j\) is a centered isotropic Gaussian vector, even when \(n_i\ne n_j\), so \(u_{ij}^m\) is exactly uniform on \(\mathbb S^{d-1}\).
For one uniform direction, the two coordinate empirical processes in \eqref{eq:app-det-HJ} concentrate about \(A_{\max}\) and \(B_{\max}\) at rate \(e^{-cd\eta^2}\) for any fixed \(\tau\).
On the event \(d^{-1}\sum_\ell d u_\ell^2=1\), both processes are uniformly Lipschitz in \(\tau\).
A mesh of \([0,1]\) with spacing \(a_d\), followed by a union bound over the mesh and at most \(N^2\) ordered pairs, yields \eqref{eq:app-det-HJ-uniform} with error \(Ca_d\) and failure probability bounded by \eqref{eq:app-det-common-event-probability}.
Taking \(\varepsilon_d\) to dominate \(Ca_d\), \(2r_0/\sqrt{n_{\min}}\), and the deterministic vanishing envelopes in \eqref{eq:app-det-sign-inputs} completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-normalization}
Let \(x,y\in\mathbb R^d\) with \(y\ne{\mathbf 0}\).
If \(\|x-y\|_2\le\|y\|_2/2\), then
\begin{equation}
\left\|\frac{x}{\|x\|_2}-\frac{y}{\|y\|_2}\right\|_2\le\frac{4\|x-y\|_2}{\|y\|_2}.
\label{eq:app-det-normalization-bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
The reverse triangle inequality gives \(\|x\|_2\ge\|y\|_2/2\).
Adding and subtracting \(y/\|x\|_2\) and applying the reverse triangle inequality once more gives the displayed bound.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-row-rigidity}
Fix deterministic samples $x_{i,s}=m_i+e_{i,s}$ with $\sum_s e_{i,s}={\mathbf 0}$ for every $i$. Suppose that, for some $0<h<1/20$,
\begin{equation}
\max_i\bigl|\|m_i\|_2-1\bigr|\le h,
\qquad
\max_{i\ne j}|m_i^\top m_j|\le h,
\qquad
\max_{i,j,s}|m_j^\top e_{i,s}|\le h.
\label{eq:app-det-row-rigidity-assumption}
\end{equation}
Then $\mathcal F_X$ is nonempty, and every $W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^X$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\max_i\|w_i-m_i\|_2
\le
C\left(h+\frac1k\right)^{1/4}
\label{eq:app-det-row-rigidity-conclusion}
\end{equation}
for a universal constant $C$.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
For $i\ne j$ and $s\le n_i$,
\begin{align}
(m_i-m_j)^\top x_{i,s}
&=\|m_i\|_2^2-m_j^\top m_i+(m_i-m_j)^\top e_{i,s}
\notag\\
&\ge (1-h)^2-h-2h
\ge 1-5h.
\label{eq:app-det-row-witness-margin}
\end{align}
Hence the matrix with rows $\widetilde w_i=m_i/(1-5h)$ is feasible. If $R^*:=\max_i\|w_i\|_2$ is the optimal row radius, then
\begin{equation}
R^*\le\frac{1+h}{1-5h}\le1+Ch.
\label{eq:app-det-row-radius-upper}
\end{equation}

Let $\bar w:=k^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^k w_r$. For any feasible $W$, averaging the constraints over $s=1,\ldots,n_i$ and summing over $j\ne i$ gives
\begin{equation}
\sum_{j\ne i}(w_i-w_j)^\top m_i\ge k-1.
\label{eq:app-det-row-summed-constraints}
\end{equation}
Since $\sum_{j\ne i}w_j=k\bar w-w_i$, this is equivalent to
\begin{equation}
(w_i-\bar w)^\top m_i\ge1-\frac1k.
\label{eq:app-det-row-centering-constraint}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\|w_i-\bar w\|_2
\ge
L:=\frac{1-1/k}{1+h}.
\label{eq:app-det-row-centered-lower}
\end{equation}
For a row-norm minimizer, the variance identity yields
\begin{align}
L^2
&\le
\frac1k\sum_{i=1}^k\|w_i-\bar w\|_2^2
=
\frac1k\sum_{i=1}^k\|w_i\|_2^2-\|\bar w\|_2^2
\le
(R^*)^2-\|\bar w\|_2^2.
\label{eq:app-det-row-variance-identity}
\end{align}
Combining this with \eqref{eq:app-det-row-radius-upper} gives
\begin{equation}
\|\bar w\|_2^2\le C\left(h+\frac1k\right).
\label{eq:app-det-row-common-shift-small}
\end{equation}
Using \eqref{eq:app-det-row-centering-constraint} once more,
\begin{equation}
w_i^\top m_i
\ge
1-\frac1k+\bar w^\top m_i
\ge
1-C\left(h+\frac1k\right)^{1/2}.
\label{eq:app-det-row-alignment-lower}
\end{equation}
Together with $\|w_i\|_2\le1+Ch$ and $\|m_i\|_2\le1+h$, this implies
\begin{align}
\|w_i-m_i\|_2^2
&=\|w_i\|_2^2+\|m_i\|_2^2-2w_i^\top m_i
\le
C\left(h+\frac1k\right)^{1/2}.
\label{eq:app-det-row-distance-square}
\end{align}
Taking square roots proves \eqref{eq:app-det-row-rigidity-conclusion}.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-row-boundary}
Under \eqref{eq:gaussian-cloud}--\eqref{eq:asymptotic-regime-clean},
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^X}
D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W)
=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-row-boundary-convergence}
\end{equation}
In fact, the stronger uniform pairwise statement
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^X}
\max_{i\ne j}
\|u_{ij}^W-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2
=o_{\mathbb P}(1)
\label{eq:app-det-row-uniform-pair}
\end{equation}
holds.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Work on $\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}. Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-rigidity} with $h=\varepsilon_d$. Since $k/d\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)$, we have $k\to\infty$, and therefore, uniformly over all row-norm minimizers,
\begin{equation}
\max_i\|w_i-m_i\|_2=o(1).
\label{eq:app-det-row-to-mean}
\end{equation}
Combining this with \ref{item:app-det-H1} gives
\begin{equation}
\Delta_d^{\mathrm{row}}
:=
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^X}
\max_i\|w_i-\mu_i\|_2
=o(1)
\label{eq:app-det-row-to-center}
\end{equation}
on $\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}$. Moreover, $\inf_{i\ne j}\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2$ is bounded below by a positive constant on the same event. Hence
\begin{equation}
\|(w_i-w_j)-(\mu_i-\mu_j)\|_2
\le2\Delta_d^{\mathrm{row}}
\label{eq:app-det-row-pair-perturbation}
\end{equation}
uniformly over $i\ne j$ and $W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^X$. Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-normalization} proves \eqref{eq:app-det-row-uniform-pair}, and averaging over ordered pairs gives \eqref{eq:app-det-row-boundary-convergence}.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-clipped-exact}
Fix $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ and $a,b>0$. Define
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)^2
:=
\min\left\{
\|x\|_2^2:
x^\top u\ge b,
\ \|x\|_\infty\le\frac{a}{\sqrt d}
\right\}.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-problem}
\end{equation}
Let $z_\ell:=\sqrt d\,|u_\ell|$. If
\begin{equation}
0<b<a\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell,
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-feasibility}
\end{equation}
then the minimizer is unique and has coordinates
\begin{equation}
x_\ell
=
\frac{a}{\sqrt d}\operatorname{sign}(u_\ell)\min\{\tau z_\ell,1\},
\qquad
\ell=1,\ldots,d,
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-solution}
\end{equation}
where $\operatorname{sign}(0):=0$ and $\tau>0$ is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}
H_u(\tau)=\frac ba.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-tau}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)^2=a^2J_u(\tau).
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-value}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
We first verify that the feasible set is nonempty. Define the coordinate-saturated vector $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d$ by
\begin{equation}
\widehat x_\ell:=\frac{a}{\sqrt d}\operatorname{sign}(u_\ell).
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-saturated-vector}
\end{equation}
Its projection onto $u$ is
\begin{equation}
\widehat x^\top u
=
\frac{a}{\sqrt d}\sum_{\ell=1}^d|u_\ell|
=
\frac ad\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell
>
b,
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-max-projection}
\end{equation}
where the strict inequality follows from \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-feasibility}. Choose \(c\) such that \(b/(\widehat x^\top u)<c<1\). Then \(c\widehat x\) satisfies the projection constraint strictly and lies strictly inside the coordinate box. The feasible set is thus nonempty.
It is also closed and bounded, so a minimizer exists. Since the objective $x\mapsto\|x\|_2^2$ is strictly convex and the feasible set is convex, this minimizer is unique.

Let $x^\star$ denote the unique minimizer. We next show that every nonzero coordinate of $x^\star$ has the same sign as the corresponding coordinate of $u$. Given any feasible $x$, define $x^\sharp$ by
\begin{equation}
x^\sharp_\ell:=
\begin{cases}
\operatorname{sign}(u_\ell)|x_\ell|,&u_\ell\ne0,\\
0,&u_\ell=0.
\end{cases}
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-sign-alignment}
\end{equation}
Then $\|x^\sharp\|_\infty\le\|x\|_\infty$, $\|x^\sharp\|_2\le\|x\|_2$, and
\begin{equation}
(x^\sharp)^\top u
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^d|x_\ell||u_\ell|
\ge
\sum_{\ell=1}^d x_\ell u_\ell
=
x^\top u.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-sign-projection}
\end{equation}
Applying this construction to $x^\star$ shows that $x^\sharp$ is feasible and has objective value no larger than that of $x^\star$. By optimality and uniqueness, $x^\star=x^\sharp$. Hence $x^\star_\ell$ has the sign of $u_\ell$ when $u_\ell\ne0$, and $x^\star_\ell=0$ when $u_\ell=0$.

The projection constraint must be active at the minimizer. Indeed, if $(x^\star)^\top u>b$, then
\begin{equation}
c:=\frac{b}{(x^\star)^\top u}
\end{equation}
satisfies $0<c<1$. The vector $cx^\star$ obeys $\|cx^\star\|_\infty\le a/\sqrt d$ and $(cx^\star)^\top u=b$, while
\begin{equation}
\|cx^\star\|_2^2=c^2\|x^\star\|_2^2<\|x^\star\|_2^2,
\end{equation}
contradicting the optimality of $x^\star$. Therefore,
\begin{equation}
(x^\star)^\top u=b.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-active-projection}
\end{equation}

Because of the sign alignment, write
\begin{equation}
y_\ell:=\frac{\sqrt d}{a}|x^\star_\ell|,
\qquad
0\le y_\ell\le1.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-y-definition}
\end{equation}
Using $|u_\ell|=z_\ell/\sqrt d$, the active projection constraint becomes
\begin{equation}
b
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^d|x^\star_\ell||u_\ell|
=
\frac ad\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell y_\ell,
\end{equation}
or equivalently,
\begin{equation}
\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell y_\ell=\frac{db}{a}.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-reduced-constraint}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
\|x^\star\|_2^2
=
\frac{a^2}{d}\sum_{\ell=1}^d y_\ell^2.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-reduced-objective}
\end{equation}
Therefore, finding $x^\star$ is equivalent to solving the convex optimization problem
\begin{equation}
\min_{0\le y_\ell\le1}
\frac12\sum_{\ell=1}^d y_\ell^2
\qquad
\text{subject to}
\qquad
\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell y_\ell\ge\frac{db}{a}.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-reduced-problem}
\end{equation}
The strict inequality in \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-feasibility} implies that the right-hand side of the constraint is strictly smaller than $\sum_\ell z_\ell$, so the reduced problem has a strictly feasible point. Hence the KKT conditions are necessary and sufficient.

Let $\tau\ge0$ be the multiplier associated with the constraint in \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-reduced-problem}. For fixed $\tau$, the Lagrangian minimization over the box $[0,1]^d$ separates across coordinates:
\begin{equation}
y_\ell
\in
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0\le y\le1}
\left\{
\frac12y^2-\tau z_\ell y
\right\}.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-coordinate-kkt}
\end{equation}
The unconstrained minimizer of the scalar objective is $y=\tau z_\ell$. Projecting this value onto $[0,1]$ gives
\begin{equation}
y_\ell=\min\{\tau z_\ell,1\}.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-y-solution}
\end{equation}
The multiplier must satisfy $\tau>0$. If $\tau=0$, then \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-coordinate-kkt} gives $y_\ell=0$ for every $\ell$, which violates the constraint because $b>0$. Since $\tau>0$, complementary slackness implies that the projection constraint is active:
\begin{equation}
\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell\min\{\tau z_\ell,1\}
=
\frac{db}{a}.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-multiplier-equation}
\end{equation}
After dividing by $d$, this is exactly
\begin{equation}
H_u(\tau)
=
\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell\min\{\tau z_\ell,1\}
=
\frac ba.
\end{equation}

It remains to verify that this equation has a unique solution. The function $H_u$ is continuous and nondecreasing on $[0,\infty)$, with
\begin{equation}
H_u(0)=0,
\qquad
\lim_{\tau\to\infty}H_u(\tau)
=
\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-H-endpoints}
\end{equation}
The condition \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-feasibility} places $b/a$ strictly between these two values, so existence follows from continuity. To prove uniqueness, take $0\le\tau_1<\tau_2$ and suppose that
\begin{equation}
H_u(\tau_1)<\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell.
\end{equation}
Then at least one coordinate with $z_\ell>0$ is not saturated at $\tau_1$, meaning $\tau_1z_\ell<1$. For that coordinate,
\begin{equation}
\min\{\tau_2z_\ell,1\}>\min\{\tau_1z_\ell,1\},
\end{equation}
while every other coordinate contributes a nondecreasing term. Thus $H_u(\tau_2)>H_u(\tau_1)$. Hence $H_u$ is strictly increasing before reaching its limiting value, and the equation $H_u(\tau)=b/a$ has a unique solution.

Substituting \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-y-solution} into the sign-aligned representation of $x^\star$ gives
\begin{equation}
x^\star_\ell
=
\frac{a}{\sqrt d}\operatorname{sign}(u_\ell)\min\{\tau z_\ell,1\},
\end{equation}
which proves \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-solution}. Finally,
\begin{align}
\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)^2
&=
\|x^\star\|_2^2 \notag\\
&=
\frac{a^2}{d}\sum_{\ell=1}^d\min\{\tau z_\ell,1\}^2 \notag\\
&=
a^2\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d\min\{\tau^2z_\ell^2,1\} \notag\\
&=
a^2J_u(\tau),
\end{align}
which proves \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-value}.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-clipped-asymptotic}
There exist constants $\delta_0,C_0>0$ such that the following holds. Suppose $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\sup_{0\le\tau\le1}|H_u(\tau)-A_{\max}(\tau)|+\sup_{0\le\tau\le1}|J_u(\tau)-B_{\max}(\tau)|\le\delta
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-HJ-close}
\end{equation}
with $0<\delta\le\delta_0$, and suppose
\begin{equation}
|a-\sqrt{2\pi}|+|b-\sqrt2|\le\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-ab-close}
\end{equation}
Then \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-feasibility} holds, the solution in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-clipped-exact} satisfies $\tau\in(0,1)$, and
\begin{align}
\frac1{\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)}
&\le C_{\max}+C_0\delta,
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-reciprocal}\\
\frac b{\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)}
&\le\kappa_{\max}+C_0\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-cosine}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Throughout the proof, $C>0$ denotes a constant independent of $d,u,a,b$, and $\delta$, and its value may change from line to line. Recall that $\tau_*>0$ is defined by
\begin{equation}
A_{\max}(\tau_*)=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}.
\label{eq:app-det-tau-star-recall}
\end{equation}
We first compare the required normalized projection $b/a$ with this reference value. By taking $\delta_0$ small enough, \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-ab-close} ensures that $a\ge\sqrt{2\pi}/2$. Hence
\begin{align}
\left|\frac ba-\frac1{\sqrt\pi}\right|
&=
\left|\frac ba-\frac{\sqrt2}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\right| \notag\\
&\le
\frac{|b-\sqrt2|}{a}
+
\sqrt2\left|\frac1a-\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\right| \notag\\
&=
\frac{|b-\sqrt2|}{a}
+
\frac{\sqrt2\,|a-\sqrt{2\pi}|}{a\sqrt{2\pi}}
\le C\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-ratio-close}
\end{align}
Thus the right-hand side of the equation $H_u(\tau)=b/a$ is within $O(\delta)$ of $A_{\max}(\tau_*)$.

We next show that the clipped problem is feasible and that its multiplier satisfies $\tau<1$. Since $\tau_*<1$ and $A_{\max}$ is strictly increasing, the constant
\begin{equation}
g_*:=A_{\max}(1)-A_{\max}(\tau_*)=A_{\max}(1)-\frac1{\sqrt\pi}
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-positive-gap}
\end{equation}
is strictly positive. By \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-HJ-close},
\begin{equation}
H_u(1)\ge A_{\max}(1)-\delta=\frac1{\sqrt\pi}+g_*-\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-H-one-lower}
\end{equation}
On the other hand, \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-ratio-close} gives
\begin{equation}
\frac ba\le\frac1{\sqrt\pi}+C\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-ratio-upper}
\end{equation}
After decreasing $\delta_0$ if necessary, these two bounds imply
\begin{equation}
0<\frac ba<H_u(1).
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-ratio-below-H-one}
\end{equation}
Because
\begin{equation}
H_u(1)=\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell\min\{z_\ell,1\}\le\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell,
\end{equation}
we obtain
\begin{equation}
0<b<a\frac1d\sum_{\ell=1}^d z_\ell.
\end{equation}
This is exactly \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-feasibility}. Moreover, $H_u(0)=0$ and $H_u(1)>b/a$, so Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-clipped-exact} gives a unique solution $\tau\in(0,1)$ of
\begin{equation}
H_u(\tau)=\frac ba.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-solution-equation}
\end{equation}

We now show that this solution is close to $\tau_*$. Using \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-solution-equation}, \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-HJ-close}, \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-ratio-close}, and \eqref{eq:app-det-tau-star-recall}, we obtain
\begin{align}
|A_{\max}(\tau)-A_{\max}(\tau_*)|
&\le
|A_{\max}(\tau)-H_u(\tau)|
+
\left|H_u(\tau)-A_{\max}(\tau_*)\right| \notag\\
&=
|A_{\max}(\tau)-H_u(\tau)|
+
\left|\frac ba-\frac1{\sqrt\pi}\right|
\le C\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-A-close}
\end{align}
For $s\in(0,1]$, differentiation under the expectation gives
\begin{equation}
A_{\max}'(s)=\mathbb E\left[G^2\mathbf{1}_{\{s|G|\le1\}}\right].
\label{eq:app-det-A-derivative}
\end{equation}
Since $s\le1$, the event $\{|G|\le1\}$ is contained in $\{s|G|\le1\}$. Therefore
\begin{equation}
A_{\max}'(s)\ge c_A,
\qquad
c_A:=\mathbb E\left[G^2\mathbf{1}_{\{|G|\le1\}}\right]>0.
\label{eq:app-det-A-derivative-lower}
\end{equation}
The mean value theorem and \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-A-close} now give
\begin{equation}
c_A|\tau-\tau_*|
\le
|A_{\max}(\tau)-A_{\max}(\tau_*)|
\le C\delta,
\end{equation}
and hence
\begin{equation}
|\tau-\tau_*|\le C\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-tau-close}
\end{equation}

We next lower-bound $J_u(\tau)$. The first assumption of the lemma gives
\begin{equation}
J_u(\tau)\ge B_{\max}(\tau)-\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-J-first-lower}
\end{equation}
The function $B_{\max}$ is Lipschitz on $[0,1]$. Indeed, for $s,t\in[0,1]$,
\begin{align}
|B_{\max}(s)-B_{\max}(t)|
&\le
\mathbb E\left[\left|\min\{s^2G^2,1\}-\min\{t^2G^2,1\}\right|\right] \notag\\
&\le
|s^2-t^2|\mathbb E[G^2]
\le
2|s-t|.
\label{eq:app-det-B-Lipschitz}
\end{align}
Combining this bound with \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-tau-close} gives
\begin{equation}
B_{\max}(\tau)\ge B_{\max}(\tau_*)-C\delta.
\end{equation}
Therefore,
\begin{equation}
J_u(\tau)\ge B_{\max}(\tau_*)-C\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-J-lower}
\end{equation}

The assumption on $a$ also gives
\begin{align}
a^2
&\ge
\left(\sqrt{2\pi}-\delta\right)^2
\ge
2\pi-C\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-a-square-lower}
\end{align}
Using the exact identity from Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-clipped-exact},
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)^2=a^2J_u(\tau),
\end{equation}
together with \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-J-lower} and \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-a-square-lower}, we obtain
\begin{align}
\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)^2
&\ge
(2\pi-C\delta)\left(B_{\max}(\tau_*)-C\delta\right) \notag\\
&\ge
2\pi B_{\max}(\tau_*)-C\delta.
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-energy-lower}
\end{align}

Set
\begin{equation}
M_*:=2\pi B_{\max}(\tau_*)>0.
\end{equation}
By taking $\delta_0$ smaller if necessary, \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-energy-lower} implies
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)^2\ge M_*-C\delta\ge\frac{M_*}{2}.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{align}
\frac1{\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)}
&\le
\frac1{\sqrt{M_*-C\delta}} \notag\\
&\le
\frac1{\sqrt{M_*}}+C\delta \notag\\
&=
C_{\max}+C\delta,
\label{eq:app-det-clipped-reciprocal-proof}
\end{align}
where the last equality follows from
\begin{equation}
C_{\max}=\left(2\pi B_{\max}(\tau_*)\right)^{-1/2}.
\end{equation}
After enlarging the constant, this proves \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-reciprocal}.

Finally, \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-ab-close} gives $b\le\sqrt2+\delta$. Therefore,
\begin{align}
\frac b{\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)}
&\le
(\sqrt2+\delta)(C_{\max}+C_0\delta) \notag\\
&\le
\sqrt2\,C_{\max}+C\delta \notag\\
&=
\kappa_{\max}+C\delta,
\end{align}
because $\kappa_{\max}=\sqrt2\,C_{\max}$. Enlarging $C_0$ once more proves \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-cosine}.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-max-boundary}
Under \eqref{eq:gaussian-cloud}--\eqref{eq:asymptotic-regime-clean},
\begin{equation}
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X}
D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W)
\ge\delta_{\max}-o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-max-boundary-separation}
\end{equation}
In fact, on the same high-probability event, every ordered pair of every max-norm minimizer has boundary-normal distance at least $\delta_{\max}-o(1)$.
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Work on $\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}$ from Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}. Fix $W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X$ and set $v_{ij}:=w_i-w_j$. By \ref{item:app-det-H5},
\begin{equation}
\|v_{ij}\|_\infty
\le2r_{\max}^*(X)
\le\frac{a_d}{\sqrt d},
\qquad
a_d:=\sqrt{2\pi}+\varepsilon_d.
\label{eq:app-det-max-pair-cap}
\end{equation}
Averaging the constraints $(w_i-w_j)^\top x_{i,s}\ge1$ over class $i$ gives $v_{ij}^\top m_i\ge1$. Applying the reverse constraints for class $j$ gives $v_{ij}^\top m_j\le-1$. Therefore
\begin{equation}
v_{ij}^\top(m_i-m_j)\ge2.
\label{eq:app-det-max-pair-projection}
\end{equation}
By \ref{item:app-det-H2}, uniformly over $i\ne j$,
\begin{equation}
\|m_i-m_j\|_2^2
=
\|m_i\|_2^2+\|m_j\|_2^2-2m_i^\top m_j
\le2+o(1).
\label{eq:app-det-mean-pair-norm-upper}
\end{equation}
Hence
\begin{equation}
v_{ij}^\top u_{ij}^m
\ge
\frac2{\|m_i-m_j\|_2}
\ge b_d,
\qquad
b_d:=\sqrt2-o(1),
\label{eq:app-det-max-unit-projection}
\end{equation}
where the error is deterministic on $\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}$ and uniform over all pairs.

Fix $i\ne j$, and abbreviate $u=u_{ij}^m$, $v=v_{ij}$, $a=a_d$, and $b=b_d$. Since $v^\top u\ge b>0$, define
\begin{equation}
y:=\frac b{v^\top u}v.
\label{eq:app-det-max-rescaled-pair}
\end{equation}
Then $y^\top u=b$, and because $b/(v^\top u)\le1$, \eqref{eq:app-det-max-pair-cap} gives $\|y\|_\infty\le a/\sqrt d$. Thus $y$ is feasible for \eqref{eq:app-det-clipped-problem}, and
\begin{equation}
\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)
\le\|y\|_2
=
\frac{b\|v\|_2}{v^\top u}.
\label{eq:app-det-max-clipped-comparison}
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
\frac{v^\top u}{\|v\|_2}
\le
\frac b{\mathfrak m_d(u;a,b)}.
\label{eq:app-det-max-cosine-upper}
\end{equation}
By \ref{item:app-det-H6} and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-clipped-asymptotic}, the right-hand side is at most $\kappa_{\max}+o(1)$, uniformly over all ordered pairs. Since $\kappa_{\max}<1$,
\begin{equation}
\left\|
\frac{v_{ij}}{\|v_{ij}\|_2}-u_{ij}^m
\right\|_2
=
\sqrt{2-2\frac{v_{ij}^\top u_{ij}^m}{\|v_{ij}\|_2}}
\ge
\delta_{\max}-o(1).
\label{eq:app-det-max-away-from-empirical}
\end{equation}
Finally, \ref{item:app-det-H4} and the reverse triangle inequality imply
\begin{equation}
\left\|
\frac{v_{ij}}{\|v_{ij}\|_2}-u_{ij}^{\mu}
\right\|_2
\ge
\delta_{\max}-o(1),
\label{eq:app-det-max-away-from-bayes}
\end{equation}
uniformly over all pairs and all max-norm minimizers. Averaging proves \eqref{eq:app-det-max-boundary-separation}.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-gaussian-critical-count}
Let $p=p(d)$ satisfy $p/d\to1$, let $H_d\in\mathbb R^{p\times d}$ have independent $\mathcal N(0,1)$ entries, and set $A_d:=H_d/\sqrt d$ and $n_d:=\min\{p,d\}$. There are universal constants $T,c,C>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $d$ and every $2/n_d\le u\le T$, an event $\mathcal H_d(u)$ satisfies
\[
\mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal H_d(u)^c\bigr)\le C\bigl(1+\log(T/u)\bigr)e^{-cdu^2},
\]
and, on this event,
\begin{equation}
\frac1{n_d}\#\{\ell:\sigma_\ell(A_d)\le t\}\le8t,\qquad u\le t\le T.
\label{eq:app-det-gaussian-critical-count}
\end{equation}
Moreover, $A_d$ has rank $n_d$ almost surely.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Write $n:=n_d$ and take $T=1/16$. Since $n/d\to1$, for all sufficiently large $d$ we have $n/d\ge9/10$. Let $B$ be a fixed $n\times n$ coordinate submatrix of $H_d$, obtained by retaining a fixed set of $n$ rows when $p\ge d$ and a fixed set of $n$ columns when $p<d$. If $p\ge d$, then $H_d^\top H_d=B^\top B+R^\top R\succeq B^\top B$ for the matrix $R$ of deleted rows, while if $p<d$, then $H_dH_d^\top=BB^\top+RR^\top\succeq BB^\top$ for the matrix $R$ of deleted columns. Hence, by monotonicity of eigenvalues under the positive-semidefinite order,
\[
\sigma_j(H_d)\ge\sigma_j(B),\qquad 1\le j\le n.
\]

Fix $t\in[1/n,T]$ and put $\ell:=\lceil3nt\rceil$. For all sufficiently large $n$, the choice $T=1/16$ ensures $\ell<n$. Let $F$ be the $n\times(n-\ell)$ matrix obtained by retaining a fixed set of $n-\ell$ columns of $B$. Apply \citet[Corollary~5.35]{vershynin2012nonasymptotic} to $F$ with row dimension $N=n$, column dimension $n-\ell$, and deviation parameter $s:=t\sqrt n/4$. Then, except with probability at most
\[
2e^{-s^2/2}=2e^{-nt^2/32},
\]
we have
\[
\sigma_{\min}(F)\ge\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-\ell}-s=\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-\ell}-\frac{t\sqrt n}{4}.
\]
Using
\[
\sqrt n-\sqrt{n-\ell}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt n+\sqrt{n-\ell}}\ge\frac{\ell}{2\sqrt n}\ge\frac32t\sqrt n,
\]
we obtain
\[
\sigma_{\min}(F)\ge\frac54t\sqrt n>t\sqrt d,
\]
where the last inequality holds for all sufficiently large $d$ because $n/d\to1$.

Writing $B=[F\ \ R_F]$, we have $BB^\top=FF^\top+R_FR_F^\top\succeq FF^\top$. Therefore the largest $n-\ell$ eigenvalues of $BB^\top$ are at least the $n-\ell$ positive eigenvalues of $FF^\top$, and hence
\[
\sigma_j(B)>t\sqrt d,\qquad 1\le j\le n-\ell.
\]
Together with $\sigma_j(H_d)\ge\sigma_j(B)$, this gives
\[
\frac1n\#\{j:\sigma_j(A_d)\le t\}\le\frac{\ell}{n}\le3t+\frac1n\le4t.
\]

Now fix $u\in[2/n,T]$ and take the dyadic grid $t_j=2^{-j}T$ down to the first grid point lying in $[u/2,u]$. Every such grid point is at least $u/2\ge1/n$, and the number of grid points is at most $C(1+\log(T/u))$. Applying the preceding fixed-threshold estimate at every grid point and taking a union bound, the probability that any of these estimates fails is at most
\[
C\bigl(1+\log(T/u)\bigr)e^{-cdu^2},
\]
because the smallest grid point is at least $u/2$ and $n/d\to1$. On the complementary event, for every $t\in[u,T]$ choose a dyadic grid point $t_j\in[t,2t]$; monotonicity of the counting function gives
\[
\frac1n\#\{\ell:\sigma_\ell(A_d)\le t\}\le\frac1n\#\{\ell:\sigma_\ell(A_d)\le t_j\}\le4t_j\le8t.
\]
Finally, $A_d$ has rank $n$ almost surely because the rank-deficient matrices form a Lebesgue-null algebraic set.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-spectral-input}
There are deterministic \(\eta_d\downarrow0\), constants \(c,C>0\), and events \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{sp}}\) such that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\!\left((\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{sp}})^c\right)\le C\exp\!\left[-c\sqrt{d\log(2N(d)(d+1))}\right]
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-event-probability}
\end{equation}
and the following statements hold on \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{sp}}\):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(S\arabic*)]
\item \label{item:app-det-S1} \(C_m\) has rank \(r_d\), \(PQ_m=Q_m\), \(\|Q_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), and
\begin{equation}
\left|\frac{\|C_m\|_*}{k}-s_\alpha\right|\le\eta_d,\qquad \inf_{i\ne j}\|q_i-q_j\|_2\ge c_\alpha>0.
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-S1}
\end{equation}
\item \label{item:app-det-S2} Uniformly over \(i\ne j\),
\begin{equation}
\max_i\|m_i-\mu_i\|_2+\|\bar m\|_2\le\eta_d,\qquad \bar m:=\frac1k\sum_i m_i,
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-mean-inputs}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\max_i|S_m[i,i]-s_\alpha|+\max_{i\ne j}|S_m[i,j]|\le\eta_d,\qquad \max_{i\ne j,s}|(q_i-q_j)^\top e_{i,s}|\le\eta_d.
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-entry-inputs}
\end{equation}
\item \label{item:app-det-S3} The reduced polar margin
\begin{equation}
\rho_X:=\min_{i\ne j,s}(q_i-q_j)^\top x_{i,s}
\label{eq:app-det-polar-margin-definition}
\end{equation}
satisfies
\begin{equation}
|\rho_X-s_\alpha|\le C\eta_d,\qquad \rho_X>0.
\label{eq:app-det-polar-feasible-margin}
\end{equation}
\item \label{item:app-det-S4} The reduced polar geometry satisfies
\begin{equation}
\left|D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(Q_m)-\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)\right|\le\eta_d.
\label{eq:app-det-polar-uniform-gap}
\end{equation}
\item \label{item:app-det-S5} If \(\alpha\ne1\), all positive singular values of \(C_m\) lie in a deterministic compact interval bounded away from zero:
\begin{equation}
c_\alpha\le\sigma_{r_d}(C_m)\le\sigma_1(C_m)\le C_\alpha.
\label{eq:app-det-C0-extreme-singular-values}
\end{equation}
If \(\alpha=1\), there are \(t_0,C_0>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
\frac1{r_d}\#\{\ell:\sigma_\ell(C_m)\le t\}\le C_0(t+\eta_d),\qquad \eta_d\le t\le t_0.
\label{eq:app-det-critical-hard-count}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
Because \(m_i=\mu_i+r\bar z_i\) is Gaussian with covariance \((1+r^2/n_i)I_d/d\), the rows are independent and admit the exact representation
\begin{equation}
M_m=D_dG/\sqrt d,\qquad D_d:=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\sqrt{1+r^2/n_1},\ldots,\sqrt{1+r^2/n_k}\right),
\label{eq:app-det-gaussian-mean-matrix}
\end{equation}
where \(G\) has independent standard Gaussian entries.
Since \(\|D_d-I_k\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Cr_0^2/n_{\min}=o(1)\) and \(\|G/\sqrt d\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(1)\) with exponentially high probability, the comparator \(C_0:=PG/\sqrt d\) obeys
\begin{equation}
\|C_m-C_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\zeta_d,\qquad \zeta_d\downarrow0.
\label{eq:app-det-Weyl-transfer}
\end{equation}
After a fixed orthogonal change of basis on \(\mathbb R^k\), the positive singular values of \(C_0\) have the same law as those of a \((k-1)\times d\) standard Gaussian matrix divided by \(\sqrt d\).
Marchenko--Pastur convergence therefore gives \(\|C_0\|_*/k\to s_\alpha\).
The normalized nuclear norm is \(O(d^{-1})\)-Lipschitz in the Gaussian entries, so Gaussian concentration and the deterministic expectation bias place this convergence under a deterministic envelope with failure probability bounded as in \eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-event-probability}.
