The rank assertion is almost sure, and Weyl's inequality yields \eqref{eq:app-det-C0-extreme-singular-values} when \(\alpha\ne1\).

At $\alpha=1$, put $L_d:=\log(2N(d)(d+1))$ and $u_d:=(L_d/d)^{1/4}$. Then $u_d\to0$, $u_d\ge2/r_d$ eventually, and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-gaussian-critical-count} gives failure at most $C\exp(-c\sqrt{dL_d})$ after absorbing its logarithmic prefactor. Weyl's inequality and \eqref{eq:app-det-Weyl-transfer} transfer the count from $C_0$ to $C_m$ by replacing $t$ with $t+\zeta_d$. Enlarge the common envelope so that $\eta_d\ge\max\{u_d,\zeta_d\}$ and take $t_0<T/2$; then \eqref{eq:app-det-critical-hard-count} follows with precisely the probability scale in \eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-event-probability}.


Let \(S_0:=(C_0C_0^\top)^{1/2}\).
Conditionally on its singular values, the left singular frame of \(C_0\) is Haar in \(\mathbf{1}^\perp\) and independent of those singular values.
Haar concentration for the quadratic forms defining \(S_0[i,j]\), followed by a union bound over \(k^2\) entries, gives
\begin{equation}
\max_i\left|S_0[i,i]-\frac{\|C_0\|_*}{k}\right|+\max_{i\ne j}|S_0[i,j]|\le\chi_d,\qquad \chi_d\downarrow0.
\label{eq:app-det-S0-entry-concentration}
\end{equation}
The gap-free square-root inequality for positive semidefinite matrices gives
\begin{equation}
\|S_m-S_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|C_mC_m^\top-C_0C_0^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{1/2}\le C\zeta_d^{1/2}.
\label{eq:app-det-gap-free-square-root}
\end{equation}
This proves the entrywise bounds in (S2) without dividing by the smallest singular value.
The empirical-mean bound is part of Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}, and the Gaussian average \(k^{-1}\sum_i m_i\) gives \(\|\bar m\|_2=o(1)\) under the same probability envelope.

Conditionally on the empirical means, \(Q_m\) is deterministic and the residuals are centered Gaussian.
Since \(\|q_i-q_j\|_2\le\sqrt2\), Gaussian tails and a union bound over at most \(N^2\) indices give the residual bound in (S2).
Using that row \(i\) of \(C_m\) is \((m_i-\bar m)^\top\), we obtain
\begin{equation}
(q_i-q_j)^\top m_i=S_m[i,i]-S_m[j,i]+(q_i-q_j)^\top\bar m=s_\alpha+O(\eta_d).
\label{eq:app-det-polar-class-margin}
\end{equation}
Adding the residual bound proves (S3).
The same identity and \(\max_{i,s}\|x_{i,s}\|_2=O(1)\) give the uniform lower bound on \(\|q_i-q_j\|_2\).

It remains to identify the angular constant.
The centering identities \(\mathbf{1}^\top Q_m={\mathbf 0}\) and \(\|Q_m\|_{\mathrm F}^2=r_d\) give
\begin{equation}
\frac1{k(k-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\|q_i-q_j\|_2^2=\frac{2r_d}{k-1}\longrightarrow\frac{2\rho_\alpha}{\alpha}.
\label{eq:app-det-polar-pair-average}
\end{equation}

If \(\alpha<1\), then \(r_d=k-1\) and \(Q_mQ_m^\top=P\), so every pair norm is exactly \(\sqrt2\). For \(\alpha>1\), let \(Q_0\) be the reduced polar factor of \(C_0\) and put \(\Pi_m:=Q_mQ_m^\top\) and \(\Pi_0:=Q_0Q_0^\top\). The left singular frame of \(C_0\), but not in general that of \(C_m=PD_dG/\sqrt d\), is Haar in \(\mathbf{1}^\perp\) when the class counts differ. The positive singular-value lower bounds and \eqref{eq:app-det-Weyl-transfer} give
\[
\|(I-\Pi_0)\Pi_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|C_m-C_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|C_m^\dagger\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_\alpha\zeta_d,
\]
and the analogous estimate with \(0\) and \(m\) exchanged. Consequently, \(\|\Pi_m-\Pi_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C_\alpha\zeta_d\). Haar-projector concentration applies to \(\Pi_0\) and yields \((e_i-e_j)^\top\Pi_0(e_i-e_j)=2/\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly over pairs on the same probability scale. Since each such quadratic form changes by at most \(2\|\Pi_m-\Pi_0\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), we obtain \(\|q_i-q_j\|_2=\sqrt{2/\alpha}+o(1)\) uniformly. At \(\alpha=1\), no perturbation of the polar factor at the hard edge is needed for this step. The deterministic bounds \(\|q_i-q_j\|_2\le\sqrt2\) and \eqref{eq:app-det-polar-pair-average} give
\[
\frac1{k(k-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\left|\|q_i-q_j\|_2-\sqrt2\right|
\le\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(2-\frac{2r_d}{k-1}\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the required pair-norm convergence holds in averaged \(L^1\) at \(\alpha=1\).

Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
(q_i-q_j)^\top(\mu_i-\mu_j)=S_m[i,i]+S_m[j,j]-S_m[i,j]-S_m[j,i]+o(1)=2s_\alpha+o(1),
\label{eq:app-det-polar-cross-inner}
\end{equation}
while \(\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2=\sqrt2+o(1)\) uniformly.
Consequently, the pairwise cosine converges in averaged \(L^1\) to
\begin{equation}
\frac{2s_\alpha}{\sqrt{2\rho_\alpha/\alpha}\sqrt2}=\frac{m_{1/2}(\alpha)}{\sqrt{\rho_\alpha}}=\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha).
\label{eq:app-det-polar-cosine}
\end{equation}
Uniform continuity of \(x\mapsto\sqrt{2-2x}\) on \([-1,1]\) proves (S4).
Collecting the deterministic envelopes proves the proposition.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-trace-truncation}
Let \(C=U\Sigma V^\top\) have rank \(r\), let \(Q=UV^\top\), and let \(B\) satisfy \(\|B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(B)\le r\).
Put \(g_\ell:=u_\ell^\top Bv_\ell\) and \(a_\ell:=1-g_\ell\in[0,2]\).
Then
\begin{align}
\|B-Q\|_{\mathrm F}^2&\le2\sum_{\ell=1}^r a_\ell,
\label{eq:app-det-Frob-vs-trace}\\
\frac1r\sum_{\ell=1}^r a_\ell&\le2\frac{\#\{\ell:\sigma_\ell\le\tau\}}r+\frac1{\tau r}\sum_{\ell=1}^r\sigma_\ell a_\ell,\qquad \tau>0.
\label{eq:app-det-truncation}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
The rank and operator-norm bounds give \(\|B\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le r\), so expanding \(\|B-Q\|_{\mathrm F}^2\) proves the first inequality.
For the second inequality, use \(a_\ell\le2\) when \(\sigma_\ell\le\tau\) and \(a_\ell\le\sigma_\ell a_\ell/\tau\) otherwise.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-average-normalization}
Let \(B,Q\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) have rows \(b_i,q_i\), suppose \(b_i-b_j\ne{\mathbf 0}\) for \(i\ne j\), and assume \(\inf_{i\ne j}\|q_i-q_j\|_2\ge c_0>0\).
If
\begin{equation}
E_2:=\frac1{k(k-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\|(b_i-b_j)-(q_i-q_j)\|_2^2,
\label{eq:app-det-average-normalization-error}
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
\frac1{k(k-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\left\|\frac{b_i-b_j}{\|b_i-b_j\|_2}-\frac{q_i-q_j}{\|q_i-q_j\|_2}\right\|_2\le\frac4{c_0}E_2^{1/2}+\frac8{c_0^2}E_2.
\label{eq:app-det-average-normalization-bound}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
For a pairwise difference error \(e_{ij}\le c_0/2\), the normalization map gives an error at most \(4e_{ij}/c_0\).
For the remaining pairs, use the trivial bound two and \(\mathbf1_{\{e_{ij}>c_0/2\}}\le4e_{ij}^2/c_0^2\), then average and apply Cauchy--Schwarz.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-spectral-rigidity}
On the events of Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input}, let \(W\in\mathcal F_X\) satisfy
\begin{equation}
\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le(1+\xi)r_{\mathrm{sp}}^*(X),\qquad 0\le\xi\le1.
\label{eq:app-det-near-spectral-assumption}
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W)\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)-\begin{cases}C_\alpha(\eta_d+\xi)^{1/2},&\alpha\ne1,\\ C(\eta_d+\xi)^{1/4},&\alpha=1.\end{cases}
\label{eq:app-det-near-spectral-bound}
\end{equation}
In particular, every exact minimizer satisfies
\begin{equation}
\frac1{r_d}\left\|\frac{PW}{\|PW\|_{\mathrm{op}}}-Q_m\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le\begin{cases}C_\alpha\eta_d,&\alpha\ne1,\\ C\sqrt{\eta_d},&\alpha=1,\end{cases}
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-frobenius-rigidity}
\end{equation}
uniformly over \(W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X\).
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
The polar witness \(Q_m/\rho_X\) is feasible, so
\begin{equation}
r_{\mathrm{sp}}^*(X)\le\rho_X^{-1}.
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-optimum-upper}
\end{equation}
For every feasible \(W\), summing the class-averaged constraints over ordered pairs gives
\begin{equation}
\langle PW,C_m\rangle\ge k-1.
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-dual-lower}
\end{equation}
Set \(A:=PW\), \(a:=\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}>0\), and \(B:=A/a\).
Centering is an operator-norm contraction and preserves all row differences, while \(\operatorname{rank}(B)\le r_d\).
Equations \eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-optimum-upper}, \eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-dual-lower}, and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input} give
\begin{equation}
\frac1{r_d}\sum_{\ell=1}^{r_d}\sigma_\ell(C_m)\left(1-u_\ell^\top Bv_\ell\right)\le C(\eta_d+\xi).
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-polar-inner-product}
\end{equation}
If \(\alpha\ne1\), the positive edge in \eqref{eq:app-det-C0-extreme-singular-values} and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-trace-truncation} yield \(r_d^{-1}\|B-Q_m\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le C_\alpha(\eta_d+\xi)\).
If \(\alpha=1\), set \(q:=\eta_d+\xi\) and use \(\tau=\sqrt q\) in \eqref{eq:app-det-truncation} together with \eqref{eq:app-det-critical-hard-count}; the result is
\begin{equation}
\frac1{r_d}\|B-Q_m\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le Cq^{1/2}.
\label{eq:app-det-critical-spectral-frobenius}
\end{equation}
The case of non-small \(q\) follows by increasing \(C\) and using the trivial bound.
Taking \(\xi=0\) proves \eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-frobenius-rigidity}.

Because both \(B\) and \(Q_m\) are centered,
\begin{equation}
\frac1{k(k-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\|(b_i-b_j)-(q_i-q_j)\|_2^2=\frac{2}{k-1}\|B-Q_m\|_{\mathrm F}^2.
\label{eq:app-det-pairwise-Frobenius}
\end{equation}
Feasibility ensures \(b_i-b_j\ne{\mathbf 0}\), and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input} supplies a uniform lower bound on the polar pair norms.
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-average-normalization}, followed by the reverse triangle inequality and \eqref{eq:app-det-polar-uniform-gap}, proves \eqref{eq:app-det-near-spectral-bound}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- proposition-17: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-spectral-boundary}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud} and~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime},
\begin{equation}
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W)\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)-o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-boundary-separation}
\end{equation}
The bound holds on the events in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input} with the deterministic error in \eqref{eq:app-det-near-spectral-bound} at \(\xi=0\).
<!-- end proposition-17 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-rigidity} with \(\xi=0\) and take the infimum over the exact minimizer set.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- head-3: body_md -->
\label{app:det-main-proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-separation-clean}]
Let \(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) be the intersection of \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) from Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event} and \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{sp}}\) from Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input}.
Both complements satisfy a bound of the form
\begin{equation}
C\exp\!\left[-c\sqrt{d\log(2N(d)(d+1))}\right].
\label{eq:app-det-intersection-tail}
\end{equation}
Since \(\log(2N(d)(d+1))\to\infty\), the quantity in \eqref{eq:app-det-intersection-tail} is at most \(e^{-\sqrt d}\) for every sufficiently large \(d\), after increasing the deterministic threshold.
The sign construction in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event} gives \(\mathcal F_X\ne\varnothing\) on this event, and compactness gives nonempty minimum-norm sets.

The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-boundary} is deterministic on \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) and gives the maximum-pair statement \eqref{eq:det-row-uniform-clean} under a deterministic vanishing envelope.
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-ray-reduction} then gives \eqref{eq:det-row-clean}.
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-max-boundary} and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-ray-reduction} give \eqref{eq:det-max-clean}.
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-boundary} gives \eqref{eq:det-sp-clean} for every fixed \(\alpha>0\), using the reduced polar factor when \(\alpha<1\) and the hard-edge truncation when \(\alpha=1\).
Choose one deterministic \(\omega_d\downarrow0\) dominating all three errors.
Because \(\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)>0\) and \(\delta_{\max}>0\), \eqref{eq:det-set-order-clean} follows for every sufficiently large \(d\).
\end{proof}
<!-- end head-3 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
Let \(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) be the intersection of \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) from Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event} and \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{sp}}\) from Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input}.
Both complements satisfy a bound of the form
\begin{equation}
C\exp\!\left[-c\sqrt{d\log(2N(d)(d+1))}\right].
\label{eq:app-det-intersection-tail}
\end{equation}
Since \(\log(2N(d)(d+1))\to\infty\), the quantity in \eqref{eq:app-det-intersection-tail} is at most \(e^{-\sqrt d}\) for every sufficiently large \(d\), after increasing the deterministic threshold.
The sign construction in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event} gives \(\mathcal F_X\ne\varnothing\) on this event, and compactness gives nonempty minimum-norm sets.

The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-boundary} is deterministic on \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) and gives the maximum-pair statement \eqref{eq:det-row-uniform-clean} under a deterministic vanishing envelope.
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-ray-reduction} then gives \eqref{eq:det-row-clean}.
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-max-boundary} and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-ray-reduction} give \eqref{eq:det-max-clean}.
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-boundary} gives \eqref{eq:det-sp-clean} for every fixed \(\alpha>0\), using the reduced polar factor when \(\alpha<1\) and the hard-edge truncation when \(\alpha=1\).
Choose one deterministic \(\omega_d\downarrow0\) dominating all three errors.
Because \(\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)>0\) and \(\delta_{\max}>0\), \eqref{eq:det-set-order-clean} follows for every sufficiently large \(d\).
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-acc-pairwise-gaussian}
For every \(i<j\), let \(e_{ij}(W):=\{p_{i\to j}(W)+p_{j\to i}(W)\}/2\). Then
\begin{equation}
\max_{i<j}\{\pi_{i,d}p_{i\to j}(W)+\pi_{j,d}p_{j\to i}(W)\}\le\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)\le\sum_{i<j}\{\pi_{i,d}p_{i\to j}(W)+\pi_{j,d}p_{j\to i}(W)\},
\label{eq:app-acc-weighted-sandwich}
\end{equation}
and hence \(\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)\ge2\pi_{\min,d}\max_{i<j}e_{ij}(W)\). Moreover, with \(c_{ij}(W):=1-d_{ij}(W)^2/2\),
\begin{equation}
e_{ij}(W)=\frac12\left[\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{s_{ij}c_{ij}(W)/2+\langle u_{ij}^W,m_{ij}\rangle}{\sigma_d}\right)+\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{s_{ij}c_{ij}(W)/2-\langle u_{ij}^W,m_{ij}\rangle}{\sigma_d}\right)\right]\ge\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{s_{ij}(c_{ij}(W))_+}{2\sigma_d}\right),
\label{eq:app-acc-pairwise-midpoint-free}
\end{equation}
where \(\overline\Phi(a)=\mathbb P(Z\ge a)\) for \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\).
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
Conditionally on \(Y=i\), the multiclass error event is the union of the events \(\{w_j^\top X^{\mathrm{te}}\ge w_i^\top X^{\mathrm{te}}\}\), up to Gaussian-null ties. The union bound gives the upper half of \eqref{eq:app-acc-weighted-sandwich}, while any fixed unordered pair gives the lower half. For \(u=u_{ij}^W\), \(v=u_{ij}^{\mu}\), \(m=m_{ij}\), and \(s=s_{ij}\), the identities \(\mu_i=m+(s/2)v\) and \(\mu_j=m-(s/2)v\) give
\[
p_{i\to j}(W)=\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{u^\top\mu_i}{\sigma_d}\right),\qquad p_{j\to i}(W)=\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{-u^\top\mu_j}{\sigma_d}\right),
\]
which proves the equality in \eqref{eq:app-acc-pairwise-midpoint-free}. For \(q\ge0\), the even function \(z\mapsto[\overline\Phi(q+z)+\overline\Phi(q-z)]/2\) is minimized at zero, while for \(q<0\) the same average is at least \(1/2\). Since \(u^\top v=1-d_{ij}(W)^2/2\), the final inequality follows.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-acc-gaussian-radial-event}
There are deterministic \(\eta_d\downarrow0\) and events \(\mathcal R_d\), depending only on the class means, such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\mathcal R_d^c)\le\frac14e^{-\sqrt d},\qquad \tau_d+\rho_d\le\eta_d\quad\text{on }\mathcal R_d.
\label{eq:app-acc-radial-event-probability}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Under the normalized convention, \(d\|\mu_i\|_2^2\) is chi-square with \(d\) degrees of freedom, while conditionally on \(\mu_i\), the inner product \(\mu_i^\top\mu_j\) is Gaussian with variance \(\|\mu_i\|_2^2/d\). Taking a sufficiently large constant \(C_\alpha\) and \(\eta_d=C_\alpha d^{-1/4}\), standard chi-square and Gaussian tails followed by a union bound over \(O(d^2)\) indices give \eqref{eq:app-acc-radial-event-probability}.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- proposition-18: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-acc-finite-bounds}
If \(A_d>0\), then
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)\le(k-1)\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{A_d}{\sigma_d}\right),\qquad \inf_{W\in\mathcal C_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)\ge2\pi_{\min,d}\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{B_d}{\sigma_d}\right).
\label{eq:app-acc-finite-bounds}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-18 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
For \(v=u_{ij}^{\mu}\), radial control gives
\[
v^\top\mu_i\ge\frac{1-\tau_d-\rho_d}{\sqrt{2(1+\tau_d+\rho_d)}},\qquad -v^\top\mu_j\ge\frac{1-\tau_d-\rho_d}{\sqrt{2(1+\tau_d+\rho_d)}}.
\]
If \(W\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}\), then \(\|u_{ij}^W-v\|_2\le h_d\), so both directed population margins are at least \(A_d\). The upper bound follows from the union bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-pairwise-gaussian}. If \(W\in\mathcal C_d^{\mathrm{clf}}\), some pair has \(d_{ij}(W)\ge\Delta_d\), while \(s_{ij}/2\le\sqrt{(1+\tau_d+\rho_d)/2}\). The midpoint-free lower bound in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-pairwise-gaussian} then gives the second inequality.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thm:app-acc-transfer}
Suppose \(\tau_d+\rho_d\to0\), \(\limsup_d h_d\le\overline h\), and \(\liminf_d\Delta_d\ge\underline\delta>0\). If \(\mathsf a(\overline h)>\mathsf b(\underline\delta)\), then under Assumption~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime},
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sup_{W\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)}{\inf_{W\in\mathcal C_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)}\longrightarrow0,
\label{eq:app-acc-transfer-ratio}
\end{equation}
and therefore, for every sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{equation}
\inf_{W\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W)>\sup_{W\in\mathcal C_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W).
\label{eq:app-acc-transfer-order}
\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
Choose constants \(0<b<a\) such that \(\mathsf b(\underline\delta)<b<a<\mathsf a(\overline h)\). Proposition~\ref{prop:app-acc-finite-bounds} gives, for all sufficiently large \(d\),
\[
\frac{\sup_{\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}}{\inf_{\mathcal C_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}}\le\frac{k-1}{2\pi_{\min,d}}\frac{\overline\Phi(a/\sigma_d)}{\overline\Phi(b/\sigma_d)}.
\]
The standard Mills bounds imply that the right-hand side is at most \(Ck\pi_{\min,d}^{-1}e^{-cd}\) for constants \(C,c>0\), because \(r_{\mathrm{te}}\le r_{\mathrm{te},0}\). Assumption~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime} makes this quantity vanish.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity}
Fix \(d\), a linearly separable training set \(X\) containing at least one sample from every class in \([k]\), a matrix norm \(\psi\), and \(0\le\varepsilon<\gamma_\psi(X)\). If \(d_{\cos}(W_t,\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X)\to0\), then
\begin{equation}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t)\le\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U),\qquad \liminf_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t)\ge\inf_{U\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U).
\label{eq:app-acc-error-continuity}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
The norm-normalized section of \(\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X\) is compact, and its strictly positive empirical margin keeps every pairwise row difference uniformly away from zero. Population error is invariant under positive scaling and continuous on this section because the Gaussian test law gives zero mass to score-tie hyperplanes. Uniform continuity on a compact neighborhood proves the claim.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- lemma-19: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-metric-transfer}
Under the fixed-data assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity}, if \(d_{\cos}(W_t,\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X)\to0\) with \(0\le\varepsilon<\gamma_\psi(X)\), then
\begin{equation}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W_t)\le\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U),\qquad \liminf_{t\to\infty}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W_t)\ge\inf_{U\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(U).
\label{eq:app-det-metric-transfer}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-19 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
The same compactness argument as in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity} applies because \(D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}\) is scale invariant and continuous whenever all pairwise row differences are nonzero.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
Work on the event \(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}}\) from Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-separation-clean}. Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}, items~\ref{item:app-det-H1}--\ref{item:app-det-H2} imply \(\tau_d+\rho_d=o(1)\) on this event. Take \(\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}=\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X\). Equation~\eqref{eq:det-row-uniform-clean} gives \(h_d=o(1)\). For \(\psi\in\{\mathrm{sp},\max\}\), take \(\mathcal C_d^{\mathrm{clf}}=\mathcal U_\psi^X\). Equations~\eqref{eq:det-sp-clean} and~\eqref{eq:det-max-clean} give \(\liminf_d\Delta_d\ge\delta_\psi>0\), where \(\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}=\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)\) and \(\delta_{\max}\) is defined in \eqref{eq:delta-max-clean}. Since
\begin{equation}
\mathsf a(0)=\frac1{\sqrt2}>\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(1-\frac{\delta_\psi^2}{2}\right)_+=\mathsf b(\delta_\psi),
\label{eq:app-acc-deterministic-amplitude-gap}
\end{equation}
Theorem~\ref{thm:app-acc-transfer} gives, for every sufficiently large \(d\) on \(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}}\),
\begin{equation}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)<\min_{\psi\in\{\mathrm{sp},\max\}}\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_\psi^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V).
\label{eq:app-acc-deterministic-set-error-order}
\end{equation}
The full-batch implicit-bias results in Appendix~\ref{app:max-sum-row}, together with Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-margin-direction-convergence}, give direction-set convergence to \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X\) for RowGD and RowGDM, to \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X\) for Spectral-GD and exact-SVD Muon, and to \(\mathcal U_{\max}^X\) for SignGD, Signum, and full-batch Adam under the stated Adam assumptions. Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity} transfers \eqref{eq:app-acc-deterministic-set-error-order} to all seven trajectories. Since \(\mathbb P(\mathcal G_d^{\mathrm{det}})\ge1-e^{-\sqrt d}\), replacing error by one minus accuracy proves \eqref{eq:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean} with the claimed probability.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- lemma-20: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-population-polar-transfer}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud} and~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime},
\begin{equation}
\frac1{r_d}\|Q_m-Q_\mu\|_{\mathrm F}^2\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0.
\label{eq:app-population-polar-transfer}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-20 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
By~\eqref{eq:app-det-mean-residual}, the \(i\)-th row of \(M_m-M_\mu\) is \(r\bar z_i^\top\), and the rows are independent centered Gaussian vectors with covariance \(r^2I_d/(n_i d)\). Hence \(M_m-M_\mu=D_d^{\mathrm e}H/\sqrt d\) for a standard Gaussian matrix \(H\) and a diagonal matrix satisfying \(\|D_d^{\mathrm e}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le r_0/\sqrt{n_{\min}}\). Since \(k/d\to\alpha\) and \(n_{\min}\to\infty\),
\begin{equation}
\delta_d:=\|C_m-C_\mu\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|M_m-M_\mu\|_{\mathrm{op}}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-population-polar-op-transfer}
\end{equation}

On the full reduced-rank event, \(\|Q_\mu\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\), \(\operatorname{rank}(Q_\mu)=r_d\), and \(\langle Q_\mu,C_\mu\rangle=\|C_\mu\|_*\). Therefore
\begin{align}
0
&\le \|C_m\|_*-\langle Q_\mu,C_m\rangle \notag\\
&\le \bigl|\|C_m\|_*-\|C_\mu\|_*\bigr|+\bigl|\langle Q_\mu,C_m-C_\mu\rangle\bigr|
\le 2r_d\delta_d.
\label{eq:app-population-polar-deficit}
\end{align}
Write \(C_m=U_m\Sigma_mV_m^\top\), and set \(a_\ell:=1-u_{m,\ell}^\top Q_\mu v_{m,\ell}\). Then~\eqref{eq:app-population-polar-deficit} gives
\begin{equation}
\frac1{r_d}\sum_{\ell=1}^{r_d}\sigma_\ell(C_m)a_\ell\le2\delta_d.
\label{eq:app-population-polar-weighted-deficit}
\end{equation}

If \(\alpha\neq1\), Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input}, item~\ref{item:app-det-S5}, bounds every positive singular value of \(C_m\) away from zero, so Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-trace-truncation} and~\eqref{eq:app-population-polar-weighted-deficit} yield \(r_d^{-1}\|Q_m-Q_\mu\|_{\mathrm F}^2=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).

Suppose \(\alpha=1\). Choose a deterministic sequence \(\bar\delta_d\downarrow0\) such that \(\delta_d\le\bar\delta_d\) with probability tending to one, and set \(\tau_d:=\max\{\eta_d,\sqrt{\bar\delta_d}\}\), where \(\eta_d\) is the envelope in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input}. For all sufficiently large \(d\), \(\tau_d\le t_0\), and item~\ref{item:app-det-S5} together with Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-trace-truncation} gives
\[
\frac1{r_d}\|Q_m-Q_\mu\|_{\mathrm F}^2
\le 4C_0(\tau_d+\eta_d)+\frac{4\delta_d}{\tau_d}
=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
This proves~\eqref{eq:app-population-polar-transfer}.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
We first establish the claimed geometry uniformly over the corresponding exact maximum-margin faces.

For the Row geometry, Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-rigidity} and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}, item~\ref{item:app-det-H1}, give
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^X}\max_i\|w_i-\mu_i\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-row-population-rigidity}
\end{equation}
Since \(\min_i\|\mu_i\|_2=1-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-normalization} yields
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^X}\max_i\|\widehat w_i-\widehat\mu_i\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-row-direction}
\end{equation}

For the Max geometry, put \(g:=\sqrt{2/\pi}\), let \(T_i:=\operatorname{sign}(\mu_i)\), and write \(t_{\max}:=r_{\max}^*(X)\). For \(W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X\), set \(A:=W/t_{\max}\). The sharp radius estimate~\eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-radii} and the global sign rigidity~\eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-global-sign} imply
\begin{equation}
t_{\max}=\frac{1+o_{\mathbb P}(1)}{g\sqrt d},\qquad
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X}\frac{\|A-T\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{kd}=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\label{eq:app-limiting-max-global}
\end{equation}
where \(T\) has rows \(T_i^\top\). Let \(\bar A:=k^{-1}\sum_iA_i\) and \(\bar T:=k^{-1}\sum_iT_i\). Jensen's inequality,~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-max-global}, and \(\mathbb E\|\bar T\|_2^2=d/k=O(1)\) give \(\sup_W\|\bar A\|_2/\sqrt d=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). The class-averaged feasibility constraint~\eqref{eq:app-det-row-centering-constraint} then gives, uniformly over \(i\) and \(W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X\),
\[
A_i^\top\mu_i\ge g\sqrt d-o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt d).
\]
Together with \(\max_i|\|\mu_i\|_1/\sqrt d-g|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) from~\eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-gaussian-inputs}, this implies \(D_i:=\|\mu_i\|_1-A_i^\top\mu_i=o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt d)\) uniformly. Substituting this bound into~\eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-row-split} and using the uniform Gaussian small-ball estimate~\eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-small-ball} yields
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X}\max_i\frac1d\|A_i-T_i\|_2^2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-max-row-rigidity}
\end{equation}
Since \(\|T_i\|_2=\sqrt d\), normalization stability gives
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X}\max_i\left\|\widehat w_i-\frac{\operatorname{sign}(\mu_i)}{\sqrt d}\right\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-max-direction}
\end{equation}

For the Spectral geometry, let \(B:=PW/\|PW\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). Combining~\eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-frobenius-rigidity} with Lemma~\ref{lem:app-population-polar-transfer} gives
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\frac1{r_d}\|B-Q_\mu\|_{\mathrm F}^2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-spectral-population-rigidity}
\end{equation}
This proves the population-mean version of the spectral geometry claimed in the proposition.

It remains to identify the mean angles when \(\alpha>1\). For Row,~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-row-direction} immediately gives a limiting angle of zero. For Max,~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-max-direction}, \(\max_i|\|\mu_i\|_2-1|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and~\eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-gaussian-inputs} give
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X}\max_i\left|
\frac{w_i^\top\mu_i}{\|w_i\|_2\|\mu_i\|_2}
-\sqrt{\frac2\pi}
\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-max-angle-cosine}
\end{equation}

For Spectral, \(\alpha>1\) implies \(r_d=d\). Since \(C_\mu\) is a centered Gaussian matrix, the left singular frame \(U_\mu\) is Haar in \(\mathbf1^\perp\) and independent of its singular values. Haar-projector concentration and the Marchenko--Pastur limit therefore give
\begin{equation}
\max_i\left|\|q_i\|_2^2-\frac1\alpha\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\qquad
\max_i\left|q_i^\top\mu_i-s_\alpha\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-population-polar-row}
\end{equation}
Indeed, if \(S_\mu:=Q_\mu C_\mu^\top=U_\mu\Sigma_\mu U_\mu^\top\), conditional Haar concentration gives \(\max_i|S_\mu[i,i]-\|C_\mu\|_*/k|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), while \(\|C_\mu\|_*/k\to s_\alpha\) and \(q_i^\top(\mu_i-\bar\mu)=S_\mu[i,i]\) with \(\|\bar\mu\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Since \(s_\alpha=m_{1/2}(\alpha)/\sqrt\alpha\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)=m_{1/2}(\alpha)\) for \(\alpha>1\),~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-population-polar-row} yields
\begin{equation}
\max_i\left|
\frac{q_i^\top\mu_i}{\|q_i\|_2\|\mu_i\|_2}
-\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)
\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-population-polar-cosine}
\end{equation}

We now transfer~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-population-polar-cosine} from \(Q_\mu\) to arbitrary exact Spectral minimizers. Fix \(W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X\), set \(a:=\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), and let \(\bar w:=k^{-1}\sum_iw_i\) and \(h:=\bar w/a\). Centering preserves every margin and cannot increase the operator norm, so exact optimality gives \(\|PW\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}=a\). Hence, with \(B:=PW/a\),
\begin{equation}
\frac Wa=B+\mathbf1h^\top,\qquad \mathbf1^\top B={\mathbf 0}^\top.
\label{eq:app-limiting-spectral-shift}
\end{equation}
Because \(\|Q_\mu\|_{\mathrm F}^2=d\),~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-spectral-population-rigidity} gives \(\|B\|_{\mathrm F}^2=d-o_{\mathbb P}(d)\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X\). The two terms in~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-spectral-shift} are Frobenius-orthogonal, while \(\|W/a\|_{\mathrm{op}}=1\) implies \(\|W/a\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le d\). Therefore
\[
d\ge\left\|\frac Wa\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2=\|B\|_{\mathrm F}^2+k\|h\|_2^2,
\]
and hence
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\|h\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-spectral-shift-small}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\frac1k\sum_{i=1}^k\left\|\frac{w_i}{a}-q_i\right\|_2^2
=
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\left\{\frac1k\|B-Q_\mu\|_{\mathrm F}^2+\|h\|_2^2\right\}
=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-limiting-spectral-row-average}
\end{equation}
Moreover, every spectral row is nonzero with probability tending to one: if \(w_i={\mathbf 0}\), then~\eqref{eq:app-det-row-centering-constraint} gives \(-ah^\top m_i\ge1-1/k\), contradicting \(a=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\),~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-spectral-shift-small}, and \(\max_i\|m_i\|_2=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Since~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-population-polar-row} bounds \(\min_i\|q_i\|_2\) away from zero,~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-spectral-row-average} and normalization stability imply that, for every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\),
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\frac1k\#\left\{i:
\left|
\arccos\!\left(\frac{w_i^\top\mu_i}{\|w_i\|_2\|\mu_i\|_2}\right)
-\arccos\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)
\right|>\varepsilon
\right\}
\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0.
\label{eq:app-limiting-spectral-angle-fraction}
\end{equation}
Because every angle lies in \([0,\pi]\),~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-spectral-angle-fraction} implies
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\left|
\frac1k\sum_{i=1}^k
\arccos\!\left(\frac{w_i^\top\mu_i}{\|w_i\|_2\|\mu_i\|_2}\right)
-\arccos\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)
\right|
\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}0.
\label{eq:app-limiting-spectral-mean-angle}
\end{equation}

Finally,~\eqref{eq:minmax-equivalence-clean} identifies each maximum-margin direction set with the positive rays through the corresponding exact minimum-norm face. The full-batch implicit-bias results used in Theorem~\ref{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}, together with Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-margin-direction-convergence}, give direction-set convergence to \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X\) for RowGD and RowGDM, to \(\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X\) for SpecGD and Muon, and to \(\mathcal U_{\max}^X\) for SignGD, Signum, and Adam. At each fixed \(d\), the normalized row directions, the centered spectral representative \(PW/\|PW\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), and the mean class--row angle are continuous on the corresponding compact direction sets on the high-probability events established above. Taking \(t\to\infty\) first and then \(d\to\infty\) therefore transfers~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-row-direction},~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-max-direction},~\eqref{eq:app-limiting-spectral-population-rigidity}, and the three angle limits to the optimizer trajectories, proving Proposition~\ref{prop:limiting-geometry}.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-21: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-det-exponent-reduction}
For every classifier with nonzero pairwise row differences, set \(I_d(W):=d\mathsf E_d(W)/(2r_{\mathrm{te}}^2)\) and \(C_0:=3/2+\frac12\log(2\pi)\). Then
\begin{equation}
\max\{0,I_d(W)-\log(k-1)\}\le-\log\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)\le I_d(W)+\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})+\log(1+\sqrt{2I_d(W)})+C_0.
\label{eq:app-det-exponent-reduction}
\end{equation}
Consequently, uniformly over any classifier family on which \(\mathsf E_d(W)=O(1)\), one has \(\mathsf F_d(W)=\mathsf E_d(W)+o(1)\) under Assumption~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}.
<!-- end lemma-21 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
For a directed pair, the exact error is \(\overline\Phi(\sqrt d\,(u_{ij}^W)^\top\mu_i/r_{\mathrm{te}})\). Let \(t=\sqrt{2I_d(W)}\). The Gaussian tail bounds
\[
\frac{e^{-C_0}}{1+t}e^{-t^2/2}\le\overline\Phi(t)\le\frac12e^{-t^2/2}
\]
show that one directed pair contributes at least \(\pi_{\min,d}e^{-C_0-I_d(W)}/(1+\sqrt{2I_d(W)})\) to the multiclass error, while a classwise union bound gives \(\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W)\le(k-1)e^{-I_d(W)}\) when all directed population margins are nonnegative; if one is negative then \(I_d(W)=0\), and the same logarithmic lower bound is trivial. This proves \eqref{eq:app-det-exponent-reduction}. Multiplying by \(2r_{\mathrm{te}}^2/d\) and using \(k=O(d)\), \(\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d)\), and \(r_{\mathrm{te}}\le r_{\mathrm{te},0}\) proves the uniform \(o(1)\) reduction.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proposition-19: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-sharp-directed-signals}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud} and~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, in probability,
\begin{equation}
r_{\max}^*(X)=\frac{1+o(1)}{g\sqrt d},\qquad r_{\mathrm{sp}}^*(X)=\frac{1+o(1)}{s_\alpha}.
\label{eq:app-det-sharp-radii}
\end{equation}
Moreover, uniformly over the complete exact faces,
\begin{align}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X}\max_{i\ne j}\left|(u_{ij}^W)^\top\mu_i-\frac1{\sqrt\pi}\right|&=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\label{eq:app-det-max-sharp-signal}\\
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\min_{i\ne j}(u_{ij}^W)^\top\mu_i&\ge\frac{s_\alpha}{\sqrt2}-o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-sharp-signal}
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-19 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Let \(M_\mu\) have rows \(\mu_i^\top\), let \(C_\mu:=PM_\mu\), and let \(T:=\operatorname{sign}(M_\mu)\). Standard Gaussian concentration, uniformly over the \(k=\Theta(d)\) classes, gives
\begin{equation}
\frac{\|C_\mu\|_{\mathrm{sum}}}{k\sqrt d}=g+o_{\mathbb P}(1),\qquad \max_i\left|\frac{\|\mu_i\|_1}{\sqrt d}-g\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(1),\qquad \max_{i\ne j}\frac{|T_j^\top\mu_i|}{\sqrt d}=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\label{eq:app-det-sharp-gaussian-inputs}
\end{equation}
and, for every fixed \(a>0\),
\begin{equation}
\frac1{kd}\#\{(i,\ell):\sqrt d\,|C_\mu[i,\ell]|\le a\}\xrightarrow{\mathbb P}\mathbb P(|G|\le a),\qquad \max_i\frac1d\#\{\ell:\sqrt d\,|\mu_i[\ell]|\le a\}\le\mathbb P(|G|\le a)+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-sharp-small-ball}
\end{equation}
Also \(\|C_m-C_\mu\|_{\mathrm{sum}}=o_{\mathbb P}(k\sqrt d)\) by Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}. Every feasible \(W\) satisfies the averaged exposure inequality \(\langle W,C_m\rangle\ge k-1\). Max--sum duality and \eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-gaussian-inputs} therefore give \(r_{\max}^*(X)\ge(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))/(g\sqrt d)\), while Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}, item~\ref{item:app-det-H5} gives the matching upper bound. Similarly, operator--nuclear duality and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input}, item~\ref{item:app-det-S1} give \(r_{\mathrm{sp}}^*(X)\ge(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))/s_\alpha\), while the polar witness \(Q_m/\rho_X\) and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input}, item~\ref{item:app-det-S3} give the matching upper bound. This proves \eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-radii}.

Fix \(W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X\) and set \(A:=W/r_{\max}^*(X)\), so \(\|A\|_{\max}=1\). The exposure inequality and the exact Max radius imply
\begin{equation}
\langle A,C_\mu\rangle\ge\|C_\mu\|_{\mathrm{sum}}-o_{\mathbb P}(k\sqrt d)
\label{eq:app-det-sharp-max-exposure}
\end{equation}
uniformly over the complete Max face. Put \(S:=\operatorname{sign}(C_\mu)\) and \(\Delta_{i\ell}:=1-A[i,\ell]S[i,\ell]\in[0,2]\). Since \((A[i,\ell]-S[i,\ell])^2=\Delta_{i\ell}^2\le2\Delta_{i\ell}\), for every fixed \(a>0\),
\begin{equation}
\frac{\|A-S\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{kd}\le\frac{2\sqrt d}{akd}\left(\|C_\mu\|_{\mathrm{sum}}-\langle A,C_\mu\rangle\right)+\frac4{kd}\#\{(i,\ell):\sqrt d\,|C_\mu[i,\ell]|\le a\}.
\label{eq:app-det-sharp-global-split}
\end{equation}
First sending \(d\to\infty\) and then \(a\downarrow0\) gives \(\sup_W\|A-S\|_{\mathrm F}^2/(kd)=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Since \(C_\mu[i,\ell]=\mu_i[\ell]-\bar\mu[\ell]\), where \(\bar\mu=k^{-1}\sum_i\mu_i\) and \(\|\bar\mu\|_2=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), the same small-ball argument transfers \(S\) to \(T\), yielding
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\max}^X}\frac{\|A-T\|_{\mathrm F}^2}{kd}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-sharp-global-sign}
\end{equation}
Let \(\bar A=k^{-1}\sum_iA_i\) and \(\bar T=k^{-1}\sum_iT_i\). Jensen's inequality and \eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-global-sign}, together with \(\mathbb E\|\bar T\|_2^2=d/k=O(1)\), imply \(\sup_W\|\bar A\|_2/\sqrt d=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Averaging the class-\(i\) constraints over its samples and over all competitors gives
\[
(A_i-\bar A)^\top m_i\ge\frac{k-1}{k\,r_{\max}^*(X)}=g\sqrt d-o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt d).
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}, item~\ref{item:app-det-H1}, the bound \(\|A_i-\bar A\|_2\le2\sqrt d\), and the preceding control of \(\bar A\) therefore imply \(A_i^\top\mu_i\ge g\sqrt d-o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt d)\) uniformly over \(i\) and the complete face. The nonnegative deficiency \(D_i:=\|\mu_i\|_1-A_i^\top\mu_i\) is thus \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt d)\) uniformly. For every fixed \(a>0\),
\begin{equation}
\frac1d\|A_i-T_i\|_2^2\le\frac{2D_i}{a\sqrt d}+\frac4d\#\{\ell:\sqrt d\,|\mu_i[\ell]|\le a\}.
\label{eq:app-det-sharp-row-split}
\end{equation}
Using \eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-small-ball} and then sending \(a\downarrow0\) proves \(\sup_W\max_i\|A_i-T_i\|_2/\sqrt d=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Finally, uniformly over \(i\ne j\), \((T_i-T_j)^\top\mu_i=g\sqrt d+o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt d)\) and \(\|T_i-T_j\|_2=\sqrt{2d}+o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt d)\), which proves \eqref{eq:app-det-max-sharp-signal}.

For Spectral, class-average feasibility gives \((w_i-w_j)^\top m_i\ge1\), while \(\|w_i-w_j\|_2\le\sqrt2\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sqrt2\,r_{\mathrm{sp}}^*(X)\). Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}, item~\ref{item:app-det-H1} and \eqref{eq:app-det-sharp-radii} therefore give \((u_{ij}^W)^\top\mu_i\ge s_\alpha/\sqrt2-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly, proving \eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-sharp-signal}.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- proposition-20: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-det-error-exponents}
Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:gaussian-cloud} and~\ref{ass:asymptotic-regime}, uniformly over the indicated complete maximum-margin direction sets,
\begin{align}
\sup_{R\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X}\left|\mathsf F_d(R)-\frac12\right|&=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\label{eq:app-det-row-exponent}\\
\sup_{M\in\mathcal U_{\max}^X}\left|\mathsf F_d(M)-\frac1\pi\right|&=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\label{eq:app-det-max-exponent}\\
\frac{s_\alpha^2}{2}-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\le\mathsf F_d(S)&\le\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)^2}{2}+o_{\mathbb P}(1),\qquad S\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X.
\label{eq:app-det-spectral-exponent}
\end{align}
Consequently, for \(0<\alpha\le1\), the spectral interval collapses to \(\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)^2/2\); at \(\alpha=1\), this value is \(32/(9\pi^2)\). Uniformly over \(R\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X\), \(M\in\mathcal U_{\max}^X\), and \(S\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X\),
\begin{equation}
\log\frac{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(M)}{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(R)}=\left(\frac{\pi-2}{4\pi}+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\right)\frac d{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2},
\label{eq:app-det-row-max-error-gain}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{1-\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)^2}{2}-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\le\frac{2r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log\frac{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(S)}{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(R)}\le\frac{1-s_\alpha^2}{2}+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-row-spectral-error-gain}
\end{equation}
The Row--Spectral gain is exact when \(\alpha\le1\).
<!-- end proposition-20 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
For Row, Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-boundary} and the Gaussian mean shell imply \((u_{ij}^R)^\top\mu_i=1/\sqrt2+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly over all directed pairs and the complete Row face. Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-sharp-directed-signals} gives the corresponding uniform Max signal \(1/\sqrt\pi+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). Hence \(\mathsf E_d(R)=1/2+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and \(\mathsf E_d(M)=1/\pi+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly.

For Spectral, Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-sharp-directed-signals} gives \(\mathsf E_d(S)\ge s_\alpha^2/2-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) uniformly. Theorem~\ref{thm:deterministic-separation-clean} implies that every spectral direction has an ordered pair with \(d_{ij}(S)\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), and hence \((u_{ij}^S)^\top u_{ij}^{\mu}\le\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). For that unordered pair,
\[
(u_{ij}^S)^\top\mu_i+(u_{ji}^S)^\top\mu_j=(u_{ij}^S)^\top(\mu_i-\mu_j)\le\sqrt2\,\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
Both directed signals are positive by the preceding lower bound, so at least one is at most \(\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)/\sqrt2+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\). This proves the upper endpoint for \(\mathsf E_d(S)\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-exponent-reduction} transfers all three statements from \(\mathsf E_d\) to \(\mathsf F_d\). Finally, \(s_\alpha=\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)\) for \(\alpha\le1\), while subtraction of the exponents gives \eqref{eq:app-det-row-max-error-gain}--\eqref{eq:app-det-row-spectral-error-gain}.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proposition-21: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-det-optimizer-error-exponents}
Under the assumptions and optimizer conventions of Theorem~\ref{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}, the deterministic full-batch optimizer trajectories satisfy, in probability,
\begin{align}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\left|\mathsf F_d\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}}\right)-\frac12\right|&=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\label{eq:app-rowgdm-error-exponent}\\
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\left|\mathsf F_d\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}}\right)-\frac1\pi\right|&=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-adam-error-exponent}
\end{align}
Exact-SVD Muon satisfies
\begin{equation}
\frac{s_\alpha^2}{2}-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\le\liminf_{t\to\infty}\mathsf F_d\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{Muon}}\right)\le\limsup_{t\to\infty}\mathsf F_d\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{Muon}}\right)\le\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)^2}{2}+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-muon-error-exponent}
\end{equation}
Define the Row--Spectral exponent-gap constant
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\rm exp}(\alpha):=\frac{1-\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)^2}{4}=\frac14\left(1-\frac{m_{1/2}(\alpha)^2}{\alpha\wedge1}\right)>0,
\qquad
m_{1/2}(\alpha):=\frac{\alpha}{2\pi}\int_{a_\alpha}^{b_\alpha}\frac{\sqrt{(b_\alpha-x)(x-a_\alpha)}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx,
\label{eq:app-det-c-alpha}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}
a_\alpha=(1-\alpha^{-1/2})^2,\qquad b_\alpha=(1+\alpha^{-1/2})^2.
\end{equation}
Equivalently,
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\rm exp}(\alpha)=\frac14\left[1-\frac{\alpha^2}{4\pi^2(\alpha\wedge1)}\left(\int_{a_\alpha}^{b_\alpha}\frac{\sqrt{(b_\alpha-x)(x-a_\alpha)}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx\right)^2\right].
\label{eq:app-det-c-alpha-expanded}
\end{equation}
For example,
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\rm exp}(1)=\frac14\left(1-\frac{64}{9\pi^2}\right)\approx0.06987,\qquad \Delta_{\rm exp}(2)\approx0.03247,\qquad \Delta_{\rm exp}(3)\approx0.02133.
\label{eq:app-det-c-alpha-examples}
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\left|\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log\frac{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}})}{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}})}-\frac{\pi-2}{4\pi}\right|=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\label{eq:app-rowgdm-adam-error-gain}
\end{equation}
and
\begin{align}
\Delta_{\rm exp}(\alpha)-o_{\mathbb P}(1)
&\le\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log\frac{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{Muon}})}{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}})}
\nonumber\\
&\le\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log\frac{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{Muon}})}{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{RowGDM}})}
\le\frac{1-s_\alpha^2}{4}+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-rowgdm-muon-error-gain}
\end{align}
The same conclusions hold with RowGDM replaced by RowGD, with Adam replaced by SignGD or Signum, and with Muon replaced by Spectral-GD. When \(0<\alpha\le1\), the two Row--Muon bounds coincide. Here, \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) refers to the limit \(d\to\infty\), after taking \(t\to\infty\) at each fixed \(d\).
<!-- end proposition-21 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
The full-batch margin-convergence results used in Theorem~\ref{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean} imply that the normalized trajectories approach the corresponding row-, entrywise max-, and spectral-norm maximum-margin direction sets. Since Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-error-exponents} holds uniformly over each complete direction set, Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity} transfers its exponent bounds to the long-time optimizer trajectories. This gives \eqref{eq:app-rowgdm-error-exponent}--\eqref{eq:app-muon-error-exponent}. The definition \eqref{eq:app-det-c-alpha} follows from \(\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)=m_{1/2}(\alpha)/\sqrt{\alpha\wedge1}\), and the integral form follows from the Marchenko--Pastur density. The log-error ratio statements follow from
\[
\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log\frac{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W^{(2)})}{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W^{(1)})}=\frac12\left(\mathsf F_d(W^{(1)})-\mathsf F_d(W^{(2)})\right).
\]
No uniqueness of the optimizer-selected limiting direction is required.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-det-muon-adam-order}
Under the assumptions and optimizer conventions of Theorem~\ref{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}, suppose \(0<\alpha<\alpha_\star\), where \(\alpha_\star\approx1.225\) is the aspect-ratio threshold defined by \(s_{\alpha_\star}^2=2/\pi\). Then, with
\[
c_{\mathrm{MA}}(\alpha):=\frac14\left(s_\alpha^2-\frac2\pi\right)>0,
\]
the deterministic full-batch trajectories satisfy
\begin{equation}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log\frac{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{Muon}})}{\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}})}\le -c_{\mathrm{MA}}(\alpha)+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\label{eq:app-det-muon-adam-order}
\end{equation}
Thus exact-SVD Muon has asymptotically smaller population error, and hence higher population accuracy, than full-batch Adam with probability tending to one. The same conclusion holds with Muon replaced by Spectral-GD and Adam replaced by SignGD or Signum.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
Proposition~\ref{cor:app-det-optimizer-error-exponents} gives \(\liminf_{t\to\infty}\mathsf F_d(W_t^{\mathrm{Muon}})\ge s_\alpha^2/2-o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) and \(\mathsf F_d(W_t^{\mathrm{Adam}})=1/\pi+o_{\mathbb P}(1)\) at long times. Using \(\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\log(\mathcal E_2/\mathcal E_1)=\frac12(\mathsf F_d(W_1)-\mathsf F_d(W_2))\) gives \eqref{eq:app-det-muon-adam-order}.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:app-det-muon-adam-practice}
In practical last-layer training, Adam is typically preferred to Muon, whereas Corollary~\ref{cor:app-det-muon-adam-order} predicts the opposite ordering for \(\alpha<\alpha_\star\). A likely source of this mismatch is that our result compares only asymptotic convergence directions and therefore does not capture convergence speed or finite-time trajectories. The comparison is also idealized, using deterministic full-batch training, exact-SVD Muon, and Adam without a numerical-stability constant. For \(\alpha\ge\alpha_\star\), the ordering between Adam and Muon remains open.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-22: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-stoch-near-reduction}
Fix a linearly separable dataset \(X\), a matrix norm \(\psi\), and \(0\le\varepsilon<\gamma_\psi(X)\). For every \(U\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X\), define
\begin{equation}
V_U:=\frac{U}{\operatorname{mar}_X(U)},\qquad \xi_\psi(\varepsilon;X):=\frac{\varepsilon}{\gamma_\psi(X)-\varepsilon}.
\label{eq:app-stoch-near-representative}
\end{equation}
Then \(V_U\in\mathcal F_X\),
\begin{equation}
\psi(V_U)\le\left(1+\xi_\psi(\varepsilon;X)\right)r_\psi^*(X),
\label{eq:app-stoch-near-norm-bound}
\end{equation}
and \(V_U\) has the same normalized pairwise row differences as \(U\).
<!-- end lemma-22 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
Set \(\widehat U:=U/\psi(U)\). By definition of \(\mathcal U_{\psi,\varepsilon}^X\), \(\operatorname{mar}_X(\widehat U)\ge\gamma_\psi(X)-\varepsilon>0\). Hence \(V_U=\widehat U/\operatorname{mar}_X(\widehat U)\) is feasible and
\[
\psi(V_U)=\frac1{\operatorname{mar}_X(\widehat U)}\le\frac1{\gamma_\psi(X)-\varepsilon}=\frac{r_\psi^*(X)}{1-\varepsilon/\gamma_\psi(X)}=\left(1+\xi_\psi(\varepsilon;X)\right)r_\psi^*(X).
\]
The normalized pairwise row differences are unchanged under positive scaling.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- lemma-23: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-stoch-combined-input}
There are deterministic \(\omega_d\downarrow0\), constants \(C,c>0\), and events \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}}\) such that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\!\left((\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}})^c\right)\le C\exp\!\left[-c\sqrt{d\log(2N(d)(d+1))}\right],
\label{eq:app-stoch-near-event-probability}
\end{equation}
all conclusions of Propositions~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event} and~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input} hold with their vanishing errors bounded by \(\omega_d\), and
\begin{equation}
\max_{i,s}\|x_{i,s}\|_2\le1+2r_0+\omega_d,\qquad \max_{i,s}\|x_{i,s}\|_1\le(1+2r_0+\omega_d)\sqrt d.
\label{eq:app-stoch-data-radius-bounds}
\end{equation}
We may additionally take \(\omega_d\ge1/k\).
<!-- end lemma-23 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Intersect the events in Propositions~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event} and~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-input} with the event \(\max_{i,s}\|z_{i,s}\|_2\le2\). The latter fails with probability at most \(2N e^{-cd}\), which is smaller than the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-near-event-probability}. Under the normalized convention~\eqref{eq:app-normalized-data}, the mean shell gives \(\max_i\|\mu_i\|_2\le1+\omega_d\), so \(\|x_{i,s}\|_2\le1+\omega_d+2r_0\), and the \(\ell_1\) bound follows from \(\|x\|_1\le\sqrt d\,\|x\|_2\). Enlarge one deterministic envelope to dominate all finitely many errors and \(1/k\).
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- proposition-22: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-stoch-near-stability}
There are constants \(C_{\mathrm{row}},C_{\max}>0\) and \(C_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)>0\) such that, on \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}}\), for every \(0\le\xi\le1\),
\begin{align}
W\in\mathcal F_X,\ \|W\|_{\mathrm{row}}\le(1+\xi)r_{\mathrm{row}}^*(X)&\Longrightarrow \max_{i\ne j}\|u_{ij}^W-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2\le C_{\mathrm{row}}(\omega_d+\xi)^{1/4},
\label{eq:app-stoch-row-near-stability}\\
W\in\mathcal F_X,\ \|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le(1+\xi)r_{\mathrm{sp}}^*(X)\Longrightarrow& D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W)\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)-C_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)(\omega_d+\xi)^{1/4},
\label{eq:app-stoch-sp-near-stability}\\
W\in\mathcal F_X,\
\|W\|_{\max}\le(1+\xi)r_{\max}^*(X)&\Longrightarrow D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(W)\ge\delta_{\max}-C_{\max}(\omega_d+\xi).
\label{eq:app-stoch-max-near-stability}
\end{align}
<!-- end proposition-22 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
For the row norm, put \(q:=\omega_d+\xi\). The empirical-mean witness in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-rigidity} gives \(r_{\mathrm{row}}^*(X)\le1+C\omega_d\), so \(\max_i\|w_i\|_2\le1+Cq\). Averaging feasibility within class \(i\) and then over all competing classes gives \((w_i-\bar w)^\top m_i\ge1-1/k\). The row variance identity then gives \(\|\bar w\|_2^2\le Cq\), and substituting this bound back into the averaged margin inequality yields \(\max_i\|w_i-m_i\|_2\le Cq^{1/4}\). The mean perturbation in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event} and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-normalization} prove~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-row-near-stability}.

For the spectral norm, Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-spectral-rigidity} gives an error \(C_\alpha q^{1/2}\) when \(\alpha\ne1\) and \(Cq^{1/4}\) when \(\alpha=1\). Since \(q^{1/2}\le q^{1/4}\) for \(q\le1\), enlarging the constant proves~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-sp-near-stability} uniformly over all aspect ratios.

For the max norm, fix \(i\ne j\), set \(v:=w_i-w_j\), and put \(u:=u_{ij}^m\). Near-optimality and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H5) give
\begin{equation}
\|v\|_\infty\le\frac{\sqrt{2\pi}+Cq}{\sqrt d}.
\label{eq:app-stoch-max-near-cap}
\end{equation}
The two class-averaged feasibility constraints imply \(v^\top(m_i-m_j)\ge2\), and hence \(v^\top u\ge\sqrt2-Cq\). Applying the clipped minimum-energy characterization in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-clipped-exact}, the uniform empirical laws in Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H6), and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-det-clipped-asymptotic} gives
\begin{equation}
\frac{v^\top u}{\|v\|_2}\le\kappa_{\max}+Cq.
\label{eq:app-stoch-max-near-cosine}
\end{equation}
The cosine-distance identity and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H4) prove~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-max-near-stability}.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- proposition-23: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-stoch-ratio-bounds}
On \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}}\), for every sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{equation}
\frac{R_{\mathrm{row}}(X)}{\gamma_{\mathrm{row}}(X)}\le K_{\mathrm{row}},\qquad \frac{R_{\mathrm{sp}}(X)}{\gamma_{\mathrm{sp}}(X)}\le K_{\mathrm{sp}},\qquad \frac{R_{\max}(X)}{\gamma_{\max}(X)}\le K_{\max},
\label{eq:app-stoch-ratio-bounds}
\end{equation}
where one may take
\begin{equation}
K_{\mathrm{row}}:=4(1+2r_0),\qquad K_{\mathrm{sp}}:=\frac{8(1+2r_0)}{s_\alpha},\qquad K_{\max}:=(\sqrt{2\pi}+1)(1+2r_0).
\label{eq:app-stoch-ratio-constants}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-23 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Each ratio equals \(R_\psi(X)r_\psi^*(X)\). For every sufficiently large \(d\), Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-rigidity} gives \(r_{\mathrm{row}}^*(X)\le2\), the reduced-polar witness~\eqref{eq:app-det-spectral-optimum-upper} and \(\rho_X\to s_\alpha>0\) give \(r_{\mathrm{sp}}^*(X)\le4/s_\alpha\), and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-common-event}(H5) gives \(r_{\max}^*(X)\le(\sqrt{2\pi}+1)/(2\sqrt d)\). Equation~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-data-radius-bounds} and \(\omega_d\to0\) imply, for sufficiently large \(d\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{row}}(X)=R_{\mathrm{sp}}(X)\le2(1+2r_0),\qquad R_{\max}(X)\le2(1+2r_0)\sqrt d.
\]
Combining these estimates proves~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-ratio-bounds}.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- proposition-24: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-stoch-near-geometry}
\label{thm:stochastic-separation-clean}
Under the data and batching assumptions of Proposition~\ref{thm:stoch-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}, fix \(\beta\in[\beta_0,1)\). Then, for every sufficiently large \(d\), on \(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}}\), all three effective margins \(\gamma_\psi(X)-\varepsilon_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)\) are positive and
\begin{align}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}^X}\max_{i\ne j}\|u_{ij}^U-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2&\le h_*,
\label{eq:app-stoch-row-set-upper}\\
\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp},\beta,b}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V)&\ge\frac{\delta_*}{2},
\label{eq:app-stoch-sp-set-lower}\\
\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\max,\beta,b}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V)&\ge\frac{\delta_*}{2}.
\label{eq:app-stoch-max-set-lower}
\end{align}
Moreover, after increasing the deterministic dimension threshold if necessary,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}})\ge1-e^{-\sqrt d}.
\label{eq:app-stoch-clean-probability}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-24 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
For each geometry, define the relative stochastic deficit
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\psi,d}(\beta):=\frac{\varepsilon_{\psi,\beta,b}(X)}{\gamma_\psi(X)}=2(1-\beta)m_d(m_d^2-1)\frac{R_\psi(X)}{\gamma_\psi(X)}.
\label{eq:app-stoch-relative-deficit}
\end{equation}
Since \(m_d\le m_0\), Proposition~\ref{prop:app-stoch-ratio-bounds} gives
\[
\Delta_{\psi,d}(\beta)\le2(1-\beta)A_0K_*\le\theta_*<1.
\]
Thus every effective margin is positive. By the definition of \(\theta_*\),
\begin{equation}
\frac{\Delta_{\psi,d}(\beta)}{1-\Delta_{\psi,d}(\beta)}\le\frac{b_*}{2}.
\label{eq:app-stoch-near-slack-bound}
\end{equation}
For every \(U\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\beta,b}^X\), Lemma~\ref{lem:app-stoch-near-reduction} therefore gives a feasible representative with identical normalized pairwise row differences and relative norm slack at most \(b_*/2\). For every sufficiently large \(d\), \(\omega_d\le b_*/2\), so Proposition~\ref{prop:app-stoch-near-stability} gives
\[
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}^X}\max_{i\ne j}\|u_{ij}^U-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2\le C_{\mathrm{row}}b_*^{1/4}\le h_*,
\]
\[
\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp},\beta,b}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V)\ge\delta_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)-C_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)b_*^{1/4}\ge\delta_*-\frac{\delta_*}{8}\ge\frac{\delta_*}{2},
\]
and
\[
\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\max,\beta,b}^X}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V)\ge\delta_{\max}-C_{\max}b_*\ge\delta_*-\frac{\delta_*}{8}\ge\frac{\delta_*}{2}.
\]
This proves~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-row-set-upper}--\eqref{eq:app-stoch-max-set-lower}. Finally, \(\log(2N(d)(d+1))\to\infty\), so the failure probability in~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-near-event-probability} is at most \(e^{-\sqrt d}\) for every sufficiently large \(d\).
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
Fix \(\beta\in[\beta_0,1)\), and let \(\mathcal R_d\) be the Gaussian radial event from Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-gaussian-radial-event}. Set
\[
\mathcal H_d:=\mathcal E_d^{\mathrm{near}}\cap\mathcal R_d.
\]
By~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-near-event-probability} and~\eqref{eq:app-acc-radial-event-probability}, after increasing the deterministic dimension threshold,
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\mathcal H_d)\ge1-e^{-\sqrt d}.
\label{eq:app-stoch-accuracy-event}
\end{equation}

Work on \(\mathcal H_d\). Define the Row family
\[
\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}:=\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}^X
\]
and, for \(\psi\in\{\mathrm{sp},\max\}\), the competitor family
\[
\mathcal C_{\psi,d}^{\mathrm{clf}}:=\mathcal U_{\psi,\beta,b}^X.
\]
Proposition~\ref{prop:app-stoch-near-geometry} gives
\begin{equation}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\max_{i\ne j}\|u_{ij}^U-u_{ij}^{\mu}\|_2\le h_*,
\qquad
\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_{\psi,d}^{\mathrm{clf}}}D_{\mathrm{avg\text{-}bdry}}(V)\ge\frac{\delta_*}{2}.
\label{eq:app-acc-stochastic-geometry-input}
\end{equation}
The choice of \(h_*\) in~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-accuracy-amplitude-budget} gives the strict limiting amplitude gap
\begin{equation}
\mathsf a(h_*)>\mathsf b(\delta_*/2),
\label{eq:app-acc-stochastic-amplitude-gap}
\end{equation}
where \(\mathsf a\) and \(\mathsf b\) are defined in~\eqref{eq:app-acc-limiting-amplitudes}.

Choose fixed constants \(0<b<a\) such that
\begin{equation}
\mathsf b(\delta_*/2)<b<a<\mathsf a(h_*).
\label{eq:app-stoch-fixed-amplitude-gap}
\end{equation}
On \(\mathcal R_d\), the radial deviation and coherence in~\eqref{eq:app-acc-radial-coherence} converge to zero under a deterministic envelope. Therefore, for every sufficiently large \(d\), the finite-dimensional amplitudes in~\eqref{eq:app-acc-row-amplitude}--\eqref{eq:app-acc-competitor-amplitude} satisfy
\[
A_d\ge a,\qquad B_d\le b
\]
for the Row family and each of the two competitor families. Proposition~\ref{prop:app-acc-finite-bounds} consequently gives
\begin{equation}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)\le(k-1)\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{a}{\sigma_d}\right),
\qquad
\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_{\psi,d}^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V)\ge2\pi_{\min,d}\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{b}{\sigma_d}\right).
\label{eq:app-stoch-family-error-bounds}
\end{equation}
For \(x\ge y\ge0\), the Gaussian upper tail satisfies \(\overline\Phi(x)/\overline\Phi(y)\le\exp(-(x^2-y^2)/2)\). Hence \(k=O(d)\), \(r_{\mathrm{te}}\le r_{\mathrm{te},0}\), and \(\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d)\) imply
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sup_{U\in\mathcal R_d^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)}{\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_{\psi,d}^{\mathrm{clf}}}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V)}
\le
\frac{Ck}{\pi_{\min,d}}e^{-cd}
\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:app-stoch-family-error-ratio}
\end{equation}
Hence, for every sufficiently large \(d\) on \(\mathcal H_d\),
\begin{equation}
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)
<
\min_{\psi\in\{\mathrm{sp},\max\}}
\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\psi,\beta,b}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V).
\label{eq:app-stoch-set-error-order}
\end{equation}

It remains to transfer the set ordering to the optimizer trajectories. Proposition~\ref{prop:app-stoch-near-geometry} ensures that all effective margins are positive. Corollary~\ref{cor:app-ga-margin-transfer} therefore gives
\begin{align}
d_{\cos}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}},\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}^X\right)&\longrightarrow0,\nonumber\\
d_{\cos}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Muon}},\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp},\beta,b}^X\right)&\longrightarrow0,\nonumber\\
d_{\cos}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Signum}},\mathcal U_{\max,\beta,b}^X\right)&\longrightarrow0.
\label{eq:app-stoch-trajectory-near-set}
\end{align}
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity} to~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-trajectory-near-set} and then using~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-set-error-order} gives, for each \(\mathrm{opt}\in\{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Muon},\mathrm{RR\text{-}Signum}\}\),
\begin{align}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}}\right)
&\le
\sup_{U\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row},\beta,b}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(U)\nonumber\\
&<
\inf_{V\in\mathcal U_{\psi_{\mathrm{opt}},\beta,b}^X}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}(V)\nonumber\\
&\le
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\mathcal E_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right),
\label{eq:app-stoch-trajectory-error-order}
\end{align}
where \(\psi_{\mathrm{Muon}}=\psi_{\mathrm{sp}}\) and \(\psi_{\mathrm{Signum}}=\psi_{\max}\). Since \(\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}=1-\mathcal E_{\pi,d}\),
\[
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{RR\text{-}RowSGDM}}\right)
>
\max_{\mathrm{opt}\in\{\mathrm{RR\text{-}Muon},\mathrm{RR\text{-}Signum}\}}
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right).
\]
Since \(H_d\) and the dimension threshold above are independent of \(\beta\in[\beta_0,1)\), and the random-reshuffling margin bounds hold deterministically for every reshuffling realization, the conclusion holds simultaneously for all such \(\beta\) and every realization of the reshuffling.
Together with~\eqref{eq:app-stoch-accuracy-event}, this proves~\eqref{eq:stoch-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-package}
Assume \(1\le b<N\). For \(z=(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\in\mathbb R^N\), define \(T_Bz:=b^{-1}\sum_{n\in B}z_n\) and \(\sigma(z)^2:=\mathbb E_B[(T_Bz)^2]\). Then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E_B[T_Bz]=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^Nz_n,
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-first-moment}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\sigma(z)^2=\frac{b-1}{bN(N-1)}\left(\sum_{n=1}^Nz_n\right)^2+\frac{N-b}{bN(N-1)}\sum_{n=1}^Nz_n^2.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-second-moment}
\end{equation}
Consequently, with \(\mu_1(W):=\mathbb E_B[G_B(W)]\) and \(\mu_2(W):=\mathbb E_B[G_B(W)^{\odot2}]\),
\begin{equation}
\mu_1(W)=\frac1N S(W),\qquad \mu_2(W)=\frac{(b-1)S(W)^{\odot2}+(N-b)Q(W)}{bN(N-1)},
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-moments-matrix}
\end{equation}
and therefore
\begin{equation}
\mu_1(W)\oslash\mu_2(W)^{\odot1/2}=\Phi_{N,b}(W).
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-law-direction}
\end{equation}
Moreover, because \(1\le b<N\), \(\sigma\) is a norm and
\begin{equation}
\underline c_{N,b}\|z\|_2\le\sigma(z)\le\frac1{\sqrt b}\|z\|_2,\qquad \underline c_{N,b}:=\sqrt{\frac{N-b}{bN(N-1)}},
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-sigma-equivalence}
\end{equation}
while every \(b\)-subset satisfies
\begin{equation}
|T_Bz|\le K_{N,b}\sigma(z),\qquad \frac1b\sum_{n\in B}|z_n|\le K_{N,b}\sigma(z),\qquad K_{N,b}:=\sqrt{\frac{N(N-1)}{N-b}}.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-relative-batch-bound}
\end{equation}
For a matrix coordinate \(\rho=(r,a)\), define \(z_n^\rho(W):=g_n(W)[\rho]\) and \(\sigma_\rho(W):=\sigma(z^\rho(W))\). Under the nonzero-coordinate assumption in Proposition~\ref{thm:rr-adamproxy-epoch-high-memory}, \(\sigma_\rho(W)>0\) for every finite \(W\) and every \(\rho\).
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
Let \(I_n:=\mathbf 1_{\{n\in B\}}\). Since \(B\) is a uniform \(b\)-subset, \(\mathbb E I_n=b/N\) and \(\mathbb E[I_nI_{n'}]=b(b-1)/(N(N-1))\) for \(n\ne n'\). Expanding \(\mathbb E[(T_Bz)^2]\) gives \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-second-moment}, while \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-first-moment} is immediate.
Applying the two identities coordinate-wise to \(g_n(W)\) gives \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-moments-matrix}, and substituting these expressions into \(\mu_1(W)\oslash\mu_2(W)^{\odot1/2}\) gives \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-law-direction} by \eqref{eq:adamproxy-direction-explicit-clean}. The second term in \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-second-moment} gives the lower bound in \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-sigma-equivalence}, while \(|T_Bz|\le b^{-1}\sum_{n\in B}|z_n|\le b^{-1/2}\|z\|_2\) gives the upper bound and \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-relative-batch-bound}.
Finally, at finite \(W\), every softmax probability is strictly positive. If \(r=y_n\), then \(g_n(W)[r,a]=-(1-p_{n,y_n}(W))x_n[a]\ne0\), while if \(r\ne y_n\), then \(g_n(W)[r,a]=p_{n,r}(W)x_n[a]\ne0\). Hence \(z^\rho(W)\ne0\), so \(\sigma_\rho(W)>0\).
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-step-stability}
Let \(0<\beta_1\le\beta_2<1\) and define
\begin{equation}
A(\beta_1,\beta_2)^2:=\frac{(1-\beta_1)^2}{(1-\beta_2)(1-\beta_1^2/\beta_2)}.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-ratio-constant}
\end{equation}
Then \(\beta_1^2<\beta_2\), and for \(U_t:=M_{t+1}\oslash V_{t+1}^{\odot1/2}\),
\begin{equation}
\|U_t\|_{\max}\le A(\beta_1,\beta_2),\qquad \|W_{t+1}-W_t\|_{\mathrm F}\le\sqrt{kd}\,A(\beta_1,\beta_2)\eta_t.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-step-bound}
\end{equation}
There are finite data-dependent constants \(L,C\) such that, for all \(U,W\), every batch \(B\), and every coordinate \(\rho\),
\begin{equation}
\frac{|G_B(U)[\rho]-G_B(W)[\rho]|}{\sigma_\rho(W)}\le C\left(e^{L\|U-W\|_{\mathrm F}}-1\right),
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-stability}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{|G_B(U)[\rho]^2-G_B(W)[\rho]^2|}{\sigma_\rho(W)^2}\le C\left(e^{2L\|U-W\|_{\mathrm F}}-1\right).
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-square-stability}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Fix one coordinate and write \(Y_u:=G_{B_u}(W_u)[\rho]\). Zero initialization gives \(M_{t+1}=(1-\beta_1)\sum_{j=0}^t\beta_1^jY_{t-j}\) and \(V_{t+1}=(1-\beta_2)\sum_{j=0}^t\beta_2^jY_{t-j}^2\). If \(V_{t+1}=0\), then \(M_{t+1}=0\); otherwise Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(M_{t+1}^2\le A(\beta_1,\beta_2)^2V_{t+1}\), proving \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-step-bound}. For the stability bounds, let \(\Delta:=U-W\). The logit perturbations satisfy \(|e_c^\top\Delta x_n|\le\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm F}\|x_n\|_2\), so every softmax probability ratio, and also the ratio of \(1-p_{n,y_n}\), lies between \(e^{-L\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm F}}\) and \(e^{L\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm F}}\) after enlarging \(L\). Each coordinate of \(g_n\) is a fixed feature coordinate multiplied by one of these quantities, giving \(|g_n(U)[\rho]-g_n(W)[\rho]|\le(e^{L\|\Delta\|_{\mathrm F}}-1)|g_n(W)[\rho]|\). Summing over \(n\in B\) and applying \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-relative-batch-bound} proves \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-stability}; the identity \(|a^2-b^2|\le|a-b|(|a|+|b|)\) then gives \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-square-stability}.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-ema-concentration}
For every \(\delta>0\), there exists \(\omega_\delta:(0,1)\to[0,1]\) with \(\omega_\delta(\beta)\to0\) as \(\beta\uparrow1\) such that, for every epoch start \(\tau=rm\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P\left(\max_{0\le s<m}\sup_{z\ne{\mathbf 0}}\left|(1-\beta)\sum_{j=0}^\infty\beta^j\left(Y_{\tau+s-j}(z)-\mathbb EY_0(z)\right)\right|>\delta\right)\le\omega_\delta(\beta).
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-ema-first}
\end{equation}
The same statement holds with \(Y_t(z)^2\) in place of \(Y_t(z)\) and \(\mathbb E[Y_0(z)^2]=1\). For fixed \(N,b\), one may take \(\omega_\delta(\beta)\le C_\delta(1-\beta)\).
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
It is enough to work on the compact \(\sigma\)-unit sphere. Group the lags in the exponential average by reshuffling epoch. Contributions from distinct epochs are independent, every epoch block has mean zero, and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-package} uniformly bounds \(|Y_t(z)|\). Hence the variance of the centered exponential average is at most \(C(1-\beta)^2\sum_{q\ge0}\beta^{2qm}\le C'(1-\beta)\). Chebyshev's inequality gives the stated rate for each fixed \(z\). The maps \(z\mapsto T_Bz\) are uniformly Lipschitz in the \(\sigma\)-norm, so a finite \(\delta\)-net and a union bound make the estimate uniform over \(z\) and over \(s=0,\ldots,m-1\). The argument for \(Y_t(z)^2\) is identical because \(Y_t(z)\) is uniformly bounded.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-freezing}
Fix \(0<\beta_1\le\beta_2<1\). Under the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{thm:rr-adamproxy-epoch-high-memory}, for every coordinate \(\rho\), uniformly over \(0\le s<m\),
\begin{equation}
\frac{|M_{\tau_r+s+1}[\rho]-\overline M_{\tau_r+s}^{\beta_1}(W_{\tau_r})[\rho]|}{\sigma_\rho(W_{\tau_r})}\xrightarrow[r\to\infty]{\mathbb P}0,
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-freezing-first}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
\frac{|V_{\tau_r+s+1}[\rho]-\overline V_{\tau_r+s}^{\beta_2}(W_{\tau_r})[\rho]|}{\sigma_\rho(W_{\tau_r})^2}\xrightarrow[r\to\infty]{\mathbb P}0.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-freezing-second}
\end{equation}
The convergence is uniform over the finitely many coordinates.
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
Fix \(t=\tau_r+s\). The first-moment difference consists of the missing negative-time tail and movement errors obtained by replacing \(W_{t-j}\) by \(W_{\tau_r}\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-package} bounds the normalized missing tail by \(C\beta_1^{t+1}\). For \(0\le j\le s\), Lemma~\ref{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-step-stability} and monotonicity of \(\eta_t\) give \(\|W_{t-j}-W_{\tau_r}\|_{\mathrm F}\le C_{\beta_1,\beta_2}m\eta_{\tau_r}\to0\). For \(j>s\), writing \(q=j-s\) gives \(\|W_{\tau_r-q}-W_{\tau_r}\|_{\mathrm F}\le C_{\beta_1,\beta_2}\sum_{u=\tau_r-q}^{\tau_r-1}\eta_u\). Therefore \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-stability} bounds the normalized past-lag contribution by
\[
C(1-\beta_1)\sum_{q=1}^{\tau_r}\beta_1^{q+s}\left(\exp\left(C\sum_{u=\tau_r-q}^{\tau_r-1}\eta_u\right)-1\right),
\]
which tends to zero by Assumption~\ref{ass:lr-momentum}. This proves \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-freezing-first}. The second-moment argument is identical using \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-square-stability} and \(\beta_2\), proving \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-freezing-second}.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-ratio-continuity}
There is a universal \(C_{\mathrm{rat}}<\infty\) such that, whenever \(\sigma>0\), \(|a_0|\le\sigma\), \(|a-a_0|\le\delta\sigma\), and \(|v-\sigma^2|\le\delta\sigma^2\) with \(0<\delta\le1/2\),
\begin{equation}
\left|\frac a{\sqrt v}-\frac{a_0}{\sigma}\right|\le C_{\mathrm{rat}}\delta.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-ratio-continuity}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
Since \(v\ge\sigma^2/2\),
\[
\left|\frac a{\sqrt v}-\frac{a_0}{\sigma}\right|\le\frac{|a-a_0|}{\sqrt v}+|a_0|\left|\frac1{\sqrt v}-\frac1\sigma\right|\le\sqrt2\,\delta+\left|(1+e)^{-1/2}-1\right|,
\]
where \(v=\sigma^2(1+e)\) and \(|e|\le\delta\). The map \(x\mapsto(1+x)^{-1/2}\) is Lipschitz on \([-1/2,1/2]\).
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- proof-57: body_md -->
Let \(f_{N,b}(W):=\mu_1(W)\oslash\mu_2(W)^{\odot1/2}=\Phi_{N,b}(W)\) by Lemma~\ref{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-batch-package}. Because the Adam update uses the gradient convention,
\begin{equation}
\frac{W_{\tau_r+m}-W_{\tau_r}}{\gamma_r}=-\sum_{s=0}^{m-1}\frac{\eta_{\tau_r+s}}{\gamma_r}U_{\tau_r+s},\qquad \sum_{s=0}^{m-1}\frac{\eta_{\tau_r+s}}{\gamma_r}=1.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-epoch-displacement}
\end{equation}
Fix \(0<\delta\le1/4\). Lemma~\ref{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-ema-concentration} gives, with probability at least \(1-\omega_\delta(\beta_1)-\omega_\delta(\beta_2)\), relative \(\delta\)-control of both frozen memories around \(\mu_1(W_{\tau_r})\) and \(\mu_2(W_{\tau_r})\), simultaneously over the epoch and all coordinates. Lemma~\ref{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-freezing} transfers these bounds to the actual memories with \(2\delta\) in place of \(\delta\), up to an event whose probability vanishes as \(r\to\infty\). Jensen's inequality gives \(|\mu_1(W)[\rho]|\le\sqrt{\mu_2(W)[\rho]}=\sigma_\rho(W)\), so Lemma~\ref{lem:app-rr-adamproxy-ratio-continuity} yields
\begin{equation}
\max_{0\le s<m}\|U_{\tau_r+s}-\Phi_{N,b}(W_{\tau_r})\|_{\max}\le C\delta
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-stepwise-proxy-bound}
\end{equation}
with the same asymptotic probability. Combining \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-epoch-displacement} and \eqref{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-stepwise-proxy-bound} gives
\begin{equation}
\left\|\frac{W_{\tau_r+m}-W_{\tau_r}}{\gamma_r}+\Phi_{N,b}(W_{\tau_r})\right\|_{\max}\le C\delta.
\label{eq:app-rr-adamproxy-epoch-proxy-bound}
\end{equation}
Given \(\varepsilon>0\), choose \(\delta\) so that \(C\delta<\varepsilon\). Taking \(r\to\infty\) first yields a limsup probability bounded by \(\omega_\delta(\beta_1)+\omega_\delta(\beta_2)\), and then taking \((\beta_1,\beta_2)\to(1,1)\) through \(0<\beta_1\le\beta_2<1\) proves \eqref{eq:rr-adamproxy-one-epoch-limit-clean}.
<!-- end proof-57 -->
<!-- proposition-25: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-adamproxy-coordinate-cap}
Let \(\kappa\ge0\), let \(W_0\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) be finite, and consider \(W_{t+1}=W_t+a_t\Psi_\kappa(W_t)\), where \(a_t>0\), \(a_t\to0\), and \(\sum_{t=0}^\infty a_t=\infty\).
Define
\[
T_t:=\sum_{s=0}^{t-1}a_s,\qquad K_\kappa(X):=2(1+\sqrt\kappa)R_1(X),\qquad \rho_\kappa(X):=\frac{\gamma_{\max}(X)^2}{K_\kappa(X)}>0.
\]
Then \(L(W_t)\to0\), \(\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)\to\infty\), and
\begin{align}
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{T_t}&\ge\rho_\kappa(X),
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-linear-margin-growth}\\
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}{\|W_t\|_{\max}}&\ge\rho_\kappa(X),
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-positive-normalized-margin}\\
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\left\|\frac{W_t}{\operatorname{mar}_X(W_t)}\right\|_{\max}&\le K_\kappa(X)r_{\max}^*(X)^2.
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-coordinate-cap}
\end{align}
The margin-normalized matrices in \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-coordinate-cap} are well defined and have minimum training margin one for all sufficiently large \(t\).
<!-- end proposition-25 -->
<!-- proof-58: body_md -->
For finite \(W\), define
\[
\mathcal G(W):=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N(1-p_{n,y_n}(W)),\qquad R(W):=\sum_{(n,c)\in\mathcal Q}p_{n,c}(W)=N\mathcal G(W)>0,
\]
and let \(\theta_{n,c}(W):=p_{n,c}(W)/R(W)\).
Then \(\theta(W)\) belongs to the probability simplex \(\Delta(\mathcal Q)\).
For any \(\theta\in\Delta(\mathcal Q)\), write
\begin{align*}
Z_n(\theta)&:=\sum_{c\ne y_n}\theta_{n,c}A_{n,c},\qquad \mathsf S(\theta):=\sum_{n=1}^NZ_n(\theta),\\
\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)&:=\left(\mathsf S(\theta)^{\odot2}+\kappa\sum_{n=1}^NZ_n(\theta)^{\odot2}\right)^{\odot1/2}.
\end{align*}
Since \(h_n(W)=R(W)Z_n(\theta(W))\), the common factor \(R(W)\) cancels in the proxy ratio, giving
\begin{equation}
\Psi_\kappa(W)=\mathsf S(\theta(W))\oslash\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta(W)),\qquad \|\Psi_\kappa(W)\|_{\max}\le1.
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-step-bound}
\end{equation}
The coordinate bound follows from \(\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]\ge|\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]|\), including zero denominators under the stated convention.
The entrywise inequalities \(|\mathsf S(\theta)|\le\sum_n|Z_n(\theta)|\) and \((\sum_nZ_n(\theta)^{\odot2})^{\odot1/2}\le\sum_n|Z_n(\theta)|\) imply
\begin{equation}
\|\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}\le(1+\sqrt\kappa)\sum_n\|Z_n(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}\le2(1+\sqrt\kappa)R_1(X)=K_\kappa(X).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-trajectory-metric-mass}
\end{equation}
Here the last inequality uses \(\|A_{n,c}\|_{\mathrm{sum}}=2\|x_n\|_1\) and \(\sum_{(n,c)\in\mathcal Q}\theta_{n,c}=1\).
Let \(V_*\) attain \(\gamma_{\max}(X)\) on the compact max-norm unit ball.
Max--sum duality and the margin constraints for \(V_*\) give
\[
\|\mathsf S(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}\ge\langle V_*,\mathsf S(\theta)\rangle=\sum_{(n,c)\in\mathcal Q}\theta_{n,c}\langle V_*,A_{n,c}\rangle\ge\gamma_{\max}(X).
\]
If \(\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]=0\), then \(\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]=0\).
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz on the remaining coordinates therefore yields
\begin{equation}
\mathcal J_\kappa(\theta):=\sum_{\rho:\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]>0}\frac{\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]^2}{\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)[\rho]}\ge\frac{\|\mathsf S(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}^2}{\|\mathsf D_\kappa(\theta)\|_{\mathrm{sum}}}\ge\rho_\kappa(X).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-uniform-dissipation}
\end{equation}
Since \(\nabla L(W)=-\mathcal G(W)\mathsf S(\theta(W))\), it follows that
\begin{equation}
-\langle\nabla L(W),\Psi_\kappa(W)\rangle=\mathcal G(W)\mathcal J_\kappa(\theta(W))\ge\rho_\kappa(X)\mathcal G(W).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-uniform-descent}
\end{equation}

To control the discrete-time remainder, fix \(\|\Delta\|_{\max}\le1\).
Then \(\|\Delta x_n\|_\infty\le R_1(X)\), and the softmax Hessian satisfies
\[
D^2\ell_n(V)[\Delta,\Delta]=\operatorname{Var}_{C\sim p_n(V)}\bigl((\Delta x_n)_C\bigr)\le4R_1(X)^2\bigl(1-p_{n,y_n}(V)\bigr).
\]
Indeed, the variance is at most the second moment about \((\Delta x_n)_{y_n}\), and every logit difference has magnitude at most \(2R_1(X)\).
The softmax formula also gives \(\mathcal G(W+sa\Delta)\le e^{2R_1(X)a}\mathcal G(W)\) for \(a\ge0\) and \(s\in[0,1]\).
