<!-- proposition-28: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-adamproxy-stationarity-margin}
For the limit in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-adamproxy-selected-limit}, there exists \(\alpha=\nu^{-1}>0\) such that
\begin{equation}
M_{N,b}(\theta^\star)\operatorname{vec}(\overline W)=\alpha\operatorname{vec}(\mathsf S(\theta^\star))=\alpha\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\theta_q^\star\operatorname{vec}(A_q).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-selected-stationarity}
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}:=\min_{q\in\mathcal Q}\langle\overline W,A_q\rangle>0,
\qquad
\operatorname{supp}(\theta^\star)\subseteq\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{q\in\mathcal Q}\langle\overline W,A_q\rangle.
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-positive-margin-support}
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-28 -->
<!-- proof-64: body_md -->
Let \(\mathsf S^\star:=\mathsf S(\theta^\star)\) and \(\mathsf D^\star:=\mathsf D_{N,b}(\theta^\star)\). If \(\mathsf D^\star[\rho]>0\), continuity and \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-selected-subsequence} give \(\mathsf S^\star[\rho]/\mathsf D^\star[\rho]=\nu\overline W[\rho]\). If \(\mathsf D^\star[\rho]=0\), then the inequality \(\mathsf D_{N,b}(\theta)[\rho]\ge|\mathsf S(\theta)[\rho]|\) proved above gives \(\mathsf S^\star[\rho]=0\). Hence \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-selected-stationarity} holds on every coordinate. It also gives
\begin{equation}
\langle\overline W,\mathsf S(\theta^\star)\rangle=\nu\sum_\rho\mathsf D^\star[\rho]\overline W[\rho]^2>0.
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-positive-average}
\end{equation}
To identify the support, write \(\overline m_{n,c}:=\langle\overline W,A_{n,c}\rangle\), \(\mu_n:=\min_{c\ne y_n}\overline m_{n,c}\), and \(h_{n,c}:=\overline m_{n,c}-\min\{0,\mu_n\}\). Since \(\|W_t\|_{\mathrm F}\to\infty\) and \(W_t/\|W_t\|_{\mathrm F}\to\overline W\), finite log-sum-exp asymptotics give
\[
-\frac1{\|W_t\|_{\mathrm F}}\log p_{n,c}(W_t)\longrightarrow h_{n,c}.
\]
Therefore every subsequential limit \(\theta^\star\) is supported on the atoms minimizing \(h_{n,c}\). If some \(\mu_n\le0\), then the minimum of \(h\) is zero and every minimizing atom has \(\overline m_{n,c}\le0\), contradicting \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-positive-average}. Thus every \(\mu_n>0\), so \(h_{n,c}=\overline m_{n,c}\), proving both claims in \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-positive-margin-support}.
<!-- end proof-64 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-adamproxy-psd-kkt}
Fix \(\theta\in\Delta(\mathcal Q)\). Suppose \(U\) is feasible for \eqref{eq:adamproxy-primal-clean} and \(\lambda\ge0\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
M_{N,b}(\theta)\operatorname{vec}(U)=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q}\lambda_q\operatorname{vec}(A_q),\qquad \lambda_q(\langle U,A_q\rangle-1)=0\quad(q\in\mathcal Q).
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-psd-kkt}
\end{equation}
Then \(U\in\mathcal P_{N,b}(\theta)\), and \(\lambda\) is a dual optimizer. No invertibility of \(M_{N,b}(\theta)\) is required.
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-65: body_md -->
Write \(u:=\operatorname{vec}(U)\), \(M:=M_{N,b}(\theta)\), and let \(V\) be any feasible matrix with \(v:=\operatorname{vec}(V)\). Since \(M\succeq0\),
\[
\frac12v^\top Mv-\frac12u^\top Mu=\frac12(v-u)^\top M(v-u)+\sum_q\lambda_q\langle V-U,A_q\rangle\ge0,
\]
where feasibility and complementarity are used in the last step. Thus \(U\) is primal optimal. Stationarity makes \(u\) a global minimizer of the Lagrangian for this \(\lambda\), and complementarity makes the dual value equal the primal value, so \(\lambda\) is dual optimal by weak duality.
<!-- end proof-65 -->
<!-- proof-66: body_md -->
Set \(p^\star:=\overline W/\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}\), where \(\overline W=-\overline\Phi\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}>0\) are given by Lemma~\ref{lem:app-adamproxy-selected-limit} and Proposition~\ref{prop:app-adamproxy-stationarity-margin}. Let \(\alpha\) be the scalar in \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-selected-stationarity} and define
\begin{equation}
\lambda_q^\star:=\frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}}\theta_q^\star.
\label{eq:app-adamproxy-dual-candidate}
\end{equation}
Then \(p^\star\) is feasible because \(\langle p^\star,A_q\rangle\ge1\), and dividing \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-selected-stationarity} by \(\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}\) gives the stationarity equation in Lemma~\ref{lem:app-adamproxy-psd-kkt}. If \(\lambda_q^\star>0\), then \(\theta_q^\star>0\), so \eqref{eq:app-adamproxy-positive-margin-support} gives \(\langle\overline W,A_q\rangle=\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}\) and hence complementarity. Lemma~\ref{lem:app-adamproxy-psd-kkt} therefore yields \(p^\star\in\mathcal P_{N,b}(\theta^\star)\) and dual optimality of \(\lambda^\star\). Finally,
\[
\|\lambda^\star\|_1=\frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}}\sum_q\theta_q^\star=\frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{\mathrm{AP}}}>0,
\]
so \(\theta^\star=\lambda^\star/\|\lambda^\star\|_1\). This proves the proposition.
<!-- end proof-66 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-aniso-error-comparison}
Let \(\mathcal R_d\) and \(\mathcal C_d\) be nonempty classifier families. Suppose every \(W\in\mathcal R_d\) satisfies \(Z_{i\to j}(W)\ge A_d>0\) for all \(i\ne j\), while every \(V\in\mathcal C_d\) has a directed pair \(i\ne j\) satisfying \(Z_{i\to j}(V)\le B_d\), where \(0\le B_d<A_d\). Then
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sup_{W\in\mathcal R_d}\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}(W)}{\inf_{V\in\mathcal C_d}\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}(V)}
\le
\frac{k-1}{\pi_{\min,d}}
\exp\!\left(-\frac{A_d^2-B_d^2}{2r_{\mathrm{te},0}^2}\right).
\label{eq:app-aniso-error-ratio}
\end{equation}
Consequently, if \(A_d^2\to\infty\), \(\limsup_d B_d^2/A_d^2<1\), and \(\log((k-1)/\pi_{\min,d})=o(A_d^2)\), then every classifier in \(\mathcal R_d\) has strictly larger population accuracy than every classifier in \(\mathcal C_d\) for all sufficiently large \(d\).
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-67: body_md -->
For a directed pair \(i\ne j\),
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(w_j^\top X^{\mathrm{te}}\ge w_i^\top X^{\mathrm{te}}\mid Y=i\right)
=
\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{Z_{i\to j}(W)}{r_{\mathrm{te}}}\right),
\]
where \(\overline\Phi(x)=\mathbb P(G\ge x)\) for \(G\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\). A union bound over the \(k-1\) competitors gives \(\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}(W)\le(k-1)\overline\Phi(A_d/r_{\mathrm{te}})\) for every \(W\in\mathcal R_d\). For \(V\in\mathcal C_d\), the directed pair supplied by the assumption is contained in the multiclass error event, so \(\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}(V)\ge\pi_{\min,d}\overline\Phi(B_d/r_{\mathrm{te}})\). Since \(\overline\Phi(x)/\overline\Phi(y)\le\exp(-(x^2-y^2)/2)\) for \(x\ge y\ge0\), \eqref{eq:app-aniso-error-ratio} follows. The final assertion is immediate.
<!-- end proof-67 -->
<!-- lemma-34: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-aniso-clean-optimizer-limits}
On the probability-one event on which the directional limits assumed in Theorem~\ref{thm:aniso-dd-ordering} exist, define
\[
U_{\mathrm{opt}}:=\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}}{\|W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\|_{\mathrm F}},\qquad \mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}}\cup\mathcal O_{\mathrm{comp}}.
\]
Every \(U_{\mathrm{opt}}\) is \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cl}}\)-measurable and hence independent of \(O_1,\ldots,O_k\). Moreover,
\[
U_{\mathrm{opt}}\in
\begin{cases}
\mathcal U_{\mathrm{row}}^X,&\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}},\\
\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X,&\mathrm{opt}\in\{\mathrm{SpecGD},\mathrm{Muon}\},\\
\mathcal U_{\max}^X,&\mathrm{opt}\in\{\mathrm{SignGD},\mathrm{Signum},\mathrm{Adam}\},
\end{cases}
\]
and
\begin{equation}
\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(U_{\mathrm{opt}}\right).
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-accuracy-limit}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-34 -->
<!-- proof-68: body_md -->
The empirical loss, every full-batch gradient, and every optimizer state are \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cl}}\)-measurable, so induction gives the same measurability for every iterate and hence for every normalized directional limit. The full-batch implicit-bias results used in Theorem~\ref{thm:det-optimizer-accuracy-order-clean}, together with Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-margin-direction-convergence}, place the three optimizer groups in the corresponding maximum-margin direction sets. Finally, population accuracy is invariant under positive rescaling, each margin direction has nonzero pairwise row differences, and the positive-definite Gaussian test laws assign zero probability to score-tie hyperplanes. Dominated convergence therefore gives \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-accuracy-limit}.
<!-- end proof-68 -->
<!-- lemma-35: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-aniso-clean-quantified-mean}
Fix \(0\le s_\mu<1\) and any finite collection of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cl}}\)-measurable Row, Spectral, and Max selectors. For every fixed \(0<\xi<1-s_\mu\), with probability at least \(1-e^{-d^\xi}\) for all sufficiently large \(d\), the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item Every selected Row direction satisfies
\begin{equation}
\min_{i\ne j}(u_{ij}^{U_{\mathrm{row}}})^\top\mu_i\ge\frac{1}{\sqrt2}-o(1).
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-row-signal}
\end{equation}
\item For every selected \(U_\psi\), \(\psi\in\{\mathrm{sp},\max\}\), and every fixed \(\varepsilon>0\), there exist unit vectors \(a_1^\psi,\ldots,a_k^\psi\), a directed edge set \(\mathcal G_d^\psi\) with \(|\mathcal G_d^\psi|\ge c_\varepsilon k(k-1)\), and
\[
p_{ij}^\psi:=\frac{a_i^\psi-a_j^\psi}{\|a_i^\psi-a_j^\psi\|_2}
\]
such that
\begin{align}
\max_{i\ne j}|(a_i^\psi)^\top a_j^\psi|&=o(1/\log d),\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-code-coherence}\\
\max_{(i,j)\in\mathcal G_d^\psi}\|u_{ij}^{U_\psi}-p_{ij}^\psi\|_2&\le\frac{1}{\log d},\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-code-transfer}\\
\max_{(i,j)\in\mathcal G_d^\psi}\bigl[(u_{ij}^{U_\psi})^\top\mu_i\bigr]_+^2&\le\frac{\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon}{2}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-code-signal}
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}
The event can be chosen simultaneously for the entire finite selector collection.
<!-- end lemma-35 -->
<!-- proof-69: body_md -->
Write \(L_d:=\log d\). Weighted Gaussian quadratic and bilinear concentration using \eqref{eq:app-aniso-mean-moments}, followed by a union bound over \(O(k^2)\) quantities, gives
\begin{equation}
\max_i\bigl|\|\mu_i\|_2^2-1\bigr|+\max_{i\ne j}|\mu_i^\top\mu_j|\le L_d^{-64}
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-shell}
\end{equation}
except with probability at most \(C\exp\{-cd^{1-s_\mu}/L_d^C\}\). This failure probability is at most \(e^{-d^\xi}\) for every fixed \(\xi<1-s_\mu\) and sufficiently large \(d\).

For Row, apply Proposition~\ref{prop:app-det-row-rigidity} to the clean samples with \(m_i=\mu_i\) and \(e_{i,s}={\mathbf 0}\). Equation~\eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-shell} gives \(\max_i\|w_i-\mu_i\|_2\le CL_d^{-16}\), uniformly over the exact Row face. Since \(\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2=\sqrt2+o(1)\) uniformly over pairs, normalization stability yields \(u_{ij}^W=(\mu_i-\mu_j)/\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2+O(L_d^{-16})\), and \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-row-signal} follows.

For Spectral, write the reduced singular value decomposition
\[
C^\mu=U\Lambda V^\top,\qquad Q:=UV^\top,\qquad r:=\min\{k-1,d\},
\]
and let \(q_i^\top\) denote the \(i\)-th row of \(Q\). After identifying \(\mathbf 1_k^\perp\) with \(\mathbb R^{k-1}\), the nonzero part of \(C^\mu\) has the same law as \(G\Gamma^{1/2}/\sqrt d\), where \(G\in\mathbb R^{(k-1)\times d}\) has i.i.d.\ standard Gaussian entries. Its left singular frame is therefore Haar in \(\mathbf 1_k^\perp\) and independent of the singular values. Haar projector concentration gives, on the same probability scale,
\begin{equation}
\max_i\left|\|q_i\|_2^2-\frac{r}{k}\right|+\max_{i\ne j}|q_i^\top q_j|\le L_d^{-16}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-polar-code}
\end{equation}
Moreover, since \(QC^{\mu\top}=U\Lambda U^\top\), conditional Haar concentration and the bound \(\|\bar\mu\|_2=o(1)\), where \(\bar\mu=k^{-1}\sum_i\mu_i\), give
\begin{equation}
\max_{i\ne j}\left|(q_i-q_j)^\top\mu_i-\frac{\|C^\mu\|_*}{k-1}\right|\le L_d^{-32}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-polar-flatness}
\end{equation}

The nuclear-to-Frobenius ratio satisfies
\begin{equation}
\frac{\|C^\mu\|_*}{\sqrt r\,\|C^\mu\|_{\mathrm F}}\le\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)+\eta
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-polar-ratio}
\end{equation}
for every fixed \(\eta>0\), with the same stretched-exponential confidence. Indeed, for fixed \(d\), the map
\[
A\mapsto\mathbb E_G\operatorname{tr}\!\left[\left(\frac{GAG^\top}{d}\right)^{1/2}\right]
\]
is concave and invariant under orthogonal conjugation, hence Schur-concave in the eigenvalues of \(A\). Among positive semidefinite \(A\) with \(\operatorname{tr}A=d\), it is maximized by \(I_d\). Gaussian concentration and the Marchenko--Pastur limit therefore bound the numerator by its isotropic limit, while \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-shell} gives \(\|C^\mu\|_{\mathrm F}/\sqrt k=1+o(1)\).

It remains to transfer the polar geometry to every exact Spectral margin direction. Since \(s_\mu<1\), \eqref{eq:app-aniso-power-sum-asymptotics} gives \(\Gamma\succeq c_{s_\mu}I_d\). Hence the positive singular values of \(C^\mu\) dominate \(\sqrt{c_{s_\mu}}\) times those of the corresponding standard Gaussian matrix. If \(\alpha\ne1\), the smallest positive singular value is therefore bounded below by a constant with probability \(1-e^{-cd}\). If \(\alpha=1\), the standard Gaussian hard-edge estimate and a dyadic union bound give
\begin{equation}
\frac1r\#\{\ell:\lambda_\ell(C^\mu)\le t\}\le Ct,\qquad L_d^{-8}\le t\le1.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-hard-edge}
\end{equation}
with probability at least \(1-Ce^{-cd/L_d^{16}}\).

Let \(W\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X\), put \(B:=PW/\|PW\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), and note that \(\|PW\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) because centering preserves all margins. The polar factor \(Q\) has clean margin \(\|C^\mu\|_*/(k-1)+O(L_d^{-32})\) by \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-polar-flatness}. Summing the normalized margin constraints for \(B\) therefore gives
\[
\langle B,C^\mu\rangle\ge\|C^\mu\|_*-kL_d^{-32}.
\]
Writing \(d_\ell:=1-u_\ell^\top Bv_\ell\in[0,2]\), where \(u_\ell,v_\ell\) are the singular vectors of \(C^\mu\), yields
\[
\frac1r\sum_{\ell=1}^r\lambda_\ell(C^\mu)d_\ell\le CL_d^{-32}.
\]
The positive spectral edge for \(\alpha\ne1\), and \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-hard-edge} with a split at \(t=L_d^{-8}\) for \(\alpha=1\), imply
\[
\frac1r\|B-Q\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le CL_d^{-8}.
\]
The centered pair identity then gives
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal U_{\mathrm{sp}}^X}\frac1{k(k-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\left\|u_{ij}^W-\frac{q_i-q_j}{\|q_i-q_j\|_2}\right\|_2^2\le CL_d^{-8}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-spectral-transfer}
\end{equation}

Define
\[
a_i^{\mathrm{sp}}:=\frac{q_i}{\|q_i\|_2},\qquad p_{ij}^{\mathrm{sp}}:=\frac{a_i^{\mathrm{sp}}-a_j^{\mathrm{sp}}}{\|a_i^{\mathrm{sp}}-a_j^{\mathrm{sp}}\|_2}.
\]
Equation~\eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-polar-code} gives \(\max_{i\ne j}|(a_i^{\mathrm{sp}})^\top a_j^{\mathrm{sp}}|\le CL_d^{-16}\) and shows that \(p_{ij}^{\mathrm{sp}}\) differs from \((q_i-q_j)/\|q_i-q_j\|_2\) by \(O(L_d^{-16})\). Combining \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-polar-flatness}, \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-polar-ratio}, and \(\|C^\mu\|_{\mathrm F}/\sqrt k=1+o(1)\) gives
\begin{equation}
\max_{i\ne j}\bigl[(p_{ij}^{\mathrm{sp}})^\top\mu_i\bigr]_+\le\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{sp}}(\alpha)+2\eta}{\sqrt2}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-spectral-canonical-signal}
\end{equation}
Markov's inequality applied to \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-spectral-transfer} shows that all but \(o(k^2)\) ordered pairs satisfy \(\|u_{ij}^{U_{\mathrm{sp}}}-p_{ij}^{\mathrm{sp}}\|_2\le L_d^{-1}\). Choosing \(\eta>0\) sufficiently small in terms of the prescribed \(\varepsilon\) proves part~(ii) for Spectral selectors.

For Max, use the common Haar eigenbasis of the mean covariance. Write
\[
\mu_i=U_\mu\widetilde\mu_i,\qquad \widetilde\mu_i:=\frac{D_{s_\mu}^{1/2}g_i}{\sqrt{T_{s_\mu,d}}},\qquad \widetilde c_i:=\widetilde\mu_i-\frac1k\sum_{\ell=1}^k\widetilde\mu_\ell.
\]
Then the \(i\)-th row of \(C^\mu\) is \((U_\mu\widetilde c_i)^\top\). Weighted Gaussian concentration gives
\begin{equation}
\max_i\bigl|\|\widetilde c_i\|_2^2-1\bigr|+\max_{i\ne j}|\widetilde c_i^\top\widetilde c_j|+\max_i\bigl|\widetilde c_i^\top\widetilde\mu_i-1\bigr|+\max_{i\ne j}|\widetilde c_j^\top\widetilde\mu_i|\le L_d^{-64}
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-prehaar-shell}
\end{equation}
outside an event of probability \(C\exp\{-cd^{1-s_\mu}/L_d^C\}\).

Put \(S^\mu:=\operatorname{sign}(C^\mu)\). Conditional on the vectors in \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-prehaar-shell}, standard smoothed-sign Haar concentration, using the identities
\[
\mathbb E[\operatorname{sign}(q^\top x)\operatorname{sign}(q^\top y)]=\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin\!\left(\frac{x^\top y}{\|x\|_2\|y\|_2}\right)
\]
and
\[
\sqrt d\,\mathbb E[\operatorname{sign}(q^\top x)\,q^\top v]=\sqrt d\,\mathbb E|q_1|\frac{x^\top v}{\|x\|_2}=\left(\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi}}+o(1)\right)\frac{x^\top v}{\|x\|_2},
\]
gives
\begin{align}
\left|\frac{\|C^\mu\|_{\mathrm{sum}}}{k\sqrt d}-\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\right|&\le CL_d^{-32},\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-l1}\\
\max_{i\ne j}\left|\frac{(S_i^\mu-S_j^\mu)^\top\mu_i}{\sqrt d}-\sqrt{\frac2\pi}\right|&\le CL_d^{-32},\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-signal}\\
\max_{i\ne j}\left|\frac{(S_i^\mu)^\top S_j^\mu}{d}\right|&\le CL_d^{-8},\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-coherence}\\
\frac1{kd}\#\{(i,a):\sqrt d\,|C^\mu[i,a]|\le L_d^{-16}\}&\le CL_d^{-16}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-small}
\end{align}
For example, these bounds follow by replacing the sign function by a piecewise-linear approximation at scale \(L_d^{-128}\), applying concentration on \(\mathsf O(d)\), and then controlling the smoothing error by the spherical small-ball probability. The resulting failure probability is \(C\exp\{-cd/L_d^C\}\).

Let \(W\in\mathcal U_{\max}^X\) and \(B:=W/\|W\|_{\max}\). The sign matrix is a feasible unit-Max direction with margin at least \((\sqrt{2/\pi}-CL_d^{-32})\sqrt d\), so \(\gamma_{\max}(X)\) is at least this value. Summing the normalized margin constraints for \(B\) and using \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-l1} gives
\[
\frac{\|C^\mu\|_{\mathrm{sum}}-\langle B,C^\mu\rangle}{k\sqrt d}\le CL_d^{-32}.
\]
Since \(|B[i,a]|\le1\), splitting the coordinates at \(\sqrt d\,|C^\mu[i,a]|=L_d^{-16}\) and using \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-small} yields
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal U_{\max}^X}\frac1{kd}\left\|\frac{W}{\|W\|_{\max}}-S^\mu\right\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le CL_d^{-16}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-max-transfer-matrix}
\end{equation}
Equation~\eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-coherence} implies \(\|S_i^\mu-S_j^\mu\|_2^2=2d(1+O(L_d^{-8}))\). The centered pair identity and \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-max-transfer-matrix} therefore give
\begin{equation}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal U_{\max}^X}\frac1{k(k-1)}\sum_{i\ne j}\left\|u_{ij}^W-\frac{S_i^\mu-S_j^\mu}{\|S_i^\mu-S_j^\mu\|_2}\right\|_2^2\le CL_d^{-16}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-max-transfer-pair}
\end{equation}

Define
\[
a_i^{\max}:=\frac{S_i^\mu}{\sqrt d},\qquad p_{ij}^{\max}:=\frac{S_i^\mu-S_j^\mu}{\|S_i^\mu-S_j^\mu\|_2}.
\]
Equations~\eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-signal}--\eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-sign-coherence} give
\[
\max_{i\ne j}|(a_i^{\max})^\top a_j^{\max}|\le CL_d^{-8},\qquad \max_{i\ne j}\left|\bigl[(p_{ij}^{\max})^\top\mu_i\bigr]^2-\frac1\pi\right|\le CL_d^{-8}.
\]
Markov's inequality applied to \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-max-transfer-pair} leaves all but \(o(k^2)\) pairs with direction error at most \(L_d^{-1}\). Since \(1/\pi=\vartheta_{\max}/2\), part~(ii) follows for Max selectors. The preceding bounds are uniform over the complete exact Spectral and Max faces, so the same event works for every member of the fixed finite selector collection.
<!-- end proof-69 -->
<!-- lemma-36: body_md -->
\label{lem:app-aniso-clean-sharp-common}
Condition on an event from Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-quantified-mean}, and consider the corresponding finite collection of selected Row, Spectral, and Max directions.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item If \(0\le s_\Sigma<1\), then for every fixed \(0<\chi<1-s_\Sigma\), with conditional probability at least \(1-e^{-d^\chi}\) for all sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{equation}
\max_{\mathrm{selected}\ U}\max_{i\ne j}\left|(u_{ij}^U)^\top\Sigma_i u_{ij}^U-1\right|=o(1).
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-low-residual-energy}
\end{equation}
\item Suppose \(s_\Sigma\ge1\) and put
\begin{equation}
c_d:=\frac{\log d}{T_{s_\Sigma,d}}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-cd}
\end{equation}
For every fixed \(b>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), all selected Row directions satisfy
\begin{equation}
\max_{i\ne j}(u_{ij}^{U_{\mathrm{row}}})^\top\Sigma_i u_{ij}^{U_{\mathrm{row}}}\le1+(4+2b+\varepsilon)c_d
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-row-sharp-energy}
\end{equation}
except with conditional probability at most \(C_{b,\varepsilon}d^{-b}\). For every fixed \(q\in(0,1)\), each selected competitor \(U_\psi\), \(\psi\in\{\mathrm{sp},\max\}\), has an edge \((i,j)\in\mathcal G_d^\psi\) such that
\begin{equation}
(u_{ij}^{U_\psi})^\top\Sigma_i u_{ij}^{U_\psi}\ge4qc_d+\mathbf 1_{\{s_\Sigma=1\}}(1-o(1))
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-competitor-extreme-energy}
\end{equation}
except with conditional probability at most \(C_{q,a}d^{-a}\) for every fixed \(0<a<1-q\).
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-36 -->
<!-- proof-70: body_md -->
For a unit vector \(u\) independent of \(O_i\), write \(O_i^\top u=g/\|g\|_2\). The quadratic form is
\[
u^\top\Sigma_i u=\frac{d}{\|g\|_2^2T_{s_\Sigma,d}}\sum_{r=1}^d r^{-s_\Sigma}g_r^2.
\]
When \(s_\Sigma<1\), weighted chi-square concentration gives deviations \(o(1)\) with failure at most \(e^{-d^\chi}\) for every \(\chi<1-s_\Sigma\). A union bound over the finite number of selectors and their \(O(k^2)=O(d^2)\) pair directions proves \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-low-residual-energy}.

Now suppose \(s_\Sigma\ge1\). Laurent--Massart's inequality gives, for every \(t>0\),
\[
\frac1{T_{s_\Sigma,d}}\sum_{r=1}^dr^{-s_\Sigma}g_r^2\le1+\frac{2\sqrt{T_{2s_\Sigma,d}t}+2t}{T_{s_\Sigma,d}}
\]
except with probability \(e^{-t}\), while \(\|g\|_2^2/d=1+o(1)\) exponentially fast. Taking \(t=(2+b)\log d\) and union-bounding over \(O(d^2)\) selected Row pair directions gives \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-row-sharp-energy}; the square-root term is \(o(c_d)\).


For the competitor lower bound, fix \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(0<a<1-q\), and choose \(q_+\in(q,1-a)\). Write \(L_d:=\log d\), let \(h_i:=O_ie_1\), and represent \(h_i=\xi_i/\|\xi_i\|_2\) using independent \(\xi_i\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d)\). Fix one selected competitor and its code \((a_i^\psi)\) and edge set \(\mathcal G_d^\psi\) from Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-quantified-mean}. Put \(t_d:=\sqrt{2q_+L_d}\) and define
\[
N_d:=\sum_{(i,j)\in\mathcal G_d^\psi}\mathbf 1\{\xi_i^\top a_i^\psi\ge t_d,\ \xi_i^\top a_j^\psi\le-t_d\}.
\]
The coherence bound \(\max_{i\ne j}|(a_i^\psi)^\top a_j^\psi|=o(1/L_d)\) implies, uniformly over the relevant distinct indices,
\[
\mathbb P(\xi_i^\top a_i^\psi\ge t_d,\xi_i^\top a_j^\psi\le-t_d)=d^{-2q_++o(1)},\qquad \mathbb P(\xi_i^\top a_i^\psi\ge t_d,\xi_i^\top a_j^\psi\le-t_d,\xi_i^\top a_\ell^\psi\le-t_d)=d^{-3q_++o(1)}.
\]
Indeed, the two- and three-dimensional covariance matrices differ from the identity by \(o(1/L_d)\), and Gaussian density comparison on the relevant orthants changes the logarithmic tail asymptotics by \(o(L_d)\). Edge indicators with different first indices are independent. Since \(|\mathcal G_d^\psi|=\Theta(d^2)\),
\[
\mathbb E N_d=d^{2-2q_++o(1)},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(N_d)\le\mathbb E N_d+d^{3-3q_++o(1)}.
\]
Chebyshev's inequality gives
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(N_d=0)\le d^{-(1-q_+)+o(1)}=o(d^{-a}).
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-extreme-failure}
\end{equation}
On \(\{N_d>0\}\), choose a counted edge using a fixed ordering of \(\mathcal G_d^\psi\). This choice depends only on the class-side information and \((\xi_i)_{i=1}^k\), not on the remaining residual eigenframes. Uniform Gaussian norm concentration and \(\|a_i^\psi-a_j^\psi\|_2=\sqrt2+o(1)\) give
\[
h_i^\top p_{ij}^\psi\ge\frac{2t_d}{(1+o(1))\sqrt{2d}}.
\]
For any fixed \(A>0\), spherical concentration and a union bound give, except with probability \(O(d^{-A})\),
\[
\max_{(i,j)\in\mathcal G_d^\psi}\sqrt d\,\left|h_i^\top(u_{ij}^{U_\psi}-p_{ij}^\psi)\right|\le C_A L_d^{-1/2},\qquad \max_{i\ne j}d\left|h_i^\top u_{ij}^{U_\psi}\right|^2\le C_A L_d.
\]
Here the first bound uses \(\|u_{ij}^{U_\psi}-p_{ij}^\psi\|_2\le L_d^{-1}\), and all directions in these bounds are fixed after conditioning on the class-side information. The selected edge therefore satisfies
\[
d\bigl(h_i^\top u_{ij}^{U_\psi}\bigr)^2\ge(4q_+-o(1))L_d\ge4qL_d
\]
for all sufficiently large \(d\). Since the top eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_i\) is \(d/T_{s_\Sigma,d}\), its contribution is at least \(4qc_d\).

Suppose \(s_\Sigma=1\). Conditional on all top eigenvectors, their auxiliary Gaussian radii, and the selected edge, the remaining eigenframe of \(O_i\) is Haar on \(h_i^\perp\). Write \(a_{ij}:=h_i^\top u_{ij}^{U_\psi}\). The remaining contribution has the conditional distribution
\[
\frac{d(1-a_{ij}^2)}{T_{1,d}}\frac{\sum_{r=2}^d r^{-1}g_r^2}{\sum_{r=2}^d g_r^2},\qquad g_2,\ldots,g_d\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N(0,1).
\]
The preceding upper bound gives \(a_{ij}^2=O(L_d/d)\). The weighted chi-square lower-tail inequality, with tail parameter \(L_d^{3/2}\), gives
\[
\sum_{r=2}^d r^{-1}g_r^2\ge T_{1,d}-1-O(L_d^{3/4})
\]
except with probability \(\exp(-L_d^{3/2})\), since \(\sum_{r=2}^d r^{-2}=O(1)\). Also, \(\sum_{r=2}^d g_r^2=(d-1)(1+O(L_d^{-2}))\) except with probability \(C\exp(-cd/L_d^4)\). Thus the remaining contribution is at least \(1-O(L_d^{-1/4})=1-o(1)\) with superpolynomial confidence. Choosing \(A>a\), integrating these conditional bounds, and using \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-extreme-failure} proves \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-competitor-extreme-energy} with failure at most \(C_{q,a}d^{-a}\). A finite union handles all selected competitors.
<!-- end proof-70 -->
<!-- proposition-29: body_md -->
\label{prop:app-aniso-clean-quantified}
Fix \(0\le s_\mu<1\), \(s_\Sigma\ge0\), and any finite collection of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cl}}\)-measurable Row, Spectral, and Max selectors. Assume
\[
\log\frac{k-1}{\pi_{\min,d}}=o(d/\log d).
\]
Then the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=2em]
\item If \(0\le s_\Sigma<1\), then for every fixed \(0<\chi<\min\{1-s_\mu,1-s_\Sigma\}\), every selected Row classifier has strictly larger population accuracy than every selected Spectral or Max classifier with probability at least \(1-e^{-d^\chi}\) for every sufficiently large \(d\).
\item If \(s_\Sigma\ge1\), then for every fixed
\begin{equation}
0<\zeta<\frac{2(1-\vartheta_\alpha)}{2+\vartheta_\alpha},
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-zeta-range}
\end{equation}
the same strict ordering holds with probability at least \(1-C_\zeta d^{-\zeta}\) for every sufficiently large \(d\).
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-29 -->
<!-- proof-71: body_md -->
Suppose first that \(s_\Sigma<1\). Fix \(0<\chi<\min\{1-s_\mu,1-s_\Sigma\}\), choose \(\chi_+\in(\chi,\min\{1-s_\mu,1-s_\Sigma\})\), and fix \(0<\varepsilon_0<1-\vartheta_\alpha\). Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-quantified-mean} and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-sharp-common}(i) with confidence exponent \(\chi_+\) implies that every selected Row direction has
\[
Z_{i\to j}(U_{\mathrm{row}})^2\ge(1/2-o(1))d
\]
uniformly over all directed pairs, whereas every selected competitor \(U_\psi\) has a directed pair with
\[
[Z_{i\to j}(U_\psi)]_+^2\le\frac{\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon_0}{2}\,d+o(d).
\]
Since \(\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon_0<1\), the competitor-to-Row squared-signal ratio has limsup strictly below one. The Row coefficient is of order \(d\), and \(\log((k-1)/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d/\log d)=o(d)\), so Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-error-comparison} gives the strict accuracy ordering. The two mean and residual events have joint failure at most \(e^{-d^\chi}\) after increasing the dimension threshold.




Now suppose \(s_\Sigma\ge1\). Fix \(\zeta\) satisfying \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-zeta-range}, choose \(b>\zeta\) sufficiently close to \(\zeta\), and then choose \(q\) so that
\begin{equation}
\vartheta_\alpha\left(1+\frac b2\right)<q<1-\zeta.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-bq-choice}
\end{equation}
Such a choice is possible because of \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-zeta-range}. Choose fixed \(\varepsilon_R,\varepsilon_M>0\) sufficiently small that
\[
(\vartheta_\alpha+\varepsilon_M)(4+2b+\varepsilon_R)<4q,\qquad (\vartheta_\alpha+\varepsilon_M)(5+2b+\varepsilon_R)<1+4q.
\]
The first inequality holds with zero slacks by \eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-bq-choice}; the second follows from the same condition and \(\vartheta_\alpha<1\). Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-quantified-mean} with signal slack \(\varepsilon_M\) and Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-sharp-common} with Row-energy slack \(\varepsilon_R\). They supply squared comparison amplitudes satisfying
\begin{align}
A_{R,d}^2&\ge\frac{(1/2-o(1))d}{1+(4+2b+\varepsilon_R)c_d},\nonumber\\
B_{\psi,d}^2&\le\frac{((\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon_M)/2)d}{4qc_d+\mathbf 1_{\{s_\Sigma=1\}}(1-o(1))}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-high-coefficients}
\end{align}
If \(s_\Sigma>1\), then \(c_d\to\infty\), and
\[
\limsup_d\frac{B_{\psi,d}^2}{A_{R,d}^2}\le\frac{(\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon_M)(4+2b+\varepsilon_R)}{4q}<1.
\]
If \(s_\Sigma=1\), then \(c_d\to1\), and
\[
\limsup_d\frac{B_{\psi,d}^2}{A_{R,d}^2}\le\frac{(\vartheta_\psi+\varepsilon_M)(5+2b+\varepsilon_R)}{1+4q}<1.
\]
Moreover, \(A_{R,d}^2\gtrsim d/\log d\), so the prior assumption is sufficient for Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-error-comparison}. The Row residual-energy failure is \(O(d^{-b})\), while the competitor-extreme failure is \(O(d^{-a})\) for every \(a<1-q\). Choose \(a\in(\zeta,1-q)\). The mean-geometry failure is stretched-exponential, so intersecting the finitely many selected-direction events gives total failure at most \(C_\zeta d^{-\zeta}\).
<!-- end proof-71 -->
<!-- proof-72: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-aniso-clean-optimizer-limits} turns the seven optimizer limits into a finite collection of \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cl}}\)-measurable Row, Spectral, and Max selectors and gives convergence of their population accuracies. Choose any fixed
\begin{equation}
0<c<\frac{2(1-\vartheta_\alpha)}{2+\vartheta_\alpha}.
\label{eq:app-aniso-clean-theorem-c}
\end{equation}
If \(0\le s_\Sigma<1\), choose any fixed \(0<\chi<\min\{1-s_\mu,1-s_\Sigma\}\). Proposition~\ref{prop:app-aniso-clean-quantified}(i) gives failure probability at most \(e^{-d^\chi}\), which is at most \(d^{-c}\) for every sufficiently large \(d\). If \(s_\Sigma\ge1\), Proposition~\ref{prop:app-aniso-clean-quantified}(ii), applied with \(\zeta=c\), gives failure probability at most \(C_cd^{-c}\). After enlarging a constant \(C\), both cases therefore hold with probability at least \(1-Cd^{-c}\). The exponent \(c\) and the constant \(C\) can be chosen independently of \(s_\mu\) and \(s_\Sigma\); only the sufficiently-large-\(d\) threshold depends on these exponents. On this event, every selected Row limit has strictly larger population accuracy than every selected Spectral or Max limit. Equation~\eqref{eq:app-aniso-clean-accuracy-limit} then gives
\[
\min_{\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{row}}}\liminf_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right)
>
\max_{\mathrm{opt}\in\mathcal O_{\mathrm{comp}}}\limsup_{t\to\infty}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\!\left(W_t^{\mathrm{opt}}\right),
\]
which is \eqref{eq:aniso-det-optimizer-ordering-clean-data}.
<!-- end proof-72 -->
<!-- head-5: body_md -->
We rescale all features by \(d^{-1/2}\), which preserves the maximum-margin direction sets and population accuracies by Lemma~\ref{lem:app-common-rescaling}.
Let \(k/d\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)\), and suppose
\begin{equation}
\Gamma_d=\operatorname{diag}(\gamma_{1,d},\ldots,\gamma_{d,d}),\qquad \frac1d\operatorname{tr}\Gamma_d=1,\qquad 0<c_\Gamma\le\gamma_{a,d}\le C_\Gamma<\infty.
\label{eq:when2-diet-profile}
\end{equation}
The independent class means and clean training set are
\begin{equation}
\mu_i=\frac1{\sqrt d}\Gamma_d^{1/2}g_i,\qquad g_i\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d),\qquad \mathcal X=\{(\mu_i,i):i\in[k]\}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-means}
\end{equation}
Write \(M\in\mathbb R^{k\times d}\) for the matrix with rows \(\mu_i^\top\), and define
\[
\mathcal F(M):=\{W:(w_i-w_j)^\top\mu_i\ge1\text{ for every }i\ne j\}.
\]
The two minimum-norm solution sets are
\begin{equation}
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}(M):=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{W\in\mathcal F(M)}\|W\|_{\mathrm{row}},\qquad \mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}(M):=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{W\in\mathcal F(M)}\|W\|_{\max}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-faces}
\end{equation}
For \(\Sigma\succ0\) and a classifier with positive directed mean margins, set
\begin{equation}
L_{i\to j}(W;\Sigma):=\frac{((w_i-w_j)^\top\mu_i)^2}{(w_i-w_j)^\top\Sigma(w_i-w_j)},\qquad E_d(W;\Sigma):=\min_{i\ne j}L_{i\to j}(W;\Sigma).
\label{eq:when2-diet-coefficient}
\end{equation}
The test distribution is
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(Y=i)=\pi_{i,d},\qquad X^{\mathrm{te}}\mid(Y=i)\sim\mathcal N\!\left(\mu_i,\frac{r_{\mathrm{te}}^2}{d}\Sigma\right),
\label{eq:when2-diet-test}
\end{equation}
where \(0<r_{\mathrm{te}}\le r_{\mathrm{te},0}<\infty\), \(\pi_{\min,d}:=\min_i\pi_{i,d}>0\), and
\begin{equation}
\log(1/\pi_{\min,d})=o(d).
\label{eq:when2-diet-prior}
\end{equation}
Write \(\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}=1-\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}\) and \(g_0:=\sqrt{2/\pi}\).
Constants denoted by \(c,C\) may change between displays; their permitted dependence is specified in each statement.
<!-- end head-5 -->
<!-- lemma-37: body_md -->
\label{lem:when2-diet-error-transfer}
Every classifier with positive directed mean margins satisfies
\begin{equation}
\pi_{\min,d}\,\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{dE_d(W;\Sigma)}}{r_{\mathrm{te}}}\right)\le\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}(W)\le(k-1)\,\overline\Phi\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{dE_d(W;\Sigma)}}{r_{\mathrm{te}}}\right),
\label{eq:when2-diet-tail}
\end{equation}
where \(\overline\Phi(x)=\mathbb P(Z\ge x)\) for \(Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1)\).
If nonempty classifier families \(\mathcal R,\mathcal C\) have positive directed mean margins and satisfy \(E_d(R;\Sigma)\ge A>B\ge E_d(V;\Sigma)>0\) for every \(R\in\mathcal R\) and \(V\in\mathcal C\), then
\begin{equation}
\frac{\sup_{R\in\mathcal R}\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}(R)}{\inf_{V\in\mathcal C}\operatorname{Err}_{\pi,d}(V)}\le\frac{k-1}{\pi_{\min,d}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{d(A-B)}{2r_{\mathrm{te},0}^2}\right).
\label{eq:when2-quant-error-ratio}
\end{equation}
In particular, a fixed positive coefficient gap gives strict uniform accuracy ordering for all sufficiently large \(d\), without any additional probabilistic loss.
<!-- end lemma-37 -->
<!-- proof-73: body_md -->
The directed pair error equals \(\overline\Phi(\sqrt{dL_{i\to j}(W;\Sigma)}/r_{\mathrm{te}})\).
A classwise union bound gives the upper bound in \eqref{eq:when2-diet-tail}, and a pair attaining \(E_d\) gives the lower bound.
For \(x\ge y\ge0\), changing variables in the Gaussian tail integral gives
\[
\overline\Phi(x)=\int_y^\infty\frac{e^{-(u+x-y)^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,du\le e^{-(x^2-y^2)/2}\overline\Phi(y).
\]
Applying this inequality with \(x=\sqrt{dA}/r_{\mathrm{te}}\) and \(y=\sqrt{dB}/r_{\mathrm{te}}\) proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-error-ratio}.
The final assertion follows from \(k=\Theta(d)\) and \eqref{eq:when2-diet-prior}.
<!-- end proof-73 -->
<!-- lemma-38: body_md -->
\label{lem:when2-quant-deterministic-rigidity}
Fix \(h_*>0\) and \(K<\infty\).
There exist \(\varepsilon_0,C>0\), depending only on \(h_*,K\), with the following property.
Let \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0\), \(k^{-1}\le\varepsilon\), and \(h\in[h_*,1]\).
Suppose deterministic means have no zero coordinates, and, with \(\bar\mu=k^{-1}\sum_i\mu_i\) and \(T_i=\operatorname{sign}(\mu_i)\), satisfy
\begin{align}
\max_i|\|\mu_i\|_2^2-1|&\le\varepsilon,& \max_{i\ne j}|\mu_i^\top\mu_j|&\le\varepsilon,& \|\bar\mu\|_2&\le\varepsilon,\nonumber\\
\max_i\left|\frac{\|\mu_i\|_1}{\sqrt d}-h\right|&\le\varepsilon,& \max_{i\ne j}\frac{|T_j^\top\mu_i|}{\sqrt d}&\le\varepsilon,& \max_{i\ne j}\frac{|T_i^\top T_j|}{d}&\le\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-quant-rigidity-input}
\end{align}
Assume also that, for \(s\in\{\varepsilon^{1/2},\varepsilon^{1/8}\}\),
\begin{equation}
\max_i\frac1d\#\{a:\sqrt d\,|\mu_i[a]|\le s\}\le Ks+\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-quant-small-ball-input}
\end{equation}
Then both solution sets are nonempty, and, writing \(t_{\max}:=\min_{W\in\mathcal F(M)}\|W\|_{\max}\),
\begin{align}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}(M)}\max_i\|w_i-\mu_i\|_2&\le C\varepsilon^{1/4},\label{eq:when2-quant-row-stability}\\
\left|\frac1{t_{\max}\sqrt d}-h\right|+\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}(M)}\max_i\frac{\|w_i/t_{\max}-T_i\|_2}{\sqrt d}&\le C\varepsilon^{1/16}.
\label{eq:when2-quant-max-stability}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-38 -->
<!-- proof-74: body_md -->
The matrix with rows \(\mu_i/(1-2\varepsilon)\) is feasible, so the optimal row radius \(R_*\) is at most \(\sqrt{1+\varepsilon}/(1-2\varepsilon)\le1+C\varepsilon\).
For any feasible \(W\), averaging the class-\(i\) constraints over competitors gives
\begin{equation}
(w_i-\bar w)^\top\mu_i\ge1-\frac1k,\qquad \bar w:=\frac1k\sum_iw_i.
\label{eq:when2-quant-averaged-constraint}
\end{equation}
For a Row minimizer, Cauchy--Schwarz and the row variance identity therefore imply
\[
\frac{(1-1/k)^2}{1+\varepsilon}\le\frac1k\sum_i\|w_i-\bar w\|_2^2\le R_*^2-\|\bar w\|_2^2.
\]
Thus \(\|\bar w\|_2\le C\varepsilon^{1/2}\), and \eqref{eq:when2-quant-averaged-constraint} gives \(w_i^\top\mu_i\ge1-C\varepsilon^{1/2}\) uniformly in \(i\).
Expanding \(\|w_i-\mu_i\|_2^2\) proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-row-stability}.

The sign matrix divided by \(\sqrt d(h-2\varepsilon)\) is feasible, so \(t_{\max}\le[\sqrt d(h-2\varepsilon)]^{-1}\).
Fix a Max minimizer and set \(H=W/t_{\max}\), \(\bar H=k^{-1}\sum_iH_i\), and
\[
D_i:=\frac{\|\mu_i\|_1-H_i^\top\mu_i}{\sqrt d}\ge0.
\]
Since \(\|H\|_{\max}=1\), averaging \eqref{eq:when2-quant-averaged-constraint} over \(i\) yields
\begin{align*}
\frac1k\sum_iD_i&\le h+\varepsilon-\frac{1-1/k}{t_{\max}\sqrt d}-\frac{\bar H^\top\bar\mu}{\sqrt d}\\
&\le h+\varepsilon-(1-1/k)(h-2\varepsilon)+\|\bar\mu\|_2\le C\varepsilon.
\end{align*}
For every \(s>0\), the coordinate bound on \(H\) gives
\begin{equation}
\frac{\|H_i-T_i\|_2^2}{d}\le\frac{2D_i}{s}+\frac4d\#\{a:\sqrt d\,|\mu_i[a]|\le s\}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-threshold-split}
\end{equation}
Indeed, outside the indicated small-coordinate set, use \((H_i[a]-T_i[a])^2\le2(1-H_i[a]T_i[a])\), and use the bound four on that set.
Taking \(s=\varepsilon^{1/2}\) and averaging gives \(\|H-T\|_{\mathrm F}^2/(kd)\le C\varepsilon^{1/2}\).
Moreover, \(\|k^{-1}\sum_iT_i\|_2^2/d\le k^{-1}+\varepsilon\le2\varepsilon\), so Jensen's inequality gives \(\|\bar H\|_2/\sqrt d\le C\varepsilon^{1/4}\).
Returning to the individual constraints now yields
\[
D_i\le h+\varepsilon-(1-1/k)(h-2\varepsilon)+\frac{\|\bar H\|_2\|\mu_i\|_2}{\sqrt d}\le C\varepsilon^{1/4}.
\]
Taking \(s=\varepsilon^{1/8}\) in \eqref{eq:when2-diet-threshold-split} proves the claimed uniform row error for \(H\).
Finally, averaging the constraints and using \(H_i^\top\mu_i\le\|\mu_i\|_1\) gives
\[
h-2\varepsilon\le\frac1{t_{\max}\sqrt d}\le\frac{h+2\varepsilon}{1-1/k}=h+O(\varepsilon).
\]
This proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-max-stability}.
The feasible witnesses and compact norm sublevel sets ensure existence of both minima.
<!-- end proof-74 -->
<!-- lemma-39: body_md -->
\label{lem:when2-diet-aligned-geometry}
Define
\begin{equation}
\bar\gamma_{1/2,d}:=\frac1d\sum_a\sqrt{\gamma_{a,d}},\qquad h_d:=g_0\bar\gamma_{1/2,d},\qquad \bar\gamma_{2,d}:=\frac1d\sum_a\gamma_{a,d}^2.
\label{eq:when2-diet-hd}
\end{equation}
There exist \(\varepsilon_0,c,C>0\), depending only on \(c_\Gamma,C_\Gamma\), such that, whenever \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0\) and \(k\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}\), an event \(\mathcal A_d(\varepsilon)\) satisfies
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P(\mathcal A_d(\varepsilon)^c)\le Ck^2e^{-cd\varepsilon^2}.
\label{eq:when2-quant-aligned-probability}
\end{equation}
On this event, both solution sets are nonempty and
\begin{align}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}(M)}\max_i\|w_i-\mu_i\|_2&\le C\varepsilon^{1/4},\label{eq:when2-diet-row-rigidity}\\
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}(M)}\max_i\frac{\|w_i/t_{\max}-T_i\|_2}{\sqrt d}&\le C\varepsilon^{1/16},\qquad T_i:=\operatorname{sign}(\mu_i).
\label{eq:when2-diet-max-rigidity}
\end{align}
Also, uniformly over \(i\ne j\),
\begin{align}
\bigl|\|\mu_i\|_2^2-1\bigr|+|\mu_i^\top\mu_j|&\le C\varepsilon,\nonumber\\
\left|\frac{(T_i-T_j)^\top\mu_i}{\sqrt d}-h_d\right|+\left|\frac{\|T_i-T_j\|_2^2}{2d}-1\right|&\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-diet-aligned-laws}
\end{align}
For \(\Sigma_\lambda:=(1-\lambda)I_d+\lambda\Gamma_d\) and \(A_d(\lambda):=1+\lambda(\bar\gamma_{2,d}-1)\), the same event satisfies
\begin{align}
\sup_{\lambda\in[0,1]}\max_{i\ne j}\left|(\mu_i-\mu_j)^\top\Sigma_\lambda(\mu_i-\mu_j)-2A_d(\lambda)\right|&\le C\varepsilon,\nonumber\\
\sup_{\lambda\in[0,1]}\max_{i\ne j}\left|\frac{(T_i-T_j)^\top\Sigma_\lambda(T_i-T_j)}{2d}-1\right|&\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-quant-aligned-energies}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-39 -->
<!-- proof-75: body_md -->
We verify the inputs of Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-quant-deterministic-rigidity} at precision \(\varepsilon\).
The independent-coordinate Gaussian quadratic-form and Bernstein bounds used below follow, for example, from the concentration tools in \citet{vershynin2012nonasymptotic}.
For the quadratic terms, the identity \(\mathbb E e^{u(Z^2-1)}=e^{-u}(1-2u)^{-1/2}\) for \(|u|<1/2\), together with the bounded spectral weights, gives deviation probability at most \(2e^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\) for each normalized quadratic form.
Polarization gives the corresponding bilinear bounds.
The variables \(\sqrt{\gamma_{a,d}}|g_i[a]|\) have uniformly bounded exponential moments, so Bernstein's inequality gives
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\left|\frac{\|\mu_i\|_1}{\sqrt d}-h_d\right|>\varepsilon\right)\le2e^{-cd\varepsilon^2}.
\]
For \(j\ne i\), conditioning on \(T_j\) gives \(T_j^\top\mu_i/\sqrt d\sim\mathcal N(0,1/d)\).
The products \(T_i[a]T_j[a]\) are independent Rademacher variables across \(a\), so their averages satisfy the same exponential bound.
For either prescribed threshold \(s\), Gaussian small-ball probabilities and Hoeffding's inequality give
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\frac1d\#\{a:\sqrt d\,|\mu_i[a]|\le s\}>Ks+\varepsilon\right)\le e^{-2d\varepsilon^2},
\]
where \(K\) depends only on \(c_\Gamma\).
Also, \(\bar\mu\) has covariance \(\Gamma_d/(kd)\); when \(k\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}\), the event \(\|\bar\mu\|_2>\varepsilon\) has probability at most \(Ce^{-cd}\).
All coordinates are nonzero almost surely, and \(g_0\sqrt{c_\Gamma}\le h_d\le g_0<1\).
A union bound over these \(O(k^2)\) events verifies the deterministic lemma's hypotheses and proves \eqref{eq:when2-diet-row-rigidity}--\eqref{eq:when2-diet-aligned-laws}.

For \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-energies}, it suffices to treat \(\lambda=0,1\), since the quadratic forms and their asserted centers are affine in \(\lambda\).
The Gaussian difference \(\mu_i-\mu_j\) has covariance \(2\Gamma_d/d\), giving mean quadratic form \(2d^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_d\Sigma_\lambda)=2A_d(\lambda)\).
The same quadratic-form bound applies at both endpoints.
For the sign contrasts, \((T_i[a]-T_j[a])^2\) are independent across coordinates, lie in \(\{0,4\}\), and have mean two.
Their bounded weighted sums therefore concentrate about \(2\operatorname{tr}\Sigma_\lambda=2d\) with failure at most \(2e^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\) at each endpoint.
Adding these events proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-probability} and \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-energies}.
<!-- end proof-75 -->
<!-- proposition-30: body_md -->
\label{prop:when2-transition}
Suppose
\begin{equation}
\bar\gamma_{1/2,d}\to\bar\gamma_{1/2},\qquad \bar\gamma_{2,d}\to\bar\gamma_2,
\label{eq:when2-diet-profile-limits}
\end{equation}
and set
\begin{equation}
h:=g_0\bar\gamma_{1/2},\qquad h^2\bar\gamma_2>1.
\label{eq:when2-diet-h}
\end{equation}
For
\begin{equation}
\Sigma_\lambda:=(1-\lambda)I_d+\lambda\Gamma_d,\qquad \lambda\in[0,1],
\label{eq:when2-diet-sigma-t}
\end{equation}
there are constants \(\varepsilon_0,C>0\), depending only on the spectral bounds, such that, whenever \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0\) and \(k\ge C\varepsilon^{-2}\), the event \(\mathcal A_d(\varepsilon)\) in Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-diet-aligned-geometry} satisfies
\begin{align}
\sup_{\lambda\in[0,1]}\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}(M)}\left|E_d(W;\Sigma_\lambda)-\frac1{2A_d(\lambda)}\right|&\le C\varepsilon^{1/4},\nonumber\\
\sup_{\lambda\in[0,1]}\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}(M)}\left|E_d(W;\Sigma_\lambda)-\frac{h_d^2}{2}\right|&\le C\varepsilon^{1/16}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-transition-coefficients}
\end{align}
The limiting coefficients cross uniquely at
\begin{equation}
\lambda_c:=\frac{h^{-2}-1}{\bar\gamma_2-1}\in(0,1).
\label{eq:when2-diet-tc}
\end{equation}
For every fixed \(\lambda\ne\lambda_c\), there exist \(c_\lambda,C_\lambda>0\), independent of \(d\), such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{align}
\lambda<\lambda_c\quad&\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbb P\!\left\{\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W)>\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W)\right\}\ge1-C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda d},\label{eq:when2-diet-row-win}\\
\lambda>\lambda_c\quad&\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbb P\!\left\{\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W)>\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W)\right\}\ge1-C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda d}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-max-win}
\end{align}
At \(\lambda=\lambda_c\), only equality of the limiting coefficients is asserted.
<!-- end proposition-30 -->
<!-- proof-76: body_md -->
The spectral bounds give \(c_\Gamma I_d\preceq\Sigma_\lambda\preceq C_\Gamma I_d\) for every \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), since trace normalization implies \(c_\Gamma\le1\le C_\Gamma\).
For Row, \eqref{eq:when2-diet-row-rigidity} allows us to replace \(w_i-w_j\) by \(\mu_i-\mu_j\) with Euclidean error \(C\varepsilon^{1/4}\).
The latter vector has directed signal \(1+O(\varepsilon)\) and test-noise quadratic form \(2A_d(\lambda)+O(\varepsilon)\), uniformly over pairs and \(\lambda\).
The denominators are bounded away from zero, proving the first estimate in \eqref{eq:when2-diet-transition-coefficients}.
For Max, scale invariance allows us to use the contrast \((H_i-H_j)/\sqrt d\), where \(H=W/t_{\max}\).
By \eqref{eq:when2-diet-max-rigidity}, this contrast differs from \((T_i-T_j)/\sqrt d\) by at most \(C\varepsilon^{1/16}\).
The canonical sign contrast has directed signal \(h_d+O(\varepsilon)\) and test-noise quadratic form \(2+O(\varepsilon)\), proving the second estimate.
These arguments also prove the same estimates for every individual \(L_{i\to j}\).

Since \(\bar\gamma_{1/2}\le1\), we have \(0<h<1\); the condition \(h^2\bar\gamma_2>1\) implies \(\bar\gamma_2>1\) and \(0<\lambda_c<1\).
Fix \(\lambda\ne\lambda_c\), and let
\[
\Delta_\lambda:=\left|\frac1{2[1+\lambda(\bar\gamma_2-1)]}-\frac{h^2}{2}\right|>0.
\]
Choose a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) small enough that the sum of the two errors in \eqref{eq:when2-diet-transition-coefficients} is at most \(\Delta_\lambda/4\).
By \eqref{eq:when2-diet-profile-limits}, the finite-dimensional coefficient gap has the asserted sign and magnitude at least \(3\Delta_\lambda/4\) for all sufficiently large \(d\).
Thus the complete-face gap is at least \(\Delta_\lambda/2\) on \(\mathcal A_d(\varepsilon)\).
Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-diet-error-transfer} proves the corresponding strict accuracy ordering.
Finally, \(k=\Theta(d)\) allows the factor \(k^2\) in \eqref{eq:when2-quant-aligned-probability} to be absorbed into \(C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda d}\).
No convergence rate for either spectral summary is required; their convergence affects only the sufficiently-large-d threshold.
<!-- end proof-76 -->
<!-- lemma-40: body_md -->
\label{lem:when2-quant-haar-sign}
Let deterministic vectors \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfy \(1/2\le\|x_i\|_2\le2\), let \(R\) be Haar on \(O(d)\) or \(\mathrm{SO}(d)\), and put \(T_i=\operatorname{sign}(Rx_i)\).
There are universal \(\varepsilon_0,c,C>0\) such that, for \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0\) and any two prescribed thresholds \(s_1,s_2\in(0,1]\), an event of probability at least \(1-Ck^2e^{-cd\varepsilon^6}\) satisfies
\begin{align}
\max_{i,j}\left|\frac{T_i^\top Rx_j}{\sqrt d}-g_0\frac{x_i^\top x_j}{\|x_i\|_2}\right|&\le C\varepsilon,\nonumber\\
\max_{i,j}\left|\frac{T_i^\top T_j}{d}-\frac2\pi\arcsin\!\left(\frac{x_i^\top x_j}{\|x_i\|_2\|x_j\|_2}\right)\right|&\le C\varepsilon,\nonumber\\
\max_i\frac1d\#\{a:\sqrt d\,|(Rx_i)[a]|\le s_\ell\}&\le Cs_\ell+C\varepsilon^2,\qquad \ell=1,2.
\label{eq:when2-quant-haar-statistics}
\end{align}
<!-- end lemma-40 -->
<!-- proof-77: body_md -->
Fix a pair and choose an orthonormal basis \(F\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) of its span, where \(m\le2\).
Write \(x_i=Fu_i\), \(x_j=Fu_j\), and let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d\times m}\) have independent standard Gaussian entries.
Then
\[
\sqrt d\,RF\ \overset{\mathrm d}=\ Y:=ZB,\qquad B:=(Z^\top Z/d)^{-1/2}.
\]
Indeed, \(Y/\sqrt d\) has orthonormal columns and its distribution is invariant under every left orthogonal transformation.
The Gaussian quadratic-form bound gives
\[
\mathbb P\!\left(\|Z^\top Z/d-I_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon^3\right)\le Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^6}.
\]
On the complementary event, \(\|B-I_m\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C\varepsilon^3\), and hence
\[
\frac1d\|(Y-Z)u\|_2^2\le C\varepsilon^6
\]
for either coefficient vector \(u\).
Set \(X=Zu\), \(\widetilde X=Yu\), and \(b=\varepsilon^2\).
Gaussian small-ball probabilities and Hoeffding's inequality imply \(d^{-1}\#\{a:|X_a|\le b\}\le C\varepsilon^2\), except with probability \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^4}\).
Consequently,
\[
\frac1d\#\{a:\operatorname{sign}(\widetilde X_a)\ne\operatorname{sign}(X_a)\}\le\frac1d\#\{a:|X_a|\le b\}+\frac{\|\widetilde X-X\|_2^2}{db^2}\le C\varepsilon^2.
\]
Thus the normalized Euclidean distance between the corresponding sign vectors is at most \(C\varepsilon\).
By Cauchy--Schwarz, replacing \(Y\) by \(Z\) changes the empirical averages involving one sign factor and one linear factor by at most \(C\varepsilon\), while the empirical correlations between the corresponding sign vectors change by at most \(C\varepsilon^2\).
For a standard Gaussian row \(z^\top\) of \(Z\), the corresponding expectations are
\[
\mathbb E[\operatorname{sign}(z^\top u)z^\top v]=g_0\frac{u^\top v}{\|u\|_2},\qquad \mathbb E[\operatorname{sign}(z^\top u)\operatorname{sign}(z^\top v)]=\frac2\pi\arcsin\!\left(\frac{u^\top v}{\|u\|_2\|v\|_2}\right).
\]
The first identity follows by conditioning \(z^\top v\) on \(z^\top u\), and the second is the standard arcsine formula for the signs of two jointly Gaussian variables.
Bernstein's and Hoeffding's inequalities concentrate the corresponding empirical averages within \(\varepsilon\) with failure at most \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\).
Finally, for either prescribed \(s\),
\[
\frac1d\#\{a:|\widetilde X_a|\le s\}\le\frac1d\#\{a:|X_a|\le s+b\}+\frac{\|\widetilde X-X\|_2^2}{db^2}\le Cs+C\varepsilon^2
\]
except with probability \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^4}\).
A union bound over the pairs and the two thresholds proves \eqref{eq:when2-quant-haar-statistics}; independence between different pairs is not needed.
<!-- end proof-77 -->
<!-- lemma-41: body_md -->
\label{lem:when2-diet-haar-recovery}
For deterministic means, define
\begin{equation}
\delta_d:=\max_i|\|\mu_i\|_2^2-1|+\max_{i\ne j}|\mu_i^\top\mu_j|.
\label{eq:when2-diet-regular}
\end{equation}
Let \(\Sigma\succ0\) satisfy \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma=d\) and \(c_\Sigma I_d\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_d\), and set
\[
\mu_i^\circ=R\mu_i,\qquad \Sigma^\circ=R\Sigma R^\top,\qquad v_{ij}:=\frac{\mu_i-\mu_j}{\|\mu_i-\mu_j\|_2},\qquad a_{ij}:=v_{ij}^\top\Sigma v_{ij},
\]
where \(R\) is an independent Haar matrix.
There are \(\varepsilon_0,c,C>0\), depending only on \(c_\Sigma,C_\Sigma\), such that, whenever
\[
0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0,\qquad \delta_d+d^{-1}+k^{-1}\le\varepsilon^2,
\]
an event of probability at least \(1-Ck^2e^{-cd\varepsilon^6}\), over \(R\) alone, satisfies
\begin{align}
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^\circ}\max_{i\ne j}\left|L_{i\to j}(W;\Sigma^\circ)-\frac1{2a_{ij}}\right|&\le C\varepsilon^{1/4},\nonumber\\
\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}^\circ}\max_{i\ne j}\left|L_{i\to j}(W;\Sigma^\circ)-\frac1{2a_{ij}+\pi-2}\right|&\le C\varepsilon^{1/16}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-coefficients}
\end{align}
Here the superscript \(\circ\) denotes solution sets and accuracies for the rotated problem.
Consequently, if \(\delta_d\to0\), \(k/d\to\alpha\in(0,\infty)\), and \eqref{eq:when2-diet-prior} holds, there exist \(c_*,C_*>0\), independent of \(d\), such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb P_R\!\left\{\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^\circ}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}^\circ(W)>\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}^\circ}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}^\circ(W)\right\}\ge1-C_*e^{-c_*d}.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-row-win}
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-41 -->
<!-- proof-78: body_md -->
The hypotheses imply \(\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\le(1+\delta_d)/k+\delta_d\le C\varepsilon^2\).
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-quant-haar-sign} to the means.
The norm and coherence assumptions, together with \eqref{eq:when2-quant-haar-statistics}, give, for \(T_i=\operatorname{sign}(R\mu_i)\),
\begin{equation}
\max_i\left|\frac{\|R\mu_i\|_1}{\sqrt d}-g_0\right|+\max_{i\ne j}\frac{|T_j^\top R\mu_i|}{\sqrt d}+\max_{i\ne j}\frac{|T_i^\top T_j|}{d}\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-sign-laws}
\end{equation}
Choose a fixed sufficiently large constant \(C_0\) and apply that lemma with thresholds \((C_0\varepsilon)^{1/2}\) and \((C_0\varepsilon)^{1/8}\).
After decreasing \(\varepsilon_0\), Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-quant-deterministic-rigidity} applies at precision \(C_0\varepsilon\), with \(h=g_0\).
It follows that every Row minimizer is within \(C\varepsilon^{1/4}\) per row of the rotated means, while every rescaled Max minimizer is within \(C\varepsilon^{1/16}\sqrt d\) per row of \(T_i\).

It remains to calculate the test-noise energy of the canonical sign contrast
\[
b_{ij}:=\frac{T_i-T_j}{\|T_i-T_j\|_2}.
\]
Fix a pair, let \(S=\operatorname{span}\{\mu_i,\mu_j\}\), and choose an orthonormal basis \(F\in\mathbb R^{d\times2}\) of \(S\).
The Gram matrix of the pair is uniformly well-conditioned under the assumed bound on \(\delta_d\).
Conditioning only on \(RF\), the vector \(b_{ij}\) is fixed whenever it is defined.
Set \(p=(RF)^\top b_{ij}\), \(q=Fp\), and \(r^2=1-\|p\|_2^2\).
The unexposed action of \(R\) on the orthogonal complement is Haar, so conditionally
\begin{equation}
R^\top b_{ij}=q+r\zeta,
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-decomposition}
\end{equation}
where \(\zeta\) is uniform on the unit sphere of \(S^\perp\).
On the sign-statistics event, \eqref{eq:when2-quant-haar-statistics} gives
\[
b_{ij}^\top R\mu_i=\frac{g_0}{\sqrt2}+O(\varepsilon),\qquad b_{ij}^\top R\mu_j=-\frac{g_0}{\sqrt2}+O(\varepsilon).
\]
The same two inner products for \(g_0v_{ij}\) are \(g_0/\sqrt2+O(\delta_d)\) and \(-g_0/\sqrt2+O(\delta_d)\).
Inverting the well-conditioned two-by-two Gram matrix therefore yields
\begin{equation}
\|q-g_0v_{ij}\|_2\le C\varepsilon,\qquad |r^2-(1-g_0^2)|\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-projection}
\end{equation}
For the conditional complement calculation, let \(P_S\) denote the orthogonal projector onto \(S\).
Representing \(\zeta\) by a normalized standard Gaussian in \(S^\perp\) and applying the bounded-weight quadratic-form and Gaussian linear-form bounds gives
\[
\left|\zeta^\top\Sigma\zeta-\frac{\operatorname{tr}((I_d-P_S)\Sigma)}{d-2}\right|+|q^\top\Sigma\zeta|\le C\varepsilon
\]
with conditional failure at most \(Ce^{-cd\varepsilon^2}\), uniformly in the exposed frame.
The trace ratio is \(1+O(d^{-1})\), since \(\operatorname{tr}\Sigma=d\) and \(\operatorname{rank}P_S=2\).
The conditional failure bound can be integrated and then union-bounded over pairs; we do not condition on the sign vectors of the other classes.
Combining this bound with \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-decomposition} and \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-projection} gives
\begin{equation}
\max_{i\ne j}\left|b_{ij}^\top\Sigma^\circ b_{ij}-(g_0^2a_{ij}+1-g_0^2)\right|\le C\varepsilon.
\label{eq:when2-diet-haar-energy}
\end{equation}
The canonical Row direction \(Rv_{ij}\) has directed signal \(1/\sqrt2+O(\delta_d)\) and test-noise energy exactly \(a_{ij}\).
The canonical Max direction has directed signal \(g_0/\sqrt2+O(\varepsilon)\), and
\[
\frac{g_0^2/2}{g_0^2a_{ij}+1-g_0^2}=\frac1{2a_{ij}+\pi-2}.
\]
Both canonical contrast norms are bounded away from zero after the Max contrasts are divided by \(\sqrt d\).
Normalization stability, the whole-face bounds already proved, and \(\Sigma^\circ\succeq c_\Sigma I_d\) therefore transfer these coefficients uniformly to the complete solution sets, proving \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-coefficients}.
The combined failure is at most \(Ck^2e^{-cd\varepsilon^6}\).

To pass to the minimum directed coefficient, put \(a_*:=\max_{i\ne j}a_{ij}\).
Then \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-coefficients} implies
\[
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^\circ}E_d(W;\Sigma^\circ)-\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}^\circ}E_d(W;\Sigma^\circ)\ge\frac1{2a_*}-\frac1{2a_*+\pi-2}-C\varepsilon^{1/16}.
\]
Since \(a_*\le C_\Sigma\), the difference of the two displayed fractions is at least
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\mathrm{rot}}:=\frac{\pi-2}{2C_\Sigma(2C_\Sigma+\pi-2)}>0.
\label{eq:when2-quant-rotation-gap}
\end{equation}
Choose a fixed \(\varepsilon>0\) so that \(C\varepsilon^{1/16}\le\Delta_{\mathrm{rot}}/2\).
The regularity assumptions eventually ensure \(\delta_d+d^{-1}+k^{-1}\le\varepsilon^2\).
Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-diet-error-transfer} gives the strict accuracy ordering, and absorbing \(k^2\) into the exponential proves \eqref{eq:when2-diet-haar-row-win}.
<!-- end proof-78 -->
<!-- proposition-31: body_md -->
\label{prop:when2-rotation-flip}
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:when2-transition}, fix \(\lambda\in(\lambda_c,1]\).
Compare the original problem with means \(\mu_i\) and covariance \(\Sigma_\lambda\) to the problem obtained by the independent common rotation \(\mu_i\mapsto R\mu_i\), \(\Sigma_\lambda\mapsto R\Sigma_\lambda R^\top\).
There exist \(c,C>0\), independent of \(d\), such that, for every sufficiently large \(d\), with joint probability at least \(1-Ce^{-cd}\),
\begin{align}
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W)&>\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}(W),\nonumber\\
\inf_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{row}}^\circ}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}^\circ(W)&>\sup_{W\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{max}}^\circ}\operatorname{Acc}_{\pi,d}^\circ(W).
\label{eq:when2-diet-rotation-flip}
\end{align}
The two problems have identical class Gram matrices, class-mean norms and pair distances, mean singular values, test-noise eigenvalues, and mean-contrast test-noise variances.
<!-- end proposition-31 -->
<!-- proof-79: body_md -->
Proposition~\ref{prop:when2-transition} gives the first ordering with exponentially small failure.
For the second ordering, choose the fixed precision \(\varepsilon\) in the last paragraph of Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-diet-haar-recovery}.
Gaussian quadratic and bilinear concentration gives
\[
\mathbb P\{\delta_d>\varepsilon^2/2\}\le Ck^2e^{-cd\varepsilon^4}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(d\), we also have \(d^{-1}+k^{-1}\le\varepsilon^2/2\).
Conditional on any means in this event, Lemma~\ref{lem:when2-diet-haar-recovery} applies with the same constants, since \(c_\Gamma I_d\preceq\Sigma_\lambda\preceq C_\Gamma I_d\).
Its conditional failure is at most \(Ck^2e^{-cd\varepsilon^6}\).
Integrating this uniform conditional bound and intersecting with the first ordering proves \eqref{eq:when2-diet-rotation-flip}.
The invariances follow directly from orthogonality; in particular,
\[
(Rv_{ij})^\top(R\Sigma_\lambda R^\top)(Rv_{ij})=v_{ij}^\top\Sigma_\lambda v_{ij}.
\]
<!-- end proof-79 -->
<!-- proof-80: body_md -->
Lemma~\ref{lem:app-common-rescaling} identifies the direction sets and accuracies in the main-text normalization with those analyzed here.
Since \(h=g_0\bar\gamma_{1/2}\), the transition point in Proposition~\ref{prop:when2-transition} is
\[
\frac{h^{-2}-1}{\bar\gamma_2-1}=\frac{\pi/(2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2)-1}{\bar\gamma_2-1}=\lambda_c.
\]
That proposition therefore gives the diagonal complete-face ordering with probability at least \(1-C_\lambda e^{-c_\lambda d}\) for every fixed \(\lambda\ne\lambda_c\) and sufficiently large \(d\).

For every fixed \(\lambda\in[0,1]\), the conditional argument in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:when2-rotation-flip} gives the rotated Row-over-Max ordering with probability at least \(1-C_{\mathrm{rot}}e^{-c_{\mathrm{rot}}d}\).
This argument does not require \(\lambda>\lambda_c\).
Its spectral bounds and the positive gap in \eqref{eq:when2-quant-rotation-gap} are uniform in \(\lambda\), so \(c_{\mathrm{rot}},C_{\mathrm{rot}}\) can be chosen independently of \(\lambda\).

At each fixed dimension on these events, Proposition~\ref{cor:app-row-full-batch} and Theorem~\ref{thm:app-ms-full-batch-adam}, together with Lemma~\ref{lem:exact-margin-direction-convergence}, place the normalized RowGDM and Adam trajectories asymptotically in their respective Row and Max maximum-margin direction sets.
Every classifier in these direction sets has nonzero pairwise row differences.
The compactness and continuity argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:app-acc-trajectory-continuity} applies to the present positive-definite Gaussian test covariances as well, since all score-tie hyperplanes have probability zero.
It transfers each uniform complete-face ordering to the stated strict comparison between the trajectory liminf and limsup accuracies, without an additional exceptional event or a directional-convergence assumption.
The same argument applies to RowGD.
<!-- end proof-80 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:app-coordinate-dispersed-profiles}
Suppose the assumptions of Proposition~\ref{prop:main-coordinate-reversal} concerning the existence of the limiting spectral summaries hold.
Assume additionally that, for some fixed \(0<\underline\gamma<1<\overline\gamma<\infty\),
\[
\underline\gamma\le\gamma_{a,d}\le\overline\gamma\qquad\text{for all }a,d,
\]
and that
\[
v_\Gamma:=\lim_{d\to\infty}\frac1d\sum_{a=1}^d(\gamma_{a,d}-1)^2>\frac{\pi}{2q_*^2}-1,\qquad q_*:=\frac{(\overline\gamma-1)\sqrt{\underline\gamma}+(1-\underline\gamma)\sqrt{\overline\gamma}}{\overline\gamma-\underline\gamma}.
\]
Then \(2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2\bar\gamma_2/\pi>1\), and hence the transition point in Proposition~\ref{prop:main-coordinate-reversal} lies in \((0,1)\).
In particular, the transition condition does not require a special spectral shape: within a fixed bounded spectral range, the displayed lower bound on the limiting spectral variance is sufficient.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-81: body_md -->
Concavity of \(x\mapsto\sqrt{x}\) places its graph above the chord joining \((\underline\gamma,\sqrt{\underline\gamma})\) and \((\overline\gamma,\sqrt{\overline\gamma})\).
Averaging this chord inequality and using \(d^{-1}\sum_a\gamma_{a,d}=1\) gives \(\bar\gamma_{1/2}\ge q_*\).
Trace normalization also gives \(\bar\gamma_2=1+v_\Gamma\), and therefore
\[
\frac{2\bar\gamma_{1/2}^2\bar\gamma_2}{\pi}\ge\frac{2q_*^2(1+v_\Gamma)}{\pi}>1.
\]
<!-- end proof-81 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:app-coordinate-dispersion-nonvacuous}
Write \(l:=\underline\gamma\) and \(u:=\overline\gamma\).
The variance permitted by the spectral range is itself bounded.
Indeed, since \(l\le\gamma_{a,d}\le u\), we have \((\gamma_{a,d}-l)(u-\gamma_{a,d})\ge0\), or equivalently \(\gamma_{a,d}^2\le(l+u)\gamma_{a,d}-lu\).
Averaging and using the trace normalization \(d^{-1}\sum_a\gamma_{a,d}=1\) gives \(\bar\gamma_2\le l+u-lu\), and hence \(v_\Gamma=\bar\gamma_2-1\le(1-l)(u-1)\).
This bound is sharp: it is attained asymptotically by a two-point spectral profile supported on \(l\) and \(u\) with respective masses \((u-1)/(u-l)\) and \((1-l)/(u-l)\).

Consequently, the dispersion condition in Corollary~\ref{cor:app-coordinate-dispersed-profiles} is non-vacuous if and only if \((1-l)(u-1)>\pi/(2q_*^2)-1\).
Using \(q_*=(1+\sqrt{lu})/(\sqrt l+\sqrt u)\), this is equivalently
\[
\frac{2(1+\sqrt{lu})^2(l+u-lu)}{\pi(\sqrt l+\sqrt u)^2}>1.
\]
For each fixed \(l\in(0,1)\), the left-hand side is strictly increasing in \(u>1\), so there is a unique critical value \(u_c(l)>1\) above which the sufficient dispersion condition can be satisfied.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- head-6: body_md -->
The main-text experiment in Figure~\ref{fig:experiments} (left) uses \(k=60\) classes and dimension \(d=20\). For each class \(i\), we draw \(\mu_i\sim\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d/d)\), draw the number of training examples independently and uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,5\}\), and generate \(x_{i,r}^{\mathrm{tr}}=\mu_i+0.2236\,\varepsilon_{i,r}^{\mathrm{tr}}\) and \(x_{i,r}^{\mathrm{te}}=\mu_i+2.2361\,\varepsilon_{i,r}^{\mathrm{te}}\), where all residual vectors are independent \(\mathcal N({\mathbf 0},I_d/d)\). Test-class proportions are drawn independently from \(\operatorname{Dirichlet}(\mathbf 1_k)\), and each of the 30 paired seeds uses \(120{,}000\) evaluation examples. All methods within a seed use the same training and evaluation data.
<!-- end head-6 -->
<!-- head-7: body_md -->
Consistent with the final validation-perplexity ordering in Figure~\ref{fig:experiments} (right), RowSGDM achieves lower held-out NLL and perplexity than both Muon and Adam on each of the five paired seeds. RowSGDM also has the smallest boundary discrepancy and the largest boundary cosine on every seed, so its performance advantage is accompanied by closer alignment between learned classifier boundaries and empirical class-mean differences. Table~\ref{tab:language-model-last-layer-results} summarizes the five-seed held-out results.
<!-- end head-7 -->
<!-- head-8: body_md -->
For the three final checkpoints examined here, the primary class-mean point estimates in Table~\ref{tab:app-lm-spectral-exponents} all satisfy \(\widehat{s}_\mu<1\): \(0.957735\) for OLMoE, \(0.932780\) for Qwen3, and \(0.985366\) for AMUSE. The within-class covariance exponents are more heterogeneous and can exceed one, as reflected by the maxima in the table.
<!-- end head-8 -->
